9 october 2026. this archive read the pater column of thirty-six frames of the gračišće baptism register, found no defranceschi, and published that the family was «not established at gračišće in the eighteenth century». the patrini column of the same frames holds about twenty of them. correction published. ⚠ the worst part is that the archive had already written the warning down. its own search record says: «the father column was read … a defranceschi could stand as a mother's maiden name or a godparent … «none seen in twelve frames» is the claim; «none exists» is not». a correctly stated limit is not a closed gap. it sat for two days while the conclusion built on it spread into four files and an errand. so two rules, and the second is the one that was missing. 1. a ruled register is a set of columns, and a question phrased «was he living here?» names only one of them. the surname can be in pater, mater (as olim/nata), patrini, conditio — and in this book it was in the one nobody asked about. sweep the whole row. 2. ⭐ when a limit is written into the log, raise it as a row in the same breath. a «⚠ limits:» paragraph is a note to a reader who may never come; a worklist row is a note to somebody who will. this archive's log is full of honestly stated limits, and that honesty is worth nothing until each one becomes a task. ⭐ and the payoff for closing it was not a tidier nil — it was a better fact. the father-column nil still stands. set beside the godparent column it now says something far stranger: the defranceschi were at gračišće as cives from 1791 to 1808 and had not one child baptised there in eighteen years. present, wanted at the font, not breeding in the parish. an absence became a household.
never write a /who/ slug from a name — link /person//, which always exists

9 october 2026. the gate failed with «no such page» for /who/anna-de-franceschi-nobilis-pisinensis/ and /who/vincenca-defranceschi/ — two slugs composed out of the people's names while writing the prose around them. this is now the fifth slug invented and caught by the gate in one session; the others were /library/, /registers/, /sovereignty/ and /gazetteer/, whose real names are /the-library/, /parish-books/, /timeline/ and /places/. the rule, because the failure is always the same shape: a url is a fact about the site, not a guess from a name. for a person, there is one form that cannot be wrong: /person//. it is generated for every row in the roster, by pid, so the moment a person exists the page exists. /who// is a different thing — a name index that gathers everyone sharing a name, built from each row's own who field, which a new row does not have unless it is given one. writing a /who/ slug for a brand-new person asks for a page nothing has built. so: link /person// for an individual; link /who// only by copying a who value that is already in the roster; and for any other page, check the file list rather than reasoning from the page's title. ⚠ the same failure also tripped the kit check in the same run, which validates links too — so one invented slug reports as two red lines and looks like two problems.
a correction is a claim. verify it as hard as the thing it corrects — harder, because it feels careful

9 october 2026. this archive published a correction today, and the correction was wrong. a fast pass re-read a godmother as «catharina defranceschi» where the first pass had «theresia», announced the fix, and built a finding on top of it — a second woman of the name crossing between two parishes. re-cropped at twenty times with the mother's cell alongside for alignment, the word is «theresia». the original reading was right all along. in the same pass four entries were re-dated to the wrong year, and an apparent «disorder» in the register was announced that turned out to be a misread page header. ⚠ every evidence rule in this archive was written for first readings. a hand is only legible against itself. never read rank off an abbreviation without a second construction. crop past the cell, not to it. assert the new text is present after writing. none of them says anything about the second reading, and the second reading is where this archive has now been wrong twice in one day. the rule, and the reason it is not obvious: > a correction is a claim like any other. it needs the same crop, the same magnification, the same second construction, the same doc. it needs them more, because a correction arrives already wearing the clothes of care — it is the act of a session that is paying attention, and that feeling substitutes for the work. in practice, before publishing any correction of a reading: 1. crop the disputed word again, at the magnification the original reading did not have, with an adjacent cell in frame for alignment. 2. say which reading the evidence supports and what would change your mind. «the word is x» is weaker than «the word is x, because the ascender at position 4 is crossed, and y has no letter there». 3. if the correction creates a new person, a new place or a new link — stop and verify once more. a correction that generates a finding is the most dangerous kind, because the finding makes it attractive. 4. prefer «this reading is not settled» to a confident swap. a negative or an open question costs the archive nothing; a confident wrong correction costs it a published claim, the claim built on it, and the correction of the correction.
check the closing sentence against the search log — it is the least careful line and the most quotable

9 october 2026. three published errors in one day, and all three were the same shape. 1. a correction that was itself a misreading — «catharina» for «theresia», made at speed because correcting feels like the careful act. 2. confirmation rolls announced as something «nobody had counted» that this archive had catalogued from the film's own title card nine days earlier. 3. «baptising their children somewhere else, and the somewhere else is gologorica» — asserted about a book whose search row, four files away, says «no defranceschi baptism between 1799 and 1806». ⚠ none of them was in the evidence. every one was in the sentence that ties the finding off. the body of a finding gets the crops, the magnification, the second construction, the doc tag. then comes the closing line — the one that says what it all means, the one a reader will quote — and it is written from momentum, out of what the archive «obviously» holds, at the end of an hour's work when the hard part feels done. > it is also the only line most readers will carry away. so, before publishing any finding, take its last sentence on its own and ask of it the three questions the body already answered: 1. which file and row says this? not «the archive holds» — which search key, which frame? 2. is it doc, inf or memory? if it names another source as agreeing, open that source. 3. would it survive if the reader checked only this sentence? a finding is told when a reader reads it — and the closing line is what they read. ⚠ the pattern is not carelessness about evidence. it is carefulness that stops one sentence early, and it will recur unless the last line is treated as a claim rather than a summary.
a told finding is not a drawn conclusion — re-read your own pages when a new question arrives

9 october 2026. this archive spent a day establishing that the defranceschi baptised no children anywhere for twelve years, listed three possible reasons, and then found the answer sitting on its own page, published five days earlier. «house 36, in eighteen months» was written on 6 october. it has the baby dead at six months in july 1791, the unmarried aunt dead of «febris putrida» in april 1792, the twenty-six-year-old wife dead of apoplexy four weeks after her — and the sentence «he did not remarry. he died a widower twenty-one years later.» everything needed to answer a question nobody had yet asked. ⚠ this is not the archive's usual failure and it should not be filed as one. the standing rule is that a finding is done when it is told, not when it is logged — and this finding was told, in full, on the right page, with its plate and its sources. what was not done was to draw its consequence when a new question made one available. > a told finding is inert until somebody asks it a question it can answer. so the rule has a second half: 1. when a new question is framed — «where were the children?», «when did they arrive?» — grep the archive's own story pages for the years involved, not only its search log and its roster. the search log records what was looked for; the story pages record what was found, and a thing found for one reason answers another. 2. ⭐ search by date range, not by subject. the house-36 block never mentions childbearing, fertility or a gap. it would not have matched any search for the question it answers. it matches 1791–1792, and the question was about 1791–1803. 3. when the answer does turn up this way, say that it was already there. the temptation is to present a connection as a discovery, and the difference is the whole of this archive's credibility.

none of this is a complaint about the sources. familysearch's films are the reason any of this was possible at all, and the volunteers who indexed the baptisms saved months. the point is narrower: these tools answer the question you actually asked, which is often not the question you meant — and the only defence is to open the image.

/sources/.title: Sources — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: everything this archive is built on, what each one actually gave, and where each one is weak. every page carries a block linking back to the entries here that it rests on.

an archive that will not say where it got something is a rumour with a stylesheet. this page is the answer to “how do you know that?”, and it is meant to be usable: where a source can be written to, its address is here; where it can be searched, the link is live; where it is wrong or thin, that is said in the entry rather than buried.

three of these sources conflict with others on points of fact. in every case this archive prefers the contemporaneous register over the later family memory, says so on the page where the conflict appears, and leaves the question open rather than quietly picking a winner.

141 of the 159 link to the thing itself, 8 are paper this family holds and say where, and 10 carry neither — scholarly books and articles where choosing the right edition is research and a wrong link is worse than none.

32 kinds, and 10 of them were the vocabulary. 22 have been typed straight into a row and have no definition on this page: secondary, popular, printed, 1845, printed, 1926 — held, digital repository, archive, trieste, newspaper, chapter, article, archive, book, heritage register, test, register film, dataset, online source, bibliography, newspapers, encyclopedia, commercial, parish register (microfilm), printed regesti of state papers, doctoral thesis. two differ only in case — archive and archive — which no reader can tell apart and no filter can join. they are counted here rather than quietly merged, because folding them is a decision about what each source is.

a paid british index, and after the austrian catalogue the most productive single source this archive has used. it holds the american half of the family in documents — the 1930 census with three of the eleven in one brooklyn flat, joseph's certificate of arrival (martha washington, out of trieste, 11 october 1910, aged eighteen), albina's 1928 petition in her own words («i emigrated from genoa … on the vessel conte rosso»), and frank schinkopan's 1920 declaration giving his birth at pisino. its british newspapers hold a whole chapter nobody knew was there: between 1865 and 1878 a master of this name commands austrian ships in the black sea grain and bristol channel coal trades — the natalia, the rachel, the peppina luigia, the aquilone.

in «etos i etnos zavičaja», čakavski sabor, pula – rijeka 1985, pp. 177–253

seventy-six pages on the de franceschi of gologorica by one of croatia's leading historians of istria — «between ethos and ethnos», on a family that was friulian-carnian in origin and italian-national in politics, in a village that was croatian in speech. it is the standing scholarly account of the household this archive's gologorica registers reconstruct, and it is the source trogrlić leans on for the statement that the family settled there in the seventeenth century.

every report the bishops of pićan (pedena) sent to rome between 1589 and 1780, summarised from the vatican archive. pedena was the diocese of gallignana and gologorica, and the bishop was the temporal lord of gologorica from about 1600. the reports give the lordship, the colonus tenants and what was done to them, the diocese's revenue, the names and ages of the clergy, and the replacement of the glagolitic liturgy with latin.

(the likeliest cause is that the galeb run did not include the -ski spelling, which is the only one that hits — but the note said «every spelling», and it should not have.) free, and it has to be driven like a person — an asp.net search that will not answer a plain command-line request. it carries the two bakar newspapers, which is the sharpest reason to work it, and both are empty: «galeb» and «kvarner» return zero in every spelling across two complete runs, with the controls passing (107 for «bakar» in galeb, 102 for «narod» in kvarner). a genuine absence, not a scanning failure.

free, and it must be worked by spelling and by zone. the first pass ran newspapers only and only the fused spellings, reporting «defranceski» 2 and «defranceschi» 13; this archive's own rule — that each spelling returns a different, non-overlapping set — had not been applied to it. a trove nil is usually weak: newspaper digitisation mostly stops in 1954, and whether the «wimmera mail-times» is digitised for 1949–54 has never been established — so the horsham silence of the 1940s and 1950s proves much less than it appears to. an api key was issued to david on 27 september 2026, valid to december 2026, and it changes what this source is. the key is held at private/trove.env, which is gitignored — this repository is published, so a key committed here is a key published. ⚠ the finding that matters more than the key: trove does not fold the space. familysearch returns the same 8,235 records for «defranceschi» and «de franceschi»; findmypast folds it too. trove does not. a quoted search for «defranceschi» returns 13 newspaper articles and «de franceschi» returns 128, and they overlap by three. this archive's earlier trove passes ran the fused spellings and reported 13, and were treating the source as swept. counted by the api across nine categories: defranceschi 73 · de franceschi 393 · defranceski 3 · de franceski 6 · franceski 34 — and the non-newspaper categories had never been searched at all: 176 books and 26 music entries sit under «de franceschi» alone. all 170 distinct newspaper and gazette articles are now harvested to data/harvest/trove-newspapers.json. one limit, stated so it is not rediscovered: the api returns metadata but no ocr text for gazettes — wordcount is given and articletext comes back empty at every reclevel. the text is on the public article page at https://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id>, which answers a plain request and is where the naturalisation names were read. ⚠ the key came with an undertaking, and this archive breached it before reading it. the letter to trove support of 20 september 2026 (rsref189042, in the d'arcy archive) says the request is metadata only — titles, place coverage and date ranges — and that the archive would cite trove for «a title and a date range and nothing more». article search is outside that, and 53 article snippets were published to a public remote before anyone here had seen the letter. the snippets are withdrawn; what remains in the harvest is citation-level — spelling, date, paper, heading, page, url. the wider question is on the work list and is david's, and no further article search or article-text fetching happens here until he answers it. the sanctioned use, and how to do it — from the d'arcy session, 27 september, recorded here so it is not relearned. two endpoints, both get, both taking x-api-key as a header and never a query parameter, so the key cannot be logged by a proxy or left in a shell history: /v3/newspaper/titles and /v3/gazette/titles. per-title holdings — still inside the undertaking, because an issue count per year is a date range — come from /v3/newspaper/title/{id}?include=years. five traps, every one of which returns a confident zero rather than an error: · the gazette endpoint returns its list under the key newspaper, not gazette. asking for gazette gives an empty list and no error; d'arcy was one commit from publishing «australia has no gazettes». compare the response's own total against what you parsed and refuse if they differ. (2,014 newspapers, 38 gazettes.) · startdate/enddate flatten a broken run. «clarion (brisbane, qld. : 1940 – 1943; 1945 – 1956)» reads as covering 1944. 90 of 2,052 titles have such a gap, and a false «a paper covered that year» is the worst answer a coverage table can give. · the bracket may be «brisbane, qld.», bare «qld.», or have no colon at all — «(1933 – 1982)» — which puts a date range in the place field and invents towns called 1933. · state is «queensland», not «qld». · json has no integer keys. issue counts stored under int years come back as strings and every lookup misses — d'arcy read brisbane 1902 as 0 issues across 37 papers, and caught it only because that number could not honestly be zero. their file also keeps yearsknown: false for a failed request, which is a different fact from holding nothing — the same separation this archive makes for an unreadable file.

the venetian senate's deliberations on istria for 1670–1676, in regest form — registers 46 to 50. this is the volume that documents the cretan refugee settlement at parenzo decree by decree: the sixty families and the first list; nineteen of the twenty-three who embarked at zante; the request for land to build their own church; the houses still empty in 1673 and let out for repair money; twenty-five families counted in 1674; four declared forfeit for leaving; six holding 145 campi in 1675. it also carries the 26 october 1673 decree on the cretans' admission to the council of parenzo, and the 1 december 1674 freeze on that council's attempt to expel members — which is the subject of camillo de franceschi's 1952 paper. and the 27 june 1671 decree settling the caiducci of risano in forty-one houses at pola and in repaired casali at medulin, on the public land «rimasti dopo le concessioni fatte ai cretensi».

lia de luca, «venezia e le immigrazioni in istria nel cinque e seicento»
università ca' foscari venezia, scuola di dottorato in storia sociale europea, ciclo 24 (a.a. 2008/09–2010/11), discussed 2012, 256 pp. iris.unive.it

the modern study of exactly this question — who venice moved into istria, and how — written out of the senate's own filze at the archivio di stato di venezia. chapter 5.6, «gli ultimi tentativi di ripopolamento organizzato», is the cretan settlement of parenzo and the hajduk settlement of the pola district as one operation. it supplies what the printed regesti leave out: that the whole cretan community sheltering at zante was to be moved to parenzo with 2,000 ducats and building materials for sixty families; that in july 1673 a survey of usurped land in the parenzo territory was opened to free ground for them, and «alcune famiglie immigrate ottennero di essere ammesse nel consiglio di parenzo»; and that in september 1671 pola, sissan, lisignan, castel di mormaran, pomer and medolin petitioned against the hajduks together.

⚠ the repository copy at iris.unive.it is behind a cloudflare bot check, which this archive does not work around. david signed in and supplied the pdf on 12 october 2026 — the standing division of labour. its bibliography cites camillo's 1952 paper three times and pins it at pp. 57–115, which until now this archive had from joksimović alone.

what was deliberately not done

the antenati search at the italian state archives sits behind a bot check, and it was not bypassed. familysearch's images were not bulk-downloaded: their terms do not permit it, and seventeenth- to nineteenth-century secretary hand defeats optical character recognition anyway. commercial heraldry sites were read for leads and their pictures were not reproduced. no image of a living person appears anywhere on this site.
if you want to check something

start with the page it appears on — each carries its own source block — then come here for the address. the two archives most worth writing to are pazin, which answered this family twice in 2021 for about a hundred kuna a time, and arolsen, which is free.

12 oct 2026 three more on the candia war — two useful for context, one about the besiegers and not this family yielded whether the war literature touches this family or its route pérez negrete (in the morosini quatercentenary volume, poligrafico e zecca dello stato 2019): the war's shape — ottoman landing 24 june 1645, canea lost 1645, rethymno 3 november 1646, candia besieged 22 years in two phases (1648–49, 1667–69); köprülü came with nearly 70,000 men; france and malta gave the island up in august 1669; morosini surrendered on 6 september without the senate's authorisation. ⭐ the ca' foscari thesis gives the road: «da venezia le navi… procedevano lungo la costa dalmata fino ad arrivare a corfù, quindi verso zante…» — zante and corfu were the two staging ports on the venice–candia route, and the dalmatian coast was its first leg. this family's candia → zante → šibenik is not a wandering; it is the supply road walked backwards. it also records the psara storm of 17–18 march 1648 — 17 galleys lost, grimani drowned — which is the only fleet wrecked in a storm in this war, and it is twenty-one years too early to be ours. and it notes venetian families buying their way into the senate to fund the war, which is the world a refugee family entering a noble council belongs to. ⚠ kolovos, «a town for the besiegers» is about the ottoman siege-town outside candia, 1650–69 — the other side of the wall. no refugees, no evacuation, no franceschi. a fine paper and nothing for this archive.what it produced on this siteseget, and crete · pérez negrete in «francesco morosini 1619–1694» (2019) · «l'esercito veneziano e la difesa di candia» (ca' foscari ma) · kolovos in «the eastern mediterranean under ottoman rule: crete 1645–1840» (2008)

12 oct 2026 pomara, diasporas 43 (2025) — how venice actually planted refugees in istria, with the numbers yielded the mechanism behind the seget land grant of 1604 and the post-1669 settlements new to this archive — published 11 june 2025. ⚠ it is about albanians, not cretans, and is used only for the machinery. istria's population: ~60,000 (1610) → 36,000 (1625) → 30,000 (1630s) — a province losing half its people in a generation. refugees were colonists on terms: a loan of 500 ducats for tools and animals, repayable without interest from the third year; cash advances per household head; and land. one group of eight families received 700 plots near umag, described as «uncultivated, thorny and stony», with the obligation to make them «a perfect crop». friction with the existing population is documented, and prejudice in the poreč area is traced from the late 17th century. that is the frame the seget grant of 1604 and the poreč sixty of 1669 both sit in.what it produced on this siteseget, and crete · bruno pomara, «an attempted albanian settlement in istria… (1610–1612)», diasporas 43 (2025), 95–127

21 sept 2026 the svetvincenat baptism volume 1764-1791 read to its last leaf -- and what a complete volume is worth yielded svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885 — frames 113–131, completing the volume every opening of this volume has now been read — frames 5 to 131, the whole of 1764 to 1791. the register closes on 28 may 1791 with the archpriest's own tally; frames 132–134 are the microfilm's target boards, not pages. the completeness is the finding. a negative from a volume read frame by frame is evidence. a negative from a volume searched by index is nothing at all. ### what the name does in this book it stands at other people's fonts, constantly, and it almost never appears as a parent. in twenty-seven years there are six baptisms of the surname — franca (1769), pasqua vittoria (1773), domenica (1776), domenico (1777), giovanni (1778) and maria matthia (1784) — and well over sixty appearances as godparent. that shape is what a settled, respectable, and small family looks like in a parish register. ### the people this volume establishes - antonio, the bell-ringer, dnus, alive from before 1769 to 12 october 1788 (magnified) — about fifty-eight at the last sighting. - mattea, his wife, 1 may 1780 to 18 august 1782 (magnified). - vittorio, his son, called «filius antonii» in 1773, 1782 and 1787 — three independent entries, plus the 1812 burial's kin: antonio. the most-named man of the surname in the book. - euphemia, vittorio's wife, named in full — «uxor victorii de franceschi» — on 22 august 1785, four times in six weeks in early 1787, and last on 15 january 1791. - maria, antonio's daughter, 18 january 1786 and 30 september 1787, the second adding «ex hac parochia». - domenico, dnus, and his wife fosca — she is the parish's standing godmother, in eight-plus entries across 1780–1789. ### the act this sweep missed, and how it was recovered reading all 127 openings, i did not see the one baptism that mattered most — and the index did. the familysearch index entry for maria matthia de franceschi carries the image ark 3:1:3qs7-l99x-k3fv, which is frame 106 — a frame this sweep had already read and passed over. going back to it with a narrow crop: > «anno dni 1784 die 4 septembris. maria matthia filia legitima, ac naturalis victorii, et euphemiæ jugalium de franceschi, nata 3 currentis, hodie per me subscriptum baptizata. patrini fuere stephanus dubglich a dimino, et dna antonia fachinetti.» maria matthia, daughter of vittorio and euphemia de franceschi, born 3 september 1784, baptised the next day. (doc — the act itself, not the index of it.) this is the only baptism of vittorio's line on these leaves, and it makes the couple a documented marriage rather than an inferred one. the godmother, dna antonia fachinetti, is of the parish gentry; the godfather comes from dvigrad. the honest account of how it was found is the useful part. a frame-by-frame sweep is not a guarantee. eleven consecutive entries in one column at spread scale is exactly where attention fails, and this act sat in the eleventh. the index caught what the reading missed; the reading then proved what the index only asserted. neither method was sufficient alone. see /corrections/. ### what this volume genuinely does not contain there is no baptism for maria, antonio's daughter. frames 5–60 cover 1764–1775 continuously and she is not in them. she was likely born before 1764, in the earlier volume — whose first 154 images remain unread. croatia, hrvatska, istria, rijeka 0 not one croatian collection. the service reads italian civil registration — births, marriages, deaths, proclamations, banns supplements — and some american sets. it does not read the croatia church books, which is where almost all of this family's record lies. so why did it find rotilio? because his marriage was proclaimed at trieste in 1928, when istria was italian and the relevant office kept italian civil registers. the document that settled a croatian question was an italian one. that is the shape of what this service can do here: it reaches the family during the italian period and on the italian mainland, and nowhere else. ### what this opens and what it closes reachable — anything in italian civil registration: the istrian communes 1918–1943, trieste, pisino, fiume as fiume the italian province, and the mainland households at castelgomberto and elsewhere. albina cincopan had lived at trieste, which the proclamation says in as many words, and trieste's registers are inside this boundary. not reachable, and no amount of querying will change it — the fiume households of the 1740s (item 143), the gračišće registers before 1918 (item 75), klenovica and ledenice (items 76, 141), svetvinčenat, crikvenica, senj, bakar. these are church books in croatian collections and full-text does not index them. they stay archive questions, and item 141's letter to rijeka remains the route. ### the query syntax, which cost a wasted search unquoted terms are or-ed and the results are worthless. defranceschi valentino fiume returns 1,079,220 documents, with fiume matching fiume veneto in friuli — a different town in a different country. quoted, "valentino defranceschi" returns 4, all of them italian mainland and none at rijeka. always quote the phrase. 21 sept 2026 the fiume household is ours after all — the plate says «de franceschi» and the index was wrong yielded fiume film 005497925 image 150 — the 29 may 1748 entry read off the plate two hours ago this archive flagged a doubt against its own fiume household. the plate has now been read, and the doubt was misplaced — but it was right to raise it. the entry, magnified from the plate itself (film 005497925, image 150, right page, fourth entry): > die 29 maij 1748. «josephum aloysium filium legitimum d[omi]ni joannis bapt[ist]æ et d[omi]næ magdalenæ jugalium de franceschi, natus 28 hujus, baptisavit d[omi]nus can[onicu]s baches eustachius … patrini fuere d[omi]nus josephus voxila et d[omi]na eleonora frauel.» the surname is «de franceschi», written plainly. familysearch's household index for this image reads it «mancoschi» — for the parents too. the index is wrong and this archive was right. item 143 keeps its premise: there really are two defranceschi households at fiume in the 1740s. ### what the plate adds that the index never had - the child was born 28 may and baptised on the 29th — «natus 28 hujus». the index gives only the baptism. - both parents carry honorifics — d.ni joannis baptistæ and d.næ magdalenæ. this is a household the parish addressed as gentry, which squares with the d.nus already recorded for the father. - the godparents are new to this archive: dominus josephus voxila and domina eleonora frauel. neither is a defranceschi — so this entry does not, by itself, link the two fiume houses. item 143's question stands; only its premise is secured. - the celebrant was a canonicus, not the parish priest. ### the part that will change how this archive reads plates the frames were being fought, not read. four attempts at this one entry failed because crops were being guessed as fractions of the image — and the guesses were badly wrong: the book was assumed to sit in the top-left quadrant when it fills x 0.034–0.964, y 0.044–0.951 of the plate. the fix is to stop guessing and measure. the plate is fetched once — the sg30p0 url 401s to a bare request, but the browser's redirect yields a signed s3 url that serves it without a session — and then analysed locally:
page edges column and row means; paper is bright, surround is not
the gutter darkest column between 35% and 65% of the page

text lines row standard deviation, at full resolution brightness thresholding finds nothing on this film — the ink is too fine and any downscale averages it into the paper. variance works: it found 35 text lines on the left page and 38 on the right, which turns "somewhere on this plate" into "the fourth entry, lines 10 to 12". 21 sept 2026 valentino's household stood at the font with the captain of kastav's wife — but still no defranceschi godparent yielded fiume film 005497925 frame 77 — the 17 september 1739 baptism of valentino's son, read for its godparents item 143 asks how the two fiume households relate. with the plate-reading method now working, the obvious test is whether either house ever stood godparent to the other. the first of valentino's baptisms to be read says no — and says something else worth more. film 005497925, frame 77, right page — located by the index ark for matheus franciscus, then found on the plate by line-variance: > die 17 7bris 1739. «matthæus franciscus filius legitimus d. valentini et helenæ jugalium defranceschi, baptisavit d[omi]nus canonicus franciscus … ronaldi. patrini fuere nob. d[omi]nus petrus ronaldi, et nob. d[omi]na margarita uxor d[omi]ni georgij vlah, capitanei cast[u]anensis.» ### what it settles, and what it does not it does not join the two houses. the godparents are petrus ronaldi and margarita vlah — neither a defranceschi. together with the 1748 entry, whose godparents were josephus voxila and eleonora frauel, two of the family's fiume baptisms are now read and neither names anyone of the surname. (doc, for the negative.) but it places valentino socially, and higher than «venuto dalla carnia» suggests. - he is styled d. — dominus — in 1739, the year he became a citizen of fiume. not a newcomer being tolerated; a man the register addresses with the honorific. - both godparents are styled nob., noble. - the godmother is the wife of georgius vlah, capitaneus — a captain, of what reads as castuanensis: kastav, the fortified town above rijeka. - the celebrant was a canonicus, and shares the surname ronaldi with the godfather. that is the same stratum the other household moves in. joannes baptista and magdalena are d.ni with d.nus/d.na godparents; valentino is d. with nob. godparents. two defranceschi houses in one small port, both addressed as gentry, in the same decade. that is not proof of kinship — a port's merchant families share a stratum without sharing blood — but it is the first thing this archive has found that makes the two households look like one milieu rather than two coincidences. (inf, and stated as no more.) ### a caution carried forward the index gives this baptism's place as «vitipolis, modrus-fiume», not fiume. this archive does not yet know what vitipolis is and is not guessing; the plate itself is a volume of film 005497925, which the archive treats as fiume. the discrepancy is recorded, not resolved. and one more index error, of the kind already logged today: the record indexed as «antonio de franceschi, born 1753, parents elena and valentino» is not a baptism at all — the page says burial, 1 september 1753, age 0. the 1753 is familysearch's own estimate. reading it as a birth would have invented a child.what it produced on this sitework list item 143 · the kvarner households — rijeka and bakar · fiume (rijeka) · kastav

15 sept 2026 portale antenati — the udine inventory for mione and ovaro, catalogued rather than read yielded every civil-register volume for the two comuni, turned into an addressable list fifty-nine volumes, each one openable, none of them indexed by name. mione's napoleonic and austrian civil registration runs in seven series — matrimoni (9 volumes), matrimoni allegati (13), matrimoni indici (3), pubblicazioni (9), morti (9), morti indici (3) and nati (4). ovaro adds a matrimoni run of nine. the shape of that list is itself the finding. deaths and marriages run nine volumes; births run four. the civil births stop at 1810 while everything else carries on to 1815 — and 1807 is absent from every series. anyone born into these households between 1811 and 1815 is in the pieve di gorto or nowhere. years are given only where an act fixes them. four of the nati are dated exactly, and two ovaro matrimoni are; the rest are numbered within their series and given the series span, because that is what the inventory supports.what it produced on this siteall fifty-nine, every one a link · antenati on the research map · antenati, archivio di stato di udine

14 sept 2026 anno — every spelling, including the family's own yielded seven variants of the surname against the whole austrian press, and the one nobody had ever tried «defranceski» — the spelling this family actually uses — had never been searched in the austrian press. it returns 28 issues. «de franceski» gives 4 more, «defranzeschi» 19, «di franceschi» 13, «defrancheschi» 1. sixty-five issues in variants, on top of the 950 and 722 for the two main forms. and the dates give the game away. look at when «defranceski» appears in the official papers: · wiener zeitung — 21, 24 and 29 december 1872. three issues in nine days. · vereinigte laibacher zeitung — 3, 6 and 11 march 1875. three issues in eight days. and again 15, 24 and 28 june 1869. and again across june and july 1872. that is not news coverage. that is an edict. austrian official gazettes published legal notices — summonses, estates, bankruptcies, tenders — three times at set intervals, and the wiener zeitung and the laibacher zeitung were the gazettes of record for the empire and for carniola. seventeen issues of the laibach paper between 1865 and 1875 carry the name, in exactly that rhythm. so somewhere in carniola in those ten years, a defranceski was the subject of repeated official legal process. whether that is one man or several, and whether a court, an estate or a business, the issues themselves would say in a line. two more that open ground this archive has never been on: · nachrichten über verwundete und verletzte, 21 and 30 december 1914 — the austro-hungarian casualty lists. a defranceski, twice, in the war's first winter. this archive has covered the second world war in detail and has never once looked at a first world war casualty list. · lagerzeitung für wagna, 4 february 1917 — the newspaper of the wagna camp itself. the archive already holds the camp's intake lists from the rovigno monograph, with two defranceschi of dignano in them; this is the camp's own paper, which is a different record, and it names a defranceski. and the tyrolean cluster sorts itself out. «defranzeschi» is almost entirely der tiroler, the innsbrucker nachrichten and the allgemeiner tiroler anzeiger, 1899–1927, published at bozen and innsbruck — which is the trentino group this site files as a blind spot. it now has a spelling and a set of dates. none of it has been read: anno's page viewer is behind a cloudflare check this archive does not answer.what it produced on this sitevodnjan · trentino · the name in imperial service · anno — austrian newspapers online

10 sept 2026 the register — 1,508 harvested familysearch personas yielded every household in the catch, not just vodnjan's with the film blocked, the whole catch was mined for parent-pairs rather than only its istrian rows. it gave 48 households the archive did not have, holding 151 children — among them veneranda defranceschi × antonius subiotto (eight children, 1858–1874), pascha defranceschi × angelus ferrarese (seven, 1849–1864), francesco franceschi × maria de caralipeo at almissa in dalmatia (seven, 1856–1873), and josephi defranceschi × mariæ defranceschi at ližnjan (five, 1872–1888). every one is filed index, not read — the pattern is real, the spellings are the indexer's, and no page has been seen. 34 are in istria, 11 in dalmatia, 10 in the kvarner and 43 could not be placed at all. three pairs are flagged as possibly one household each — bellinich twice, zanghirella twice, lazar twice — where the surnames match once the spellings are set aside and the years all but touch. they are kept apart, because merging two households on a surname is how one family becomes a fiction. the merge itself had to be built twice. the first pass counted 100 pairs, most of them latin genitives of each other — valentini and valentino, ursulæ and orsola, josephi and giuseppe — and francetich rows that are not this family at all. normalising the genitives, collapsing doubled letters and requiring a de franceschi parent brought it to 48.what it produced on this sitevodnjan · ližnjan · rijeka and bakar · familysearch record search

10 sept 2026 family testimony — david defranceski yielded 1948: an attempt to leave the country asked what «went» meant, david answered: «they went to leave the country in 1948.» that converts a contradiction into a window. their son was born at senj on 17 december 1951, so they were back on the coast by about march 1951; ivan died at senj in 1995. they left in 1948, were home inside about two and a half years, and never got out — hedviga reached johannesburg only much later, and ivan never did. the route is not a mystery either. the family already had a household in pfullingen, in the french occupation zone: ivan had worked at reutlingen from 21 october 1941, his father was on the 1947 pfullingen list of foreigners, and his brothers zdravko and anton went out to australia from there in 1949 — anton's card stamped «emigré australie le 8.3.49». ivan and hedviga were a year behind them at a door that was closing, the iro shutting its books at the end of february 1952. a failed exit leaves no yugoslav paper. the arolsen request has been rewritten accordingly and is now the highest-value errand this project holds.what it produced on this sitesenj · pfullingen · where the name went · defranceski.com

10 sept 2026 archives de corse — archives.isula.corsica yielded whether the corsican records can be searched by surname they cannot, and finding that out is the result. the archives of the collectivité de corse are free, need no account and are not familysearch — the platform refuses a command-line client but opens normally in a browser. no module has a surname field. état civil, corsica christiana, recensements, registres matricules all take the same three criteria — commune, date range, record type — and the platform says outright that anything else is une recherche non indexée. so corsica is images to be read, like vodnjan. but the record types include table décennale — the alphabetical ten-yearly index french civil registration compiled for every commune, 1793–1902. that is roughly eleven index pages per commune instead of ten years of acts, and it is why corsica can be finished when vodnjan cannot: an austrian liber defunctorum was never indexed by anybody. six cap corse communes are on the platform and all are in scope: tomino, rogliano, ersa, centuri, morsiglia, barrettali. available types: naissances, mariages, décès, baptêmes, sépultures, publications de mariage, table décennale.what it produced on this sitevodnjan · corsica · the parish books · archives de corse

9 sept 2026 findmypast british & irish newspapers — keyword «defranceschi» yielded seventy articles; the earliest sixty are shipping intelligence a whole chapter nobody knew was there. between 1865 and 1878 a master of this name commands austrian ships in the black sea grain and bristol channel coal trades — the natalia out of constantinople and galatz, the rachel from odessa to antwerp, the peppina luigia trieste to troon, and above all the aquilone, «aus, 350, defranceschi», tracked through nineteen printed sightings from alexandria and sulina to belfast, malta, venice, ghent, barcelona and out of cardiff for guadaloupe on 11 december 1877. the masters printed beside him are bujanovich, lacovich, cattarinich, ivancich, nicolich — the sea-captain families of lošinj, rijeka and bakar, and this archive has an unplaced dominus household at bakar. and in 1896 the south wales echo writes that «signorina defranceschi belongs to an old cardiff family, and has recently taken her degree at the vienna conservatoire of music», playing harpsichord recitals at the cardiff exhibition. published at /at-sea/.what it produced on this siterijeka and bakar · at sea · findmypast

sept 2026 myheritage — david's live family tree yielded read directly from his logged-in session: 459 individuals carrying the surname, harvested through the site's own lookup and person-panel endpoints, with their dates, places, relationships and source citations the 2018 gedcom this project had been using holds 8,286 people; the live tree holds 15,643, and david's own verdict on the old file is «really old and really wrong». it is now retired. 211 of the 459 carry citations, 262 distinct familysearch arks between them. the direct line agrees wherever both hold a fact, and the tree supplies what this archive lacked: exact death dates for antonius (4 aug 1894) and for giovanni battista (14 sep 1846), gologorica rather than gračišće as the 1787 birthplace, and an ark for the 1750 giovanni that no page had ever been put in front of. the working notes behind it are not published: they quote the export row by row, and the export carries living people in full. what the reconciliation actually settled is on this page and in the corrections it produced.what it produced on this sitegologorica · the roster · myheritage — david's tree 4

sept 2026 myheritage — what the tree holds and this archive did not yielded compared row by row against the published site antonius franciscus defranceschi, born gologorica 31 january 1909, died at dachau 7 august 1945. giuseppe de franceschi, born gračišće 12 march 1892, died new york city 26 april 1940, with six citations. bruno defranceschi, born gologorica 20 november 1942, died 15 january 2023. anna maria francisca, born gologorica 1860, died trieste 1941. a «soravito de franceschi» lineage at mione running from a francesco of 1450 to francesco andrea, died 1971 — one of them, antonio bartolomeo, going mione to nantes. mione is the largest single place in the whole tree at 29 people, which this archive has treated as an origin and not as a living branch. and marijana de franceschi (bitanga-radovinović), confirming the jagul marriage from the imotski page.what it produced on this sitegologorica · carnia · imotski · myheritage — david's tree 4

sept 2026 david's google mymaps — the emigration layers yielded «high level of emigration from here» (44 pins) and «italian lines» (90 pins), read from the archived kml a departure region for the brazilian cluster, which this archive has never had. scorzè, moniego (noale), cornedo vicentino, castelgomberto and pederobba in the veneto — with «de franceschi luigi, spouse barolo caterina luigia, from moniego, noale, venezia to são paulo» and «giuseppe romano de franceschi, born scorzè 22 may 1835, died moniego». and a second region entirely: the castelnuovo pin is castelnuovo in the valsugana, trentino — four kilometres from telve, where david's tree holds eighteen people of this surname. the são paulo destinations are all coffee-belt, which is a different and later migration from the rio grande do sul colonies of 1875. brazil is two stories, not one. also on those layers: castelnovo del friuli to trostberg in bavaria (peter defranceschi b. 19 feb 1841); mione to biella; bishop lucio soravito de franceschi of adria-rovigo; and a france cluster around metz, nancy, fréjus and propriano.what it produced on this sitecarnia · trentino · where the name went · google my maps

sept 2026 gradska groblja zagreb — the city burial register yielded every spelling searched through the cemeteries' own odata service: mirogoj, miroševac, markovo polje and twenty-five other grounds, 1750 to now thirteen burials of the name, and the register carries parents' names on some of them. milan defrančeski (d. 2001, aged 78) and dragutin (d. 2004, aged 79) are entered as children of «grgo i marija» and «marija i grga» — two brothers naming the same father, which is the grga of david's old map pin, now with two graves that can be visited. it also contradicts the myheritage tree, which gives grgo as born 1931: a man whose sons were born about 1923 and 1925 was not. marija defrančeski, d. 3 june 1971 aged 87, mirogoj 147a/ii/58, with zdenka, dead 16 march 1945 aged two and not buried until christmas eve 1971 — the child moved in beside her. antun (d. 5 june 1943, aged 67) and justina (d. 1963, aged 78) share mirogoj 136/ii/43. and an uršula defrančeski, born about 1892, at miroševac. endpoint: axiomgis.com/zagreb/trazilica.svc/pvwebukopani.what it produced on this sitethe headstones · the register · the roster · gradska groblja zagreb

sept 2026 francesco de' franceschi, the painter yielded the fifteenth-century venetian painter carried on the roadmap as unfinished active 1443–1468, birth and death unknown. religious work on church commission; the style follows michele giambono and he may have worked with antonio vivarini. an altarpiece of 1447 in the museo civico at padua; a st mary magdalen and a st catherine of alexandria in the ashmolean at oxford; a st michael the archangel and a st mamas series. not kin — two and a half centuries before this family reaches istria. roadmap item closed. · namesakes, on this site

sept 2026 the family's own field photographs, 2026 yielded 491 images from six visits — carnia (ovaro, mione, muina, agrons), gologorica house and graves, gračišće, seget and umag, crikvenica–klenovica–novi–senj, and the pazin reading room — read as contact sheets so that the frames worth publishing can be chosen read as contact sheets and plated. 31 published so far. gologorica (11): the builder's tablet, the memorial to carlo, the arms cartouche with the madonna aedicule beneath it, the blazon in the tomb pediment and the same arms weathered nearly smooth on an older stone, the tomb, the house from the lane, the arcaded end with the number 22, a wall niche, a carved ring, the chapel. carnia (10): soravito de franceschi cut in stone at ovaro with anna crosilla his widow; de franceschi ugo 1930–2020; antonio 1877–1962 with marta anzola dead at twenty-five; gio. batta 1880–1963; francesco 1887–1945; an 1850s stone; the war memorial carrying vittorio and isidoro de franceschi; the campanile of santa maria di gorto over the graves — the pieve whose parishes drew up the 1679 return. gračišće (3): «f de franceschi» with marfan virginija and nazarijo; the salamon grave, which turns francisca salamon from a surname into a family still in that ground; and a marfan stone. umag and seget (7): the tomb's blue-and-gilt ironwork lunette with a lion rampant beneath a star under a coronet — the other family's arms, against gologorica's cross, arrows and pomegranate; «famiglia de franceschi — seghetto»; «famiglia ettore de franceschi»; a stone of 1848; the house at seget; the tomb whole; the pine-cone finial. living people appear in many frames and are excluded throughout. klenovica and the coast (6): «obitelj defranceski» with three portrait medallions — the household under the name it took on the coast — and then the kalanj, who are everywhere in that ground: marija 1889–1970, josip, franjo and zora on one stone, rozalija anton marija and milan on another, vinko and paulina, tomislav, marijan, and the kalanj-perković. anton rudolf's mother was ana kalanj of klenovica house 22, and it is her family and not his that stayed. also a partisan star laid in white stone among the graves. 39 field plates published across six places. the pazin reading-room set of 117 is register images rather than ground; two of them are now published on the eleven — the gračišće status animarum for house 24, which carries the midwife maria fernazar's household, the eleven children in one column, and daniel's household beneath. that page also settled josip's birth at 22 march 1863 and joined basilio of new york to this line.what it produced on this sitethe eleven of gračišće · gologorica · carnia · the plates, on this site

sept 2026 documents and photographs supplied by the family, 8 september 2026 yielded five items sent in one morning: the zdravko plaque at horsham, ivan's grave at senj, the whole opening of anton rudolf's 1890 baptism, a marriage register opening of 1772, and the 1951 senj birth certificate — checked one by one against what this archive already held three of the five were already here and all three were held in a worse copy. the horsham plaque was a 1000-pixel thumbnail out of the family tree package and is now the 3648-pixel camera original, with the founder's mark legible. ivan's grave was 400 pixels wide and the dates could not be read at all; at 2368 they read 1925–1995. anton rudolf's 1890 baptism was a cropped strip of entry 9, and the whole page adds three things the strip cut off — a pencil note «vjenčao se na crikvenici», a remarks column explaining that the parents were staying with the wife's people at klenovica, and the printer's line «tisak h. luster u senju». the 1951 certificate was new, and carries the word stateless against the father in his own country. the 1772 marriage was new as an image: this archive had the familysearch index row for it and had written that an index is only an index. it is now the page.what it produced on this sitesenj · the headstones · the plates · the plates, on this site

sept 2026 hr-hda-1448 — the croatian state archives' supplementary register microfilms yielded the finding aid at arhiv.hr, searched for crikvenica and proložac across all seven kinds of register. this collection filmed the parish offices and the civil registry offices as well as the state archives, so it is not bound by the cut that ends familysearch's croatian birth registers in the 1880s and 1890s the single most useful thing found for this archive in weeks, and it is a catalogue rather than a record. for crikvenica it lists births to 1948, marriages to 1947, deaths to 1928, and — this is the one — a status animarum of the twentieth century, roll zm-34j/251, mark m-5976, digitised, from the župni ured crikvenica. a status animarum lists a house, its head, his wife and every child with a birth date; it is the form that gave this archive the whole of gračišće house 24 in one opening. crikvenica births 1897–1908 are absent here too and may not survive, but the household book and the marriage register of 1909–1947 between them should answer the three unaccounted names on the crikvenica monument without the baptisms at all. proložac, the imotski family's own parish, runs unbroken 1853–1949 with everything from 1892 digitised. ordered by e-mail to info@arhiv.hr quoting place, kind, period, roll signature and topographic mark; read in the hda reading room, ten units a day. nothing has been read yet — this is the list of what exists and where.what it produced on this sitecrikvenica · imotski · the marriages · hrvatski državni arhiv

sept 2026 seget and imotski, taken back to the sources yielded the two non-istrian houses of the surname, researched past the secondary accounts this site had been using: the 2016 conservation study of stancija seget, the istrian encyclopaedia, and the franciscan province of split's own histories of its omiš and imotski convents seget: the house carries its own dates — «1724» on the courtyard portal and «1732» with the initials «ma. f.» on the cistern, marc'antonio's monogram on his own well-head. a generation appears that this archive had never printed: giorgio de franceschi, 1788–1865, who threw a staircase block along the east front in 1843–45 and put a classicist façade over it, frescoed inside by michele urban, the architect to be sought among those practising at trieste. the estate's economy turns from wine to olive oil about 1840. and the venier–valier disagreement is settled for venier, from 1623. imotski: four corrections. the friars were not at proložac village but on an islet in prološko blato from about 1600, marked by a stone cut a.d. 1609. the party zuane sheltered was fifteen people of whom nine were friars, with a lay brother, four schoolboys and a hermit. skalice at omiš was begun 13 july 1716 and blessed 29 october 1718 on ground belonging to pavao despotović and jakov mariani. and the friars did not return in 1717 — they returned in 1738, building at imotski from 1740. zuane's own dates are 1673–1741. and one unopened primary source: at skalice there is a book bound in sheepskin, written in bosančica on 416 leaves, which is the friars' own chronicle of the flight. it is in a friary, not an archive. and then the thesis was read. david cleared the repository's bot check himself, and «uloga obitelji franceschi u mletačkom osvajanju imotskog» — matea kaćunić, split, september 2025, 77 pages, open access — turns out to be the best single source on the dalmatian family that exists. it corrects this archive six times and adds a second estate. full account on the imotski page; the pdf is now in this project's library.what it produced on this siteomiš · imotski · seget · seget, on this site

sept 2026 the imotski death register, read off the page yielded the first unindexed familysearch register image this archive has read at full resolution, rather than through the viewer's shrunken view — imotski-glavina, atti di morte, third quarter 1845 entry 17. «franceschi domenica», 48, cattolica, «moglie di q.m giovanni vucemilovich» — and in the patria column, «nata in almissa, domiciliata in imoschi». almissa is omiš. her parents are given as «q.m vicenzo franceschi, q.m antonia cappelletti»; she died at three in the morning of 10 august 1845 in her husband's house of chronic gastritis, was seen by the district surgeon ravlin on the 11th and buried the same day in the town cemetery of imotski, by fra bernardino brajković. that is the join between the omiš branch and the imotski household, in a parish register. the method is the other half of the finding and it is reusable: familysearch serves each image as a deep zoom pyramid, and from a signed-in session the tiles of any chosen rectangle can be composed at true resolution — a 6180 × 4247 master read as clearly as the open book, instead of the 600-pixel view the ordinary viewer gives. written up on the parish books page. every unindexed volume this archive has listed is now actually readable.what it produced on this siteomiš · imotski · the parish books · imotski, on this site

sept 2026 šišić, «an abridged political history of rieka (fiume)», paris 1919 yielded a 160-page brief written for the paris peace conference by a member of the yugoslav delegation, with a documentary appendix of fiume's nineteenth-century election papers. read in full for the surname and for the istrian and kvarner place-names one hit in a hundred and sixty pages, and it is the right one. appendix xviii, the protocol of the electoral committee of fiume's second college, 20 april 1871: the assessors are «signor francesco defranceschi» and francesco seemann under president pietro dabalà, and the protocol is signed at the foot «frco defranceschi». 128 of 1,115 electors voted; 126 chose dr antonio randich to replace the resigning giovanni de ciotta in the croatian-slavonian diet. almost certainly kobler's francesco giuseppe de franceschi, patrician councillor and royal harbourmaster, of the stock that came «da pisino» — which is the county of pazin, which is where this archive's own villages are. written up on the kobler page. it also names a source worth chasing: the fiume electoral roll of 1871.what it produced on this siterijeka and bakar · carlo de franceschi · namesakes and landmarks · internet archive

sept 2026 regan & nadilo, «istarski kašteli … sjeverno od čepićkog polja», građevinar 2012 yielded a civil-engineering journal's architectural survey of the fortified places north of the čepić field, including gologorica building by building — supplied by the family a hard date for the lease, and a name for the relief. the gologorica benefice was founded in 1443 by the pazin provost andreas schuel; frederick iii took the right of appointment; the holders were the captains of pazin and the bishops of pedena, then the marquis de prié, then charles antoine biotz, and «naposljetku od 1772. obitelj de franceschi … do ukidanja feudalnih odnosa 1848» — the de franceschi held it on lease from 1772 to 1848, seventy-six years. that fits carlo's «affitto fermo» rather than contradicting it, and dates it. the house is described as «velika kamena palača obitelji de franceschi, dvokatna građevina s balkonom i portalom iz 1711., ukrašena grbom i natpisom te reljefom s prikazom isusa» — which settles a thing this site once got wrong: the relief over the door is a figure of christ, and it is real. also: gologorica burned in 1463, 1508 and 1511; the bell tower finished 1740; an imago pietatis of 1446 and a glagolitic inscription of 1595 in the parish church; and mikula gologorički, priest of this parish, wrote the croatian glagolitic version of the istrian boundary settlement of 1325.what it produced on this sitegologorica · građevinar (hrčak)

sept 2026 križman, «antička svjedočanstva o istri» (1979) — found online and read yielded david asked whether the book could be found. it can: the full text is uploaded to both scribd and idoc.pub, and it was read there carlo de franceschi is cited eleven times — indexed at pages 170, 189, 192, 193, 211 and 263, with «l'istria, note storiche» (poreč 1879) quoted at pp. 10–11, 38ff, 45 and 67, on the topography of the istrian war of 177 bc, the siege of nesactium, and whether the pontic and adriatic histri are one people. križman sets him beside kandler, gnirs, benussi and zippel, and endorses his identification of livy's mutila with medulin and faveria with mutvoran as the least likely to be wrong. and it puts gologorica in antiquity: gnirs's proposal that the ancient alùon lay on the veli potok between pićan and gologorica, where the roman inscriptions cil v 322, 323, 424 and 425 were found.what it produced on this sitegologorica · carlo de franceschi · mate križman, «antička svjedočanstva o istri»

sept 2026 twenty-three scans from the family, read and ranked in one pass yielded every one converted to text and tested for the surname in five spellings and for fifteen place-names, then the ones that scored were read three worth a section, five worth a line, eleven with the places but not the family, and four that cannot be read at all. the best is «los franceschi, la pequeña historia de una familia» by napoleón franceschi gonzález (caracas 2002) — the corsican branch written from inside it, from ersa in cap corse, first generation pietro franceschi 1694–1771, out through the french caribbean to venezuela, with not one line touching istria. that closes the corsica marker on the family's map. «atti» 39 of rovinj yields camillo de franceschi's pula bibliography, including «testamenti polesani del secolo xv con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di pola» — sixteen fifteenth-century pula wills he transcribed, which is the obvious next reading for the southern-istrian cluster. «istra iz pera nobilea» reports the ex libris «de franceschi – seghetto» on books in the provincial library — the seget house's own library — and has camillo buying the nobile drawings at koper in 1934 and 1941, and giulio drawing monuments better than nobile did. four are image-only with no text layer and need ocr: the planckenstein almanac of trieste 1869 (327 pages), jelenić on the sacred art of umag and its surroundings (135 pages), the hrvati i karolinzi catalogue, and «piazza maggiore era troppo piccola». the first two are worth the trouble; an 1869 littoral almanac is exactly where a harbourmaster or a civic assessor is listed by name.what it produced on this siteseget · corsica · the plates · the plates, on this site

sept 2026 jelenić, «sakralno bogatstvo umaga i okolice» — ocr'd and read yielded a 168-megabyte image-only scan with no text layer at all, put through optical character recognition on this project's machine and then searched. 135 pages, parallel croatian and english four things, and one of them is a correction. a section on seget: the villa fifteen hundred metres from umag among the vineyards on the novigrad road, passing to the de franceschi in 1720, «ranije vlasništvo katarine bernardo valier» — which gives the vendor a christian name and moves the venier–valier question to valier, against this site's earlier reading. the library confirmed from the parish's side — «vrlo bogatu knjižnicu» — matching the ex libris «de franceschi – seghetto» found in the provincial library. the family chapel, right of the villa entrance with its own door and a small apse outside; a wooden altar, an assumption with st anthony and st catherine, an old canvas of st lucy, a wall cupboard — restored in the 1990s, and mass said in it once a year on easter monday. and in the parish church of umag, a canvas of 1650, our lady of the rosary, whose painter's name is illegible but which carries the arms of the de franceschi of umag — nineteen years before the flight from candia. either the arms were added later by a donor family, or the name was at umag before 1669. not resolved, and not guessed at.what it produced on this siteseget · the plates · hrčak

sept 2026 «guida schematica di trieste» 1869 — ocr'd and read yielded 327 pages of city directory, scanned at 122 megabytes with no text layer; converted on this project's machine and searched for the surname in every spelling four occurrences in three hundred and twenty-seven pages, and two of them are people. «defranceschi corrado, controllore in pens., v. caserma 12» — a retired controller of the imperial financial service, listed among the possidenti e privati. and «gleyre costante (enrico de franceschi), in manifatture e pece, v. s. spiridione 7» — a merchant house in textiles and pitch, with enrico de franceschi named as the man behind it. the other two are franceschinelli and defrancesco, different formations of the same root, recorded so the next search does not stop at them. nothing joins either man to a line on this site; what the book proves is that two households of the name were living and trading in trieste in 1869, twenty years before camillo de franceschi settled there. the directories for other years would say whether they stayed.what it produced on this sitethe plates · openstarts, trieste

sept 2026 the pazin archive's own price list — the acquisitions queue, priced yielded «acquisitions» has sat on this project's research log as a wish list for months. dapa publishes a current price list; it was read, and most of what was wanted turns out to be in print and cheap seven titles, about a hundred and fifty-four euro, and the first three would close three questions this site currently prints as open. jelinčić's «knjiga ređenja u pićnu (prothocollum) 1632–1783», €19.91 — a hundred and fifty years of pedena ordinations, and an ordination entry names the ordinand's father. this archive has four priests of the name it cannot place. orbanić's edition of de buset's spiritual visitation of 1788, €13.27, 477 pages, isbn 978-953-7640-30-9, published in the vatican and covering gologorica and gallignana parish by parish in the last year of the diocese of pićan. doblanović šuran and mogorović crljenko, «matična knjiga krštenih župe umag 1483–1643», €26.54 — which is the direct test of the 1650 painting in umag that carries the family arms nineteen years before the family is supposed to have arrived. then joksimović's edition of valier's 1580 apostolic visitation of the diocese of pula, €60, aimed straight at the unplaced southern-istrian cluster; the 1571 urbarium of the county of pazin, €10; slukan altić's «katastar istre», €9.29; and dapa's own beginner's guide to genealogy in its holdings, €15. two wanted volumes are sold out. both the translator and the editor of the 1788 visitation — jakov jelinčić and elvis orbanić — are already on this project's list of people to write to, and both work at pazin.what it produced on this sitegologorica · državni arhiv u pazinu

sept 2026 istrianet — camillo de franceschi's collected bibliography yielded a queued item finally worked: the site's page of his selected works forty-five entries between 1898 and 1964, with volumes and pages, compiled from the italian librarians' biographical database and the trieste civic library catalogue. three land on questions open on this site today. «testamenti polesani del secolo xv, con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di pola», amsi 42 (1930), pp. 167–219 — now properly cited, and aimed straight at the unplaced pula cluster. «la popolazione di pola nel secolo xv e nei seguenti», archeografo triestino ser. 3 vol. 3 (1906), pp. 221–315 — the same question from the other side, ninety-four pages of it. and «quando e da chi sia stato ideato l'apocrifo istrumento di confinazione della contea di pisino con la data del 1325», archivio veneto ser. 5, 30/31 (1942) — in which camillo, of gologorica, argues that the istrian boundary settlement is a forgery, a document whose glagolitic version was written by the parish priest of gologorica. also «i castelli della val d'arsa» (1900), with unpublished documents and genealogical trees, and «ricordi di biblioteca» (1959), seventy-four pages by the man who bought the nobile drawings and shelved the seget library.what it produced on this sitegologorica · seget · carlo de franceschi · istrianet.org

sept 2026 «gazzetta di zara», 4 august 1840 (anno) yielded the oldest of the nine issues anno returned for «defranceschi» + «buccari», read page by page one occurrence of the surname, and it is at omiš, not bakar. a state-property auction notice of the i.r. pretura d'almissa, 6 july 1840, lists a vineyard at strane in vrisovec «tenuto a colonia al quarto da d. nicolò defranceschi», fiscal value fl. 8 k. 20. «buccari» appears in a wholly separate notice pages away — so anno's pairing is whole-issue co-occurrence, not a defranceschi at bakar, and the bakar lead is weaker than it looked. published on the omiš line. pdf fetched by david; the bot check was not answered.what it produced on this siteomiš · rijeka and bakar · the plates · anno — gazzetta di zara, 4 aug 1840

sept 2026 darovec, «migration to istria and the north adriatic in the modern age» (2021) yielded the queued migration paper, read in full — from the publisher's open pdf, not from academia.edu no occurrence of the surname, and the best contextual source this archive has found. it puts both of our istrian arrivals inside documented movements: the carni as one of the named peoples of istria in petronio's list of 1681, settling exactly at pazin, pićan, gradišće, žminj and tinjan; the slavicisation of immigrant friulian surnames (furlanich, callegarich), which is the mechanism behind defrančeski; and twelve venetian attempts between 1530 and 1669 to settle greeks from crete and the morea in istria, the survivors absorbed into the italian-speaking towns. published on the lines page. note for method: academia.edu is behind a bot check this archive will not answer, and the paper was open on the publisher's own site all along.what it produced on this sitethe plates · the method · hrčak

sept 2026 the eleven of gračišće, against the american record yielded united states naturalizations, censuses, death certificates and the numident, searched for every child of antonio the mason five of the eleven documented in new york, four of them in brooklyn. the proof is a misspelling: albina's new york death certificate of 27 april 1945 names her mother «maria walhart» and bruno's naturalization names her «mary walhal» — both of them the volhardt the gračišće priest wrote in 1925. also corrects this archive: antonio «tony», whom the album put in italy, naturalised at brooklyn in 1922 and 1929.what it produced on this sitethe eleven of gračišće · the eleven, on this site

sept 2026 «zbirka obitelji de franceschi u nsk» (libellarium 13/2, 2022) yielded a search for the šeget fond's finding aid turned this up instead the family's library is not lost. it is in zagreb, and it has been catalogued. 2,396 items, 1503–1945, taken out of the house at gologorica in 1948–49, boxed, and left unprocessed in the national and university library's store for sixty years — not in the card catalogue, not in the electronic one, «nobody could know of its existence». processing began 2009 and finished in 2021. it holds an aldine of 1503, the signatures of five generations, letters of d'annunzio, poems of giuseppina martinuzzi, and the very metastasio, petrarch, tasso and ariosto that carlo says he found on the family shelves as a schoolboy. published on the library page.what it produced on this sitegologorica · libellarium

sept 2026 svetvinčenat parish register, dgs 005497884 — read, not searched yielded images 397, 398 and 442 opened tile by tile and read line by line three unindexed occurrences on the first three openings. «m.ro nadal de franceschi» stands godfather on 20 may 1666, five months before his own daughter is baptised; «il sig.r ant.o di franceschi» stands godfather on 9 february 1674. godparent roles are never indexed, which is the whole reason to open the page. the baptisms of colotta (24 oct 1666) and fioretta (22 nov 1666) are confirmed word for word, both fathers styled m.ro. and the company is the argument: the godparents across these openings are spinoti, fiorenza, felicer, fabri — the canale di gorto set, standing at each other's fonts in a croatian village in 1666. by 1674 anto is sig.r and his son's compare is a count luciani: the same household, eight years, artisan to gentleman.what it produced on this sitethe parish books · familysearch film 005497884

sept 2026 «il sig.r conte lucciani», svetvinčenat 1674 — chased yielded the godfather at mattio de franceschi's baptism, traced through the index and the films he is of the albona house. the surname enlarges cleanly to lucciani; the place after «da» will not settle between d and r. the index carries a luciani family baptising at exactly these dates — bartolomio zuane on 12 november 1674, and five more between 1682 and 1693 — and every one of them resolves to the parish register of labin (albona), dgs 005494791–2. which closes a circle: carlo de franceschi names «cav. tomaso luciani … di albona» among his sources in 1879, luciani's ex libris is in the family library now at zagreb, and hauptmann found letters of tomaso luciani in the wrecked house at gologorica in 1945. two hundred years, one surname, one town — pairing stated, descent not claimed.what it produced on this sitegologorica · carlo de franceschi · the parish books · familysearch film 005497884

sept 2026 svetvinčenat film, seven openings read band by band yielded dgs 005497884 images 397, 398, 402, 415, 423, 428, 437, 442 — baptisms of 1666, 1667, 1669, 1671, 1673, 1674 eight occurrences the index does not have, all godparent roles, plus four baptisms confirmed word for word. the best line is «comp.ri furono m.ro ant.o di franceschi di piero» (25 oct 1667) — a patronymic, which gives anto a father and pushes the family a generation behind the twelve the index knows. also: mattia of 1669 is «fig.a… nata», a daughter, not the son the name suggested; anto stands godfather twice in eight days in october 1669; and the honorifics turn out not to be a clean ladder — m.ro, s.r and no style at all all appear in 1669–71, which corrects a tidier claim published here earlier. carnian company in the same pages: spinotti, fiorencis, felice, fabris, festa. twelve openings of this film still to read.what it produced on this sitecarnia · the parish books · familysearch film 005497884

143 1717 — the anchor that broke the error

205 a microfilm resolution target — a volume boundary about 2.2 frames to the year from 178 to 198, steady. so the window for 1740–1748 is frames ≈194–204, not 128–165 — and it runs into the boundary at 205, so the last years of the window may continue in the section after the target. eleven frames and a join, rather than thirty-eight in the wrong place. the method lesson is narrower than «anchor by reading», which this archive already says. reading is not enough when the digit itself is ambiguous. a year is only anchored when it is either written unambiguously or cross-checked against a neighbouring frame — and a run's plausibility is a test: 143 being 1717 while 142 was read 1746 should have been caught the moment both were written down. nothing was read on the strength of the wrong window; the error was found while setting up to read it. · pazin — contea di pisino

20 sept 2026 anzoletta — whose wife? the 1728 entry against the archive's own 1733 line not yet whether anzoletta is the wife of gio batta or of giacomo defranceschi, because this archive now says both two readings, both in this archive, and they do not agree. the families page has long carried, from the index, «1733 maria, of giacomo and anzoletta» among the twelve fathers of the name at svetvinčenat. the carta 66 entry read on 20 september says «catta fig.a leg.ma di s.r batta de fran.chi et di anzoletta sua consorte, nata li 10 d.to» — 1728. so anzoletta is given to two different husbands five years apart. three readings are possible and the archive will not pick one from a forename: 1. two women of the name. anzoletta is the venetian diminutive of angela and common; two households of one surname in one small town could easily hold two. 2. a misreading on carta 66. «batta» and «giacomo» do not look alike, but the entry is abbreviated and the archive has been wrong on a forename before. 3. a remarriage. gio batta's last known child is battistina, 23 december 1731; giacomo's first is domenico gasparo, 9 august 1732. that is seven and a half months — too short for a widow to remarry and bear a child, so if it is a remarriage the 1732 child is not hers, and the 1733 maria might be. thin, but not impossible. what settles it is carta 80 for the 1732 baptism and the 1733 entry behind the families page's line: both name the mother. neither has been opened. until they are, this archive holds two anzolettas and says so rather than quietly merging them. pending — and flagged because a silent merge here would invent a household. · svetvinčenat (san vincenti)

sept 2026 the zoppola thread — tested and cut nothing the one clue that pointed the pula–fažana–ližnjan cluster at friuli: a giambattista de franceschi with children registered at zoppola in udine in 1779, 1811 and 1813 not evidence. a smart match. four things kill it. the tree gives the same father a daughter lucia born 1779 and dead 1813 and a second daughter lucia born 19 january 1811 — a second living daughter given her sister's name, which does not happen; so these are two men. the 1813 citation names him «giambattista de franceschi o samassa», and samassa is a zoppola surname in its own right — samassa rachele and samassa giovanni are both in zoppola's own civil registers. a full-text sweep returns de franceschi all across that plain: azzano decimo 1897, cordenons, pordenone 1888 and 1898, zoppola. and zoppola is the friulian plain twenty-five kilometres west of pordenone; carnia is sixty kilometres north, in the mountains — so even a real link would not have been a carnian one. the cluster is back to having no origin, which is the honest position.what it produced on this sitecarnia · ližnjan · the corrections, on this site

medulin in these years is a village of croatian patronymics and nothing else: radonovich (dominant — dozens of entries), micaglievich, gracalich, grubisich, golemovich, stefanelich, marinovich,
