15 sept 2026 familysearch — «hungary, civil registration, 1895–1980» (collection 1452460) other whether fiume, the croatian littoral or međimurje are in it — the last of the promising candidates no. and the reason is constitutional, which makes this a better answer than a hit would have been. the collection browses by 33 hungarian counties — abaúj-torna, arad, bács-bodrog, baranya, bars, békés … vas, veszprém, zala. not one croatian-slavonian county — no zagreb, no varaždin, no modruš-rijeka, no lika-krbava, no srijem — and no fiume, despite fiume being a hungarian corpus separatum. hungary introduced civil registration in 1895. croatia-slavonia did not. under the nagodba it ran its own administration and kept the parish registers as the legal civil record until 1946. that single fact explains why familysearch's croatian collection is church books and why there is no croatian civil registration to find anywhere — it was never created. and it explains međimurje. međimurje's civil registers exist from 1895 because međimurje was administered as part of zala county — as hungary proper, not as croatia. the anomaly was never an archival quirk; it was a border. checked rather than assumed. zala in this collection holds 235 districts and not one of csáktornya, perlak, nedelicz, stridó, kottori or légrád — those sit in the slovenia-titled collection, so the two do not overlap and nothing is duplicated. the 16 defranceschi records inside are budapest, esztergom and sopron. both promising candidates are now closed. gračišće, gologorica and pićan are not in austria and not in hungary, and on present evidence they are filmed nowhere.what it produced on this sitethe collections, and what each holds · what pazin holds on paper instead · familysearch collection 1452460

every row now carries a way out of the table. the source name is a link to where the search was actually done — a portal's search page, a newspaper's run at anno, a film at familysearch, a journal's issue. where the material came from the family, or from a book that is not online, the link points instead at the page of this site where the scans and extracts live, and says «on this site» rather than naming a host.

«what it produced on this site» is the other direction: from a search to the pages its findings ended up on. that is where the extracts, the transcriptions and the images are — a register row here is the receipt, not the evidence.

three of the five outcomes are the useful ones. nothing is the heading that saves work: five gigabytes of theology journals searched end to end for twenty place-names and every spelling of the surname, and not one hit — that is worth recording so it is never done again. three of the entries under it are entirely different families who happen to share the name, and naming them is the only defence against quietly absorbing them.

blocked means a bot check, a login wall or a paywall that this project has chosen not to get round. those are recorded rather than worked around, and where a blocked route matters — antenati for the carnian civil registers is the sharpest case — it is named as a gap rather than filled with a guess. the link still goes to the front door, so anyone with an account can walk through it.
not yet is a shopping list. most of it is printed and purchasable or is one letter away. anyone who wants to move this archive forward should start there rather than at the beginning.
sources that did yield are described properly in the bibliography, with what each gave and where it is weak. open questions are on the open questions page.

/open-questions/.title: Open Questions — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 44 unanswered — 38 open, 6 blocked
what this archive does not know, written down so that a gap is never mistaken for a fact, and so that anybody who can close one can see exactly what it would take.

every one of these has been worked on and none of them has been closed. they are kept in the open because an archive that publishes only its answers is not showing its work — and because more than one of them could be closed in an afternoon by somebody who happens to live in the right town.

blocked means the next step is known and cannot be taken from a desk. 37 other questions have been answered and are kept, with their answers, below. the deaths that ought to exist and cannot be found are below that.
every open question, and what would answer it
the kinds above are the filter. each one carries what is already known and the record that would settle it — a question without that is a regret, not a queue.

1 who was koka, david's grandfather's second wife? open

a spouse node on david's live tree with nothing attached to it — no dates, no places, no children, no maiden name. «koka» is a croatian pet name, not a given name, which is how a person reaches a family tree when somebody remembers her and nobody remembers her papers. ivan anton defranceski, 1925–1995, was divorced from hedviga about 1969 and stayed at senj while she went to africa. he had twenty-six years on his own coast after that, and this is the only trace of what he did with them.
what would settle it

the senj marriage registers after 1969 are with the matični ured and past the end of every film — the same office that holds hedviga's 1926 birth, and the same errand. somebody in the family will also simply know her name.
2 where was this family between senj and johannesburg? open

hedviga immigrated to south africa in april 1975, from zimbabwe. the archive now draws her route as senj → crikvenica → harare → johannesburg: the tree puts rhodesia in the middle of it — in the middle of its war, and two years after a remarriage about 1973 — and david confirmed harare on 2 november 2026, the pin on his own map. his father ivan, 1951–2026, lived in rhodesia from about 1954 to about 1970 on the family's account. still open: how long hedviga was there, whether the children were with her, and whether ivan the elder (1925–1995, whose roster death place is senj) went too — david's map has a line «ivan and hedviga move to zimbabwe». david, who compiles this archive, was born at johannesburg after she arrived.
the family will know this better than any archive. failing that, rhodesian immigration and south african permanent-residence records of 1975, and zimbabwean electoral rolls.
3 antony de franceski's headstone makes him two years older than every document does. which is wrong? open

anton mario de franceski was born at reutlingen on 21 august 1944. four documents say so and they were written in two countries by people who had never met: the reutlingen residence list, the neuhausen list of 19 march 1945, iro identity card 52852, and naa a11534, 58–60 — an australian file of 1948 that names the household as «zdravko dob 2 april 1921; ruza dob 13 february 1922; anton dob 21 august 1944». warrill park lawn cemetery, willowbank, gives his age at death on 28 june 1999 as 56. find a grave has turned that into a birth year of 1943. born on 21 august 1944 he was 54, seven weeks short of fifty-five. that he is the same man is not in doubt. naa d4881 gives his own arrival card as «de franceski anton mario — arrived melbourne per general m b stewart 13 april 1949» — and de franceski, with a space and no c, is the spelling on the willowbank headstone and on his father's at horsham, and on none of the other ninety-four headstones of this surname the archive has read.

the queensland death registration for 1999 is not public — the state releases deaths at thirty years. two cheap tests instead: the ryerson index, free, covering australian death notices for 1999, whose server was down when this was written; and a copy of naa d4881, whose card runs to 31 december 1976 and should carry an address. a funeral notice would also name a wife and children, which this archive has none of.
4 was carlo de franceschi born in 1809 or 1810? open

this site says 17 october 1809, from the gologorica baptism register — house 17, class civilis, parents dominus josephus de franceschi and lambertina née peschle. a register is normally the end of the argument. two contemporary sources say 1810, and they are independent of each other. l'istria, 28 january 1882, reporting a visit to him: «il de franceschi in ottobre conterà gli anni 72» — in october he will be seventy-two. turning 72 in october 1882 means born october 1810. il giovine pensiero, 18 january 1893, his obituary: «nacque a moncalvo (gollogorizza) il 17 ottobre 1810 da famiglia abbastanza agiata» — the same day and month, the other year.

the register still wins on paper, and this archive keeps 1809. but two independent contemporaries — one of them sitting in the room with him — is not nothing, and an obituary usually gets its dates from the family. what would settle it: the register image itself, re-read rather than taken from a transcript, and his own memoirs, which state his age at particular moments. if the register says 1809 and carlo told people 1810 all his life, that is worth knowing about him.
5 did carlo de franceschi sit for rovigno or for pisino in 1848? open

this site says pisino, following the italian scholarship, and records him defeating the proposal to attach istria to the german confederation alongside facchinetti, madonizza, vidulich and vlach. the «journal des österreichischen lloyd» of 7 september 1848, read in full on 14 september 2026, says rovigno — three times, and consistently: «der deputirte von rovigno zum wiener reichstag, carl de franceschi»; then his day job as rathsprotokollist des landrechts zu rovigno; then a direct apostrophe, «rovigno! das ist dein deputierter am reichstage zu wien.» the paper is a hostile witness and that is not nothing — but it was printed in trieste while he was sitting in vienna, and a correspondent writing for istrian readers would be corrected quickly if he named the wrong town.

the printed register of members of the constituent reichstag of 1848 lists every deputy with his constituency and would settle it in a line. the two need not be in conflict: a man could hold a court post at rovigno and be returned for another district. but the lloyd's direct address to rovigno as his town is hard to read that way, and until the register is seen this archive prefers neither.
6 who was count damian de franceschis? open

on 25 march 1720 the provost and vicar of the cathedral of pedena came to gallignana and baptised «bartholomeus filius legitimus domini comitis damiani de franceschis ac ursulae eius coniugis». the whole gallignana baptism book of 1667–1745 has now been read leaf by leaf, and the surname occurs five times in it: this count in 1720; a presbiter philippus de franceschi celebrating a baptism on 19 march 1734; and three times a defranceschi of gologorica standing godparent, in 1733, 1743 and 1744. the count is the only one of the five who is not from gologorica and the only one this archive cannot place at all. the reading was verified against a genuine «defuncti» on the same page. he is in no source this archive holds — not the seget line puhmajer reconstructs, not the gologorica registers, not kobler's three fiume stocks.

the pedena cathedral chapter's records, which would account for the provost's journey; the gologorica and pisino registers for 1720 and after, for a bartholomaeus; and any nobiliary list of the county of pazin. a count of this surname in the habsburg county in the year the candia branch bought seget is not a person who should be untraceable.
7 what is in orbanić's edition of the 1788 pićan visitation? open

ignazio gaetano de buset conducted a spiritual visitation of the diocese of pićan — pedena — and the austrian part of the diocese of poreč between 31 march and 31 august 1788, writing 178 sheets in italian in four small volumes. elvis orbanić edited and published them: «visita spirituale del 1788 in istria», quaderni di «archiva ecclesiae» 13, vatican city, 2016, 277 pp. it records the conduct of the parish priests and curates and the internal state of every church in the diocese, parish by parish. gologorica and gallignana are both in it, and in 1788 gologorica had just come out of eight decades as the bishop of pićan's own fief.

get the book. it is a printed edition, so a library or the associazione archivistica ecclesiastica will do; no archive appointment is needed. note that the manuscripts themselves are in the diocesan archives of trieste, not pazin — which is the detail that would otherwise waste a search. the editor, elvis orbanić, directs the state archives at pazin.
8 when did agostino de franceschi of gorto live? open

the oldest de franceschi stone in the cemetery at santa maria di gorto carries an effaced inscription: «qui giace / agostino de franceschi / nato 2? luglio 18?? / morto 1? settembre 18?? / moglie e [figli] posero». the stone was then reused, and francesco de franceschi 1887–1945 and liduina cecconi 1897–1977 applied over it in metal letters. two separate readings of the same photographs have produced 26 july 1822 and 22 july 1853 for the birth, and 11 and 15 september for the death. neither is safe: the birth day is a 2 followed by a 2 or an 8, the death day a 1 followed by a 1 or a 5, and both years sit inside a blown highlight that no processing recovers.

one photograph of that stone in raking light, early morning or late afternoon, square on. failing that, the ovaro civil death register — carnia was in the kingdom of italy from 1866, so a death in the 1880s is civilly registered — which would also give his age, his parents and his widow's name, and would say whether francesco of 1887 was his posthumous son.
9 where are the udine charters of 1467, 1471 and 1502? open

the istarska enciklopedija says the family held the castle of agrons by the degano, that charters of 1467 and 1471 record the investiture of a leonardus francisci by the luogotenente of friuli with an obligation of military service, and that a document of 1502 names «ser leonardus christoforus francisci quondam johannis gismanus de carnia». these are the oldest documents anywhere that touch this family, and they carry it back four hundred years before the gologorica house. bertoša attributes all three explicitly to the researches of camillo de franceschi — so the citation is camillo's, not his, and the trail runs through camillo before it runs to udine.

three lines at once. first, camillo's «storia documentata della contea di pisino», amsi 1963 vols 10–12, which is the encyclopedia's own cited authority and which this archive does not hold — the footnote there should give the archival reference. second, camillo's working papers, whose inventories both say they include his transcriptions and the documents he used: the società istriana at trieste (26 boxes) and the national and university library at zagreb (14 boxes and 9 folders). letters to both are drafted. third, the originals, presumably in the archivio di stato di udine among the records of the luogotenenza della patria del friuli — the fond and series are being identified.
10 who was the marquis de prié of moncalvo? open

in 1712 a gian battista de franceschi, parish priest of moncalvo, took the peasants' side in a revolt against the taxes of the fief-holder's lieutenant, was arrested and shut in the castle of pazin, and was let out by the lord of moncalvo, «il marchese de prié». a year after the family built its house. and in the same century gologorica was the fief of charles antoine biotz, a belgian of the diocese of liège. two netherlandish lords of one small istrian village within a generation.

that is a fact about how the habsburg court disposed of istrian fiefs, not about this family, and it should be traced through the literature on the county of pazin rather than through parish books. camillo's «storia documentata della contea di pisino» is again the obvious place to start.
11 what is in box 1 at rijeka? open

hr-dari-382, kut. 1: the «albero genealogico della famiglia de franceschi» of 1896 — blue ink on paper, with births and deaths added later in black. puhmajer says it runs «iz vremena koje seže u 15. stoljeće», from a time reaching back into the fifteenth century, down to the 1890s, with dates, occupations and spouses. he prints about a fifth of it in his footnotes and reproduces the rest as a photograph too small to read. the fond's own finding aid is titled 1412 / 1943.

ask the državni arhiv u rijeci for a high-resolution image of the chart itself, not a transcript. then, in order: hr-dapa-828 kut. 3, the 1927 umag genealogy of the male line, as a control; krota's «sumarni inventar ro 23» (1990), the key to the whole fond, which puhmajer used for only fourteen boxes; and hr-dari-382 kut. 13 sv. 50, «instromenti diversi per li luoghi di umago et bugie», the pre-1720 deeds and the likeliest home of anything documenting the arrival in istria.
12 was alvise de franceschi really dragoman at the ottoman porte? open

the 1896 family genealogy enters alvise de franceschi (1727 – c. 1790), owner of seget, as «dragomai alla porta ottomana». a venetian dragomanno alla porta was a salaried interpreter-diplomat attached to the bailo at constantinople — a real office with a real paper trail, and one venice filled from levantine-greek families who had served her in the east. his father had married a crissulla marulli in 1727; marulli is a cretan noble surname and crissulla is chrysoula.

the «bailo a costantinopoli» series in the archivio di stato di venezia, and the senato deliberazioni costantinopoli. if he held the office, he was paid for it and there will be a file. it would also give the candia story its first document, which it has never had.
13 who were the defranceschi of bakar? open

the family remembers a lot of them there, and this archive had not a line about bakar or buccari — twenty kilometres along the same coast this line came down to in 1890, and the seat of an archdeaconry in kobler's own geography. a first sweep gives an ant. defranceschi keeping the accounts of the colapian (kupa) navigation for the royal chamber in the zagreb almanacs of 1824–47, a franciscus defranceschi as chancery clerk beside him, and a francesco defranceschi as inspector of the parish school at fiume in 1859–60. none is yet shown to be a bakar household.

two things. the bakar parish registers, which are a series this project has never touched. and «stemmi della nobiltà di buccari», bakarski zbornik 2 (1996), pp. 5–62 — fifty-seven pages on the arms of bakar's patrician houses. if the name is among them, that article has the shield.
14 who is in the gallignana baptism book of 1668–1745? open

nobody knows, because nobody has read it — and it turns out to be on the family's own hard drive. microfilm zm34k-215, images m01069946 to m01070130, is a liber baptisatorum with a title page of the 1660s and «gracisce» pencilled on the flyleaf, running in sampled pages from 1679 through 1735 and joining onto the 1746–1840 births book that follows it. this log has been calling the pre-1764 books «the only significant undigitised material» and saying they must be read on paper at pazin. one of them was already in the house.

read it. image m01069975 is the opening for the winter of 1679–80 — the exact year of the carnian headmen's return that names zuane de franceschi with a son at work in the imperial county. two hundred images of narrative latin, unindexed, no ocr possible, in the hand of the plebanus jacobus braitta. it is now the single most valuable thing anyone can do for this archive without leaving the house.
15 is the gračišće house-5 head the boy baptised at gologorica casa 31? open

the gallignana status animarum gives the head of house 5 as joan. bapt. defranceschi, agricola, born 13 august 1787. the gologorica baptism book, folio 6, has a joannes baptista defranceschi baptised at house 31 on 13 august 1787, son of joannes baptista and theresia née grach — the casa-31 «detti leonardi» branch. same name, same day, two parishes eight kilometres apart. against it: one record is a birth and the other a baptism; the gologorica household is entered cives and the gračišće man is an agricola. recorded as inferred.

the gračišće marriage of 1819 to francisca salomon, which should name the groom's father, or his death entry of 1 september 1846. either would settle it, and both are in the gračišće registers rather than the gologorica ones.
16 what is in box 2979 at udine? open

the inventory of ovaro sources in the archivio di stato di udine, printed in «ovaro: itinerari e ricerche» (1995), lists the old notarial archive by notarial seat. under «sede notarile: mione» stands b. 2979, franceschi gio. batta — two protocols of instruments 1737–1783 and a minute-book 1757–1783. a notary of this surname held the seat at mione for forty-six years, and everything drawn there in that time went through his hands. two boxes on, b. 2985, soravito franceschi antonio, 1800–1805.

write to the archivio di stato di udine. those are the years in which a valentino defranceschi «venuto dalla carnia» was made a citizen of fiume — 1739 — and the generations carlo says came over. it is the most specific unopened door on the carnian side and it needs a letter, not a search box.
17 is the shield still on the house at gologorica? open

three witnesses now say there is a carved coat of arms on the front of the family's house, across a hundred and forty years: carlo describing his family's arms privately to kobler about 1873; the architectural historian radmila matejčić in 1979 recording «il proprio palazzetto con portico ad arcate e blasone sulla facciata»; and the american branch in 2012 describing what they could still make out on it, «hard to read now due to wear and weather».

answered, the same day. the house stands, with the arcaded loggia matejčić describes. set into the façade: a tablet reading «[a]n.o domini … gio: batista de franceschi fecce fare per se et heredi svoi»; a madonna relief in a scrolled aedicule; a memorial tablet beginning «in questa casa … carlo de franceschi … patriota istriano»; and at the top an oval cartouche under a plumed helm, charged with a cross crossed by two arrows and, below a band, a pomegranate. that is carlo's private blazon of about 1873, exactly. the same arms are on both tablets of his tomb in the village cemetery and on the urn beside it. the carlo plaque is now read in full and it corrects this entry: «in qvesta casa avita / nacqve e morì / carlo de franceschi / patriotta fervente / archeologo e storico / agli stvdi della sva istria / operoso / mdcccix — mdcccxciii» — not «patriota istriano», and it says he was born and died in the house, and calls it the casa avita. the cartouche legend is partly read, by two readers independently: «… [name ending ‑a] · de · franceschi · fieri · … permisit …», latin, running clockwise with the top arc eroded away. the house is number 22. the year on the builder's tablet is now read: «anno · domni · 1711 / gion · batista / de · franceschi / fecce · fare · per · se / et · heredi · svoi» — 1711, exactly the year carlo gave kobler for the building of the house, and the name is gion, not the abbreviation. a mark right of the last numeral was read by one reader as an open-form 4; enlarged, it sits outside the digits' band and against the panel border, and 1711 is published. still wanted: one raking-light frame to close that off for good — no frame yet taken is closer than about six pixels per letter — and the lost segments of the cartouche legend. both want a long lens and a torch swept round at a low angle, four to eight exposures, after sunset.
18 does valentino's chapel above sveti ivan still stand? open

kobler, writing in the 1890s, describes it in the present tense: the chapel of st helena near the western boundary of fiume's territory, a little beyond san giovanni, with «sacellum b. mariæ virgini erectum a d. valentino defranceschi a. 1764» cut over the door. its upkeep passed in 1801 to the faribault family, who had bought his vineyard at plase, and in 1839 celestino faribault guaranteed fourteen masses a year. kobler also lists valentino's floor slab in the collegiate church, by the altar of the madonna del carmine, reading «cineres d. valentini de franceschi, qui vivens sibi ac posteris suis destinavit hanc aeternae quietis sedem».
two photographs: the lintel above sveti ivan, and the slab in the church at rijeka. questions for the rijeka conservation office or the parish. neither needs an archive appointment.
19 is the seghetto tomb still in the cemetery at umago? open

«la ricerca» 42–43 (2004): «subito vicino c'è la tomba dei conti de franceschi di seghetto. anche questa munita di stemma famigliare» — next to the tomb of the counts marcovich, the tomb of the counts de franceschi of seghetto, with the family arms on it.

answered, the same day it was asked, by somebody going and looking. it is not a headstone but a walled enclosure with iron railings, a stone canopy on four columns, a wrought-iron cross and two angels on top, and a black iron tympanum of acanthus filling the arch. at the centre of the ironwork: a shield under a five-pointed coronet, charged with a lion rampant and a star. under the canopy, a marble monument in three bays, a wreath enclosing the date 1890, and the words famiglia de franceschi di seghetto. a tablet against the wall gives francesca d. 1924, rag. giorgio d. 1940 aged 26, ing. italo d. 1944 aged 68, ferramondo d. 1945 aged 74, and anna fragiacomo ved. de franceschi d. 1960 aged 70. the lion is also on the pediment of the house at seget. it is the armorial's second family, not carlo's.
20 what is in the 1885 vodnjan election file at trieste? open

daniela simon's monograph cites a detailed complaint by the croatian party about the rural-communes election in the vodnjan district on 22 may 1885, naming the people involved, and records that «die forderung nach annullierung der wahl von g. b. de franceschi wurde an das abgeordnetenhaus gerichtet» — the demand to annul g. b. de franceschi's election was put to the chamber of deputies. she describes the same season's poll at poreč as involving vote-buying, obstruction and assaults witnessed by the district captain, with the police standing by.

archivio di stato di trieste, i.r. luogotenenza del litorale (1850–1918), atti presidiali, 1891, fascicolo 138: vodnjan, 1 september 1885; the poreč companion is fascicolo 131. ask for a scan. he served the term, so the complaint failed or lapsed; the file would say which.
21 do g. b. de franceschi's umago manuscripts survive? open

rino cigui, editing kandler's «cenni storici di umago» in the «atti» for 2004, notes that kandler was among the first to attempt a systematic history of umago «assieme al canonico francesco roselli ed a giovanni battista de franceschi», and describes him as «cultore di studi storici e autore della raccolta ‹manoscritti inediti relativi alla storia di umago›». the man this archive knows as the leader of the italian majority in the diet and a deputy at vienna for eighteen years also assembled a manuscript collection on his own town.
ask the centro di ricerche storiche at rovinj and the umag town museum whether the raccolta survives and where. if it does, it is a de franceschi archive nobody in this project has looked at.
22 where are the family's own three sources? open

the 2012 reunion album records its own chain of custody. a man who had married into the gallignana house more than fifty years before handed over his handwritten notes of the family tree; a cousin had made a tape of the family genealogy years earlier and passed it round; another cousin had been researching the family in the 1970s. none of the three is in this archive.
ask the american cousins. any one of the three would be worth more than another week in the newspapers, and the tape in particular is oral testimony from a generation now gone.
23 is there a trieste departure manifest anywhere? blocked

trieste was the austro-hungarian emigration port and the austro-americana line sailed from it to new york, and a 1917 draft card even records a gallignana-born man's birthplace as ‘frieste’ — the port standing in for the village. but no trieste outward manifest appears in any collection searched.
the trieste port records are held at the archivio di stato di trieste and are not in the familysearch index. this is the largest remaining gap on the leaving side.
24 what is in the two de franceschi family archives? open

unknown, and they are the largest untouched source in the project. hr-dari-382 at rijeka and hr-dapa-828 at pazin hold the papers of both istrian branches — letters, wills, inventories, accounts, and two made genealogies, one of about 1896 and one of 1927. a monograph has quoted from them, so they are accessible to researchers.
write to both archives. the 1896 tree at rijeka gives births, deaths and marriages for every member and would likely close several questions on this log at once.
25 how does the gračišće stonemason join the gologorica gentry? open

half answered, from the wrong end. antonius the «lapicida» is now traced back two further generations from the gračišće book of souls: he was born 20 september 1825 in house 19, son of joan. bapt. defranceschi of house 5, an «agricola» born 13 august 1787 — a farmer, not gentry either. the gračišće line is a working line for at least three generations before the stonecutter. what still has no record is any join between that line and the dominus house at gologorica, two villages away.

the 1787 birth is now the end of the documented chain, and the next request to pazin should be the gračišće baptisms of the 1780s for joan. battista, which would name his father — the giovanni of 1750–1829 the family chart carries but nothing yet proves.
26 whose children did carlo de franceschi bury? open

the burial registers of rovinj and poreč hold four entries naming the father only as «caroli» or «carlo de franceschi»: julius at rovinj in february 1854; lamberta and aurelia augusta at poreč within weeks of each other in july 1867; virginia at poreč in august 1876, aged eighteen. rovinj and poreč are the two towns carlo worked in, the dates fall inside his married life, and lamberta is his own mother's name — lambertina peschle of volosca. camillo, born at poreč thirteen months after the two infant burials, is described in the literature as the youngest of carlo's four children. four is the number who lived.
ask pazin for the poreč and rovinj death registers by name and year, and for carlo's own marriage — which would give his wife's name, still missing from this archive.
27 whose is the ližnjan family, and what happened there in 1846? open

ten burials at ližnjan in southern istria, and the register keeps returning to children: giovanni born 1845 and dead in november 1846, maria born and dead in 1846, antonio the same year. across europe those are the hunger years — blight in 1845, a failed grain harvest in 1846, typhus behind it. the ližnjan defranceschi are accounted for by no line in this archive.
ližnjan's baptism and marriage registers, to reconstruct the household behind those burials. the in-law surnames already visible are skifich, skoko, vojnić and primus.
28 where are the gologorica marriages of 1790–1849? blocked

missing from both microfilm volumes. the books run to 1789 and the next gologorica marriage register in the archive index starts only in the 1850s. that gap swallows the two marriages this line most needs: leonardus and matthea on 23 november 1790, and josephus and lambertina peschle on 3 february 1807 — the record that would name lambertina's father.
the 1790–1849 marriage register has to be found in other pazin or diocesan microfilm, or the marriages were recorded in the brides' home parishes.
29 where is giuseppe's baptism? blocked

searched, and it is not in the rijeka index. valentino and elena's fourteen children are now recovered from that register, baptised between 1737 and 1757 — josepha catharina, matheus franciscus, nicolaus francus, mattio, nicolo, francisca joanna theresia, ignatius francus mattheus, vitus joannes baptista, aloysius joannes petrus, antonio, aloysius rochus, rosalia francisca, aloysia, maria. there is no giuseppe among them. but giuseppe named sons valentino twice, in 1772 and again in 1776, and by the italian custom the first son carries the paternal grandfather's name. the likeliest reading is that giuseppe was born before his father reached fiume — which puts his baptism in carnia, in the ovaro registers that are this project's other dead end.

two routes. the ovaro parish books before 1806, which are in no portal and must be asked for at the parish. or the three-quarters of the rijeka register that is photographed but not name-indexed, which has to be read image by image.
30 is zuane de franceschi of mione an ancestor of the gologorica family? open

the 1679 headmen's list names him with a son, working as a weaver ‘nell'istria, luogo imperiale’ — the habsburg county of pazin, which is exactly where gologorica and gračišće are. thirty-two years later the de franceschi house goes up on the gologorica square; sixty-one years later giovanni battista leaves that county for fiume. the route is documented. the descent is not.

gologorica baptisms and marriages 1644–1763, and the gračišće series from 1667, looking for a zuane or giovanni arriving from friuli in the 1680s or 1690s. the gologorica books for those years are the undigitised ones.
31 are the valentino and giovanni battista lines one family? open

half answered. carlo claims giovanni battista outright as his own kin. on valentino he is careful: the fiume port captain francesco descended from him, valentino came to fiume «direttamente dalla carnia», and francesco confirmed the carnian origin — so the branch «potrebbe essere stato congiunto del mio trisavolo nato in carnia», might have been connected to my great-great-grandfather, born in carnia. two carnian families of one surname in one port; carlo would not go further and neither should this.
y-dna would settle it in weeks. otherwise the ovaro parish registers, where both would have been baptised before they left.
32 who are the twelve defranceschi families of vodnjan? open

found in the 1945 cadastre: twelve families at vodnjan against two at gologorica and one at gračišće — the largest concentration in istria, and accounted for by no line in the existing family narrative. vodnjan's registers are exceptionally deep: 133 books, baptisms from 1559, 118 digitised.
read the vodnjan baptisms. the most tractable open question in the archive — the books are catalogued and nearly all digitised.
33 are there any documented de franceschi in carnia at all? open

yes — twelve of them, found by searching the italian indexes by place rather than by name. at paluzza in the val bût: zuanne de franceschi and maria delli zotti; their son daniele born 1782, who married maria silverio; francesco and domenica englaro with sons born 1807 and 1810; francesco and cattarina delli zotti; daniele and maria pittino, whose son pietro born 1851 is the mason who died at san daniele del friuli in 1895 — the death certificate that has been in this family's folder all along, now identified. at ovaro, the parish that contains mione: sebastiano soravito de franceschi and giacoma gortani, and a battista born 1879. and monsignor lucio soravito de franceschi was born at mione di ovaro on 8 december 1939 — the surname still in the village two hundred and sixty years after the headmen's list put it there.

and then the village itself. the archivio di stato di udine has digitised fifty-nine napoleonic civil registers for the comune di mione and publishes them on antenati. the birth index for 1806-1810 opens on three de franceschi entries, and the acts name three households: osvaldo and appolonia galante, farmers of muina; francesco, a tailor, and margherita gortan of mione; and osvaldo, a carpenter, and cattarina brencis, whose son born 15 october 1810 was named giovanni battista. a tailor is exactly the cramar trade that walked the road of the furlans into istria. next, and this is now the single most valuable thing available to the project: the same series holds nine volumes of matrimoni and thirteen of matrimoni allegati for mione. napoleonic marriage allegati contain birth extracts for the couple and death extracts for their parents. one de franceschi marriage at mione between 1806 and 1815 would reach back to the middle of the eighteenth century. done, and it did. the marriage index for 1806-1810 holds two: osvaldo defranceschi with valentina prencis at mione on 6 august 1807, and osvaldo defranceschi with appolonia galante at muina on 28 january 1808. the second act reads the groom's birth certificate into the record: born 14 march 1788 at muina, of the lawful marriage of antonio qm. leonardo de franceschi and maria nata corva, with antonio's written consent dated 25 october 1807. four generations at muina, the earliest a leonardo dead before 1808. the 1807 act is not yet located.
34 who was josip's wife? open

ana kalanj, by four register entries — the baptisms of 1890, 1892, 1894 and 1896 all name her, and the 1905 burial of their daughter writes her ana kalaj-kučarica with the house-name. her own baptism survives at ledenice: 3 january 1864, daughter of josip kalanj and rosalia née perković, at klenovica house 22. but the family's own genealogy file gives josip a wife ana grubišić, born 19 september 1863 and died 28 may 1936, and holds a photograph of her gravestone reading ana de. franceschi. two different birth dates, nine months apart, and two different maiden names.
the crikvenica death register for 28 may 1936, and the marriage register. either josip married twice, or the gravestone belongs to a different ana de franceschi in the same parish.
35 which carnian family is valentino's, exactly? open

mione is no longer a guess — a de franceschi of mione is on the 1679 list. but nothing yet ties valentino, made a citizen of fiume in 1739, to that household rather than to any other carnian family of the name.

ovaro's parish registers before 1806 are in no portal. contact the parish; check the archivio storico diocesano at udine for duplicates. separately, the micoli toscano family archive at mione holds gorto contracts naming the erman, who travelled with zuane in 1679.
36 are the dalmatian franceschi related to us at all? open

almost certainly not. they reached dalmatia in the fourteenth century as a noble house, held a warship at omiš by 1590, and won the perinuša estate for storming imotski in 1717. ours were weavers and modest landowners. but the existing family account lists omiš and imotski among its four directions, so the claim is in the family's own memory and has to be tested rather than waved away.
y-dna again, which would settle it in weeks. otherwise omiš and imotski parish registers, held by the state archives in split, not pazin.
37 what is in the six oldest gologorica books? blocked

baptisms 1644–1763, marriages 1656–1781 and burials 1646–1777 are the only significant undigitised material in the istrian parishes — and they are now the highest-value target in the project, because they cover both the 1679 arrival window and giovanni battista's birth.
they must be read on paper, in the village or the pazin reading room. the archive states it will not do this for you.
38 what survives, parish by parish, for senj and crikvenica? blocked

the fond is identified — hr-dari-275, 1,822 books, 1564 to 1949, forty linear metres — but only partially filmed, only partially public, and with no parish-level inventory published. six books came from the senj registry office in march 2018 and sit at the senj collection centre.
arhinet, the national catalogue that would carry the item list, failed to resolve on every attempt. write to the rijeka archive directly.
39 where do the south african defranceski come from? blocked
thirteen of the seventeen people spelling it this way live in south africa. nothing on the open web connects a named individual to a named ship or year.
south african naturalisation and immigration records. several thousand italian former internees settled there at the end of the 1940s, which fits the date and direction — context, not evidence.
40 is there anything carved on the 1711 house? open
istrian lintels frequently carry a date with a house mark or arms. the de franceschi house stands on the main square at gologorica.
a photograph. anybody visiting can close this one.
41 who was «riccardo b———», who married angelina defranceschi at pola in 1914? open

il giornaletto di pola of 21 november 1914 carries a boxed announcement the couple paid to place: «angelina defranceschi [&] riccardo b———e partecipano il loro matrimonio. pola, 21 novembre 1914.» the paper set these announcements in ornamental swash capitals, which is exactly what anno's ocr cannot read: the groom's name comes out «criecardo jbeace». the initial c and j are the decorative ligatures either side of an ampersand, so the reading is riccardo b—e — four or five letters, beginning b, ending e. the notice ran once. the issues of 20, 22, 23 and 24 november do not repeat it, so there is no second setting to check the name against.

the page image. anno holds the scan; the announcement is a display box and will be legible at full resolution where the ocr is not. the issue. the pola marriage register for november 1914 would give both names outright, and would say who angelina's parents were — which is the fact that would attach her to a line.
42 is the angelo defranceschi of via del prato the angelo born 1851 to natale defranceschi and domenica chersin? open

il giornaletto of 25 november 1914 reports «angelo defranceschi d'anni 63, da fasana», living at no. 6 via del prato, pola, taken to the provincial hospital with his left hand torn open. sixty-three in november 1914 means born about 1851. this archive holds an angelo defranceschi born 1851, son of natale defranceschi and domenica chersin, filed at pola — and, separately, an angelo defranceschi of fasana, born 1815, a generation earlier. same name, same birth year, same town, and the village of origin the newspaper supplies is the one the other fasana entry names.

a document that joins them. the pola burial register would give his age and his village at death; the fažana baptism book for 1851 would give his parents. fažana's books have already returned forty-two records of the name between 1770 and 1855, so this is a page-turn, not a search. until then it is an inference and is labelled one.
43 who was pietro de franceschi of mione, and is he the pietro of the 1806 household list? open

felice santo's baptismal extract of 2 november 1792 names his father as «pauli filii petri de franceschi mionensis» — paolo, son of pietro. that is the oldest de franceschi this archive can name out of mione, and it comes from the pieve di gorto's own register, certified at luincis in 1815. the 1806 mione household list already holds a «pietro q.m matteo × maddalena fedeli». if that is the same man, the line reaches back another generation to a matteo, and 1792 minus a plausible age puts pietro's own birth in the 1730s or 1740s.

the pieve di gorto baptismal register for roughly 1750–1770, which would give paolo's own baptism and name his father outright. failing that, mione's morti 1806–1815 — nine volumes, all of them on antenati and none of them read — where a pietro de franceschi dying in his seventies would settle it. do not merge the two pietros on the name alone. mione had several de franceschi households and this archive has already been caught once merging two men called ivan.
44 where is the mione marriage register for 1807? open

1807 is absent from every mione series — marriages, banns, allegati, deaths, births — in the archivio di stato di udine's inventory, checked ark by ark. but the year was registered. mione's own marriage index for 1806–1810 carries «prencis valentina con defranceschi osualdo — di mione — 6 agosto 1807». and ovaro, the next comune up the valley, has its 1807 marriages (ark an_ua679983) with no gap at all. so the system did not fail in 1807. one mione volume is missing.

ask the archivio di stato di udine directly whether the 1807 mione volume survives undigitised, was lost, or was never deposited. cheaper first step: the ovaro 1807 allegati (an_ua679993) are online and unread, and a mione couple's papers could be filed there.
45 is daniele «del fu osvaldo» de canova the bride's brother? open

at the ovaro wedding of 15 june 1815, daniele del fu osvaldo de canova, 49, possidente of liariis, stands as a witness to the marriage of lucia santa, daughter of the late osvaldo antonio de canova — and the act declares all four witnesses «non parenti, né affini». her baptismal extract of 12 may 1793 confirms her father as «s.r egregio osvaldo antonio de caneva», husband of lucia colinassio. daniele, aged 49 in 1815, was born about 1766 — twenty-seven years before her, which a brother could be but a father could not.

either two men called osvaldo at liariis, or the «non parenti» formula is boilerplate. the pieve di gorto baptisms for the 1760s would say whose son daniele was. the de caneva of liariis are well recorded — a gio: batta de caneva stood godfather in 1793 and a jacoba, widow of nicolaus de caneva, in 1769.
46 was paolo de franceschi a carpenter or a landowner? open

two documents eleven days apart give different answers. the consent act of 14 june 1815 calls him «il vivente paolo de franceschi possidente domiciliato nella frazion di mione». the marriage act of 15 june 1815 calls him «paolo de franceschi di professione falegname». his son is a tessitore in one act and a sartore in another. the same fortnight, the same notary's office, the same family.

probably nothing to resolve: possidente is a statement of standing and falegname of trade, and a man can be both. it is recorded because this archive has leaned on trades as evidence — the weaver finding, the tailor argument — and this is the clearest demonstration that a single act's trade word is soft.
47 are the two osvaldo de' franceschi of mione grandfather and grandson? open

osvaldo the elder — son of the late gio: batta, married to a cattarina, father of giacoma born 25 may 1789, dead before september 1806. osvaldo «fa legname» — a carpenter, twenty-six in october 1810 so born about 1784, married to a cattarina (prences, in her six spellings), father of gio: batta born 1810, alive and signing his own name through 1815. they cannot be the same man. but the younger one is named osvaldo, his son is named gio: batta, and the elder one's father was gio: batta — which is exactly what a carnian naming pattern does across three generations.

the pieve di gorto baptisms for about 1784 would name the carpenter's father outright and settle it in one line. failing that, mione's «morti» 1806 — the elder osvaldo died between giacoma's baptism and her wedding, and if it was in 1806 the act is on antenati and unread. until then they are two men. this archive has merged two men on a shared name before and does not intend to do it again.
nothing at that state.
answered, and still on the list 3
answered but not yet folded back into the pages they affect. they stay here until they are.
is the shield still on the house at gologorica?

next: answered, the same day. the house stands, with the arcaded loggia matejčić describes. set into the façade: a tablet reading «[a]n.o domini … gio: batista de franceschi fecce fare per se et heredi svoi»; a madonna relief in a scrolled aedicule; a memorial tablet beginning «in questa casa … carlo de franceschi … patriota istriano»; and at the top an oval cartouche under a plumed helm, charged with a cross crossed by two arrows and, below a band, a pomegranate. that is carlo's private blazon of about 1873, exactly. the same arms are on both tablets of his tomb in the village cemetery and on the urn beside it. the carlo plaque is now read in full and it corrects this entry: «in qvesta casa avita / nacqve e morì / carlo de franceschi / patriotta fervente / archeologo e storico / agli stvdi della sva istria / operoso / mdcccix — mdcccxciii» — not «patriota istriano», and it says he was born and died in the house, and calls it the casa avita. the cartouche legend is partly read, by two readers independently: «… [name ending ‑a] · de · franceschi · fieri · … permisit …», latin, running clockwise with the top arc eroded away. the house is number 22. the year on the builder's tablet is now read: «anno · domni · 1711 / gion · batista / de · franceschi / fecce · fare · per · se / et · heredi · svoi» — 1711, exactly the year carlo gave kobler for the building of the house, and the name is gion, not the abbreviation. a mark right of the last numeral was read by one reader as an open-form 4; enlarged, it sits outside the digits' band and against the panel border, and 1711 is published. still wanted: one raking-light frame to close that off for good — no frame yet taken is closer than about six pixels per letter — and the lost segments of the cartouche legend. both want a long lens and a torch swept round at a low angle, four to eight exposures, after sunset.
is the seghetto tomb still in the cemetery at umago?

next: answered, the same day it was asked, by somebody going and looking. it is not a headstone but a walled enclosure with iron railings, a stone canopy on four columns, a wrought-iron cross and two angels on top, and a black iron tympanum of acanthus filling the arch. at the centre of the ironwork: a shield under a five-pointed coronet, charged with a lion rampant and a star. under the canopy, a marble monument in three bays, a wreath enclosing the date 1890, and the words famiglia de franceschi di seghetto. a tablet against the wall gives francesca d. 1924, rag. giorgio d. 1940 aged 26, ing. italo d. 1944 aged 68, ferramondo d. 1945 aged 74, and anna fragiacomo ved. de franceschi d. 1960 aged 70. the lion is also on the pediment of the house at seget. it is the armorial's second family, not carlo's.
are there any documented de franceschi in carnia at all?

next: and then the village itself. the archivio di stato di udine has digitised fifty-nine napoleonic civil registers for the comune di mione and publishes them on antenati. the birth index for 1806-1810 opens on three de franceschi entries, and the acts name three households: osvaldo and appolonia galante, farmers of muina; francesco, a tailor, and margherita gortan of mione; and osvaldo, a carpenter, and cattarina brencis, whose son born 15 october 1810 was named giovanni battista. a tailor is exactly the cramar trade that walked the road of the furlans into istria. next, and this is now the single most valuable thing available to the project: the same series holds nine volumes of matrimoni and thirteen of matrimoni allegati for mione. napoleonic marriage allegati contain birth extracts for the couple and death extracts for their parents. one de franceschi marriage at mione between 1806 and 1815 would reach back to the middle of the eighteenth century. done, and it did. the marriage index for 1806-1810 holds two: osvaldo defranceschi with valentina prencis at mione on 6 august 1807, and osvaldo defranceschi with appolonia galante at muina on 28 january 1808. the second act reads the groom's birth certificate into the record: born 14 march 1788 at muina, of the lawful marriage of antonio qm. leonardo de franceschi and maria nata corva, with antonio's written consent dated 25 october 1807. four generations at muina, the earliest a leonardo dead before 1808. the 1807 act is not yet located.
closed in this round 37
answered questions are kept, with their answers, so a question cannot be closed in one place and left open in another.

is there any documented link between mione and istria? yes, and a named one. the 1679 list drawn up by the merighi records, from mione, ‘zuane de franceschi con un suo fiolo, zuane d’erman: questi tre nell’istria, luogo imperiale’ — in the habsburg county of pazin, not venetian istria.

how old is the carnia–istria road? older than the family. in january 1511 a man of the canale di gorto bought a share in a weaving shop at motovun; a luincis man dictated his will at pićan in 1540. documents are rare in the 1500s, dense in the 1600s, very dense in the 1700s.

how far back does the dalmatian line go? on its own family chart, to a niccolò of 1318 recorded as an envoy of pope urban v — twenty generations. four hold zadar offices in the 1400s and 1500s: a notary, the municipal archivist, an officer of the port salt-house. the chart survives contact with independent sources at six points, including gasparo the admiral (1562–1609) and giovanni il zuane (1673–1741), and two 19th-century almissa households that this archive had already rebuilt from the familysearch index.

why was the hero of imotski called «perinović ive»? because the by-name was already his family's. the imotski monograph derives perinuša from a perinović family of zadar brought in as stewards, but the omiš family chart shows a pietro antonio «detto perini», 1588–1661, in the direct line three generations above him.
who is ‘the lot near split’? the omiš and imotski family — and they spell it franceschi, not defranceschi. about 60 in croatia, 25 of them in split, fewer than five at imotski.
why did the dalmatian branch lose its prefix? by decree of the napoleonic administration, which abolished nobiliary particles. not drift and not a clerk’s ear: law.

which archive holds the gologorica and gračišće registers? not pićan. both are full parishes keeping their own books, split between the parish offices, the diocesan archive at poreč, the state archives in pazin, and the pazin civil registry office.
do the registers reach back far enough to matter? yes. gologorica baptisms open in 1644, gračišće in 1667, pazin in 1582, svetvinčenat in 1568 and vodnjan in 1559.
was the surname still in the ancestral villages in 1945? yes. two defranceschi families at gologorica and one at gračišće on 1 october 1945.

is the fused spelling meaningful or just noise? partly, and less than first claimed. the fused form is used on both sides of the pre-1797 border, including by 17 of the 19 families in formerly venetian territory. only the spaced form is one-directional: it appears at seghetto and svetvinčenat and nowhere in the habsburg interior. the first draft of this archive overstated it; corrected here.

can the households be linked into descent? partly. one lineage of three generations and five households survives the tests, at rijeka: giuseppe defranceschi and francesca (children 1772–78); their son valentinus franciscus xaverius, born 22 november 1772, with ursula (eight children 1794–1805); and three of his sons heading households from 1822. four further links were too ambiguous to draw.

have all istrian towns been searched in the name index? in one sense yes and in another no. the index has no place filter at all — only surname, country and collection — so a surname sweep covers every town at once rather than town by town. but it stops returning new results past about 1,100 per query, and eight spelling windows now return almost nothing new: the last two added 19 records out of 732. roughly 964 genuine croatian records are in hand against an index that reports 3,652 fuzzy hits. the remainder is not reachable through this interface.

how much of the croatian church books is actually searchable? a quarter. familysearch reports collection 2040054 as 0.24 complete for indexing, so three-quarters of the croatian parish registers that have been photographed cannot be found by typing a name. everything the index has given this archive comes from that quarter.

did the gologorica family come from carnia? yes, and they said so themselves. carlo de franceschi wrote to giovanni kobler about 1873: «anche i miei derivano dalla carnia, ma si stabilirono in istria intorno al 1700» — mine too derive from carnia, but settled in istria around 1700. he adds that there were still de franceschi at mione and muina in carnia in his own day. the 1679 headmen's list, which he never saw, had already put a zuane de franceschi of mione at work in the county of pazin.

who built the 1711 house at gologorica? carlo's great-great-grandfather, «giambattista del fu leonardo». carlo read the inscription himself. the register agrees on the name: a godparent entry of 1769 records a «joannes baptista defranceschi filius leonardi», which is where the casa-31 branch takes its byname «detti leonardi».

is giovanni battista of fiume part of this family? carlo says yes, without qualification: «quel giovanni batt. de franceschi venuto dalla contea di pisino, come ella dice, intorno al 1740 è senz'altro proveniente dalla mia famiglia.» he was the younger of two sons, meant for the priesthood, who volunteered into maria theresa's army instead, was made castellan of bribir, and married a d'agnese. the received account has always filed him as an unrelated line.

why is the surname sometimes fused? austrian officialdom. carlo: the authorities took the italian «de» for a claim of nobility, not knowing it expresses the house, so their decrees wrote defranceschi — and some of the family signed it that way rather than risk the fine for arrogating a title they could not prove, while others kept de franceschi and a few went to plain franceschi. this archive had argued it from the pattern of the records; here it is from someone it was done to.

does this family have a coat of arms? yes — and none of the ones sold under the surname. carlo blazons it himself: a greek cross crossed by two arrows in the upper field, a pomegranate in the lower, a plumed helm above the shield. he gives no tinctures, and admits he does not know whether the other branches still kept it.

is there a second istrian branch? yes, and published scholarship says so directly. petar puhmajer's 2019 monograph on the seget estate near umag states that the family had two branches in istria — one seated at gologorica, the other at umag and seget — and that family archives survive from both. the umag branch fled crete after the candian war of 1669 and bought seget from the venier in 1720.

do family archives survive anywhere? two, both catalogued. hr-dari-382 at the state archive in rijeka holds letters, contracts, wills, inventories and accounts across several centuries, including an «albero genealogico della famiglia de franceschi» of about 1896 giving every member with dates. hr-dapa-828 at pazin holds an «albero genealogico dei signori de franceschi, umago» of 1927 for the male line, and a notebook of copied family letters from about 1830. neither has been read.

what is the earliest mention of gologorica? 1102, and carlo de franceschi wrote it himself. in «l'istria: note storiche» he lists «golgoriza (moncalvo)» among the first slavic place-names to appear in istrian diplomas — the earliest documented mention of his own birthplace, recorded as evidence of slavic settlement by the man who spent his life arguing for istria's italian character.

will the pazin archive actually supply a record? yes, for a specific request. they state publicly that staff do not undertake extensive genealogical research, and this archive reported that as a wall. but given a name, a place and a period, they searched the gračišće birth register, certified the copy and posted it to queensland for 117 kuna. the refusal is of open-ended research, not of a named request.

is there a gračišće record in hand? yes. josephus defranceschi, born 22 march 1863 and baptised the next day at gračišće, son of antonius defranceschi, «lapidarius» — a stonemason — and maria. certified from mkr gračišće 1841–1899, folio 108, entry 23. a marginal note was added by the civil registry in 1951, so the same person is traceable forward.

are the gologorica registers reachable at all? yes — but not through familysearch. david holds microfilm of them from the pazin records office: two volumes, zm34k-214 and zm34k-215, 1,463 page images covering gologorica, gračišće and cerovlje — not lindar, which is on zm34k-219 and 220; every frame was located against the films’ own title cards on 30 september 2026, and the frame map gives the thirteen books. baptisms, marriages, deaths, confirmations and household censuses. the archive's gologorica line is built from these pages, read one by one.

who were carlo de franceschi's parents and grandparents? carolus josephus defranceschi, born 17 october 1809, second of ten children of dominus josephus de franceschi and lambertina née peschle, married 3 february 1807, house 17, class civilis. his brother's 1808 baptism names the father as son of the late josephus, joining the household to dominus josephus defranceschi, b. c.1722 d.1782, and his wife helena.

where was lambertina peschle from? volosca, as every printed biography says — and the word is written on her own row in the 1826 gologorica census. she died 16 july 1863, aged 76. her father's name would be in the 1807 marriage record, which is in the register gap.

do gologorica and gračišće have images, even without a catalogue entry? no. walking the image waypoints for all 1,000 roman catholic parishes in the collection confirms it a second way: gologorica, gračišće, pićan, cerovlje, vodnjan, motovun and lindar have no images either. but their neighbours do — pazin, stari pazin, lupoglav, tinjan, kringa, boljun, sveti petar u šumi, polje čepić and kršan are all open.
has the familysearch catalogue been swept systematically? yes — 75 places across istria, kvarner, carnia, dalmatia and their neighbours, by place-authority id. 189 items across 61 places.

does familysearch hold anything for gologorica or gračišće? no. nothing at all, and nothing for pićan, cerovlje, motovun, lindar, čepić or mione either. the central istrian interior was never filmed. for this family's own villages there is no remote route — only pazin and the parish offices.

are the twelve vodnjan families in the name index? no. not one vodnjan or dignano record appears among 945 indexed croatian entries, though the parish itself has 133 books at pazin going back to 1559. vodnjan is film-and-archive rich and index-poor.
how many spellings are there worldwide? thirteen with living bearers. several have exactly one.

are the trentino defranceschi our family? no. the austrian index gives 16 records from bozen and salorno, back to a bartholomaeus de franceschi and lucia de gregorys whose children were born 1645–1651. they married kohl, kassler, knoll, pachmann, moser, angerer, perini, trentini, tabarelli — german-tyrolean and trentino names with no overlap at all with the istrian in-law world. same patronymic, same austrian habit of fusing the prefix, two unrelated families.

what are the franceschinis of klagenfurt? almost certainly carnian emigrants who went north rather than south. the -is ending is friulian, carinthia borders friuli, and vittorio franceschinis and margaretha bierlotter baptised five children at klagenfurt between 1900 and 1909.

what is ‘vitipolis’, which 178 records name? rijeka. it is the latin for the city of saint vitus — the town's patron and its cathedral — and the same thing the german sankt veit am flaum says. adding it to fiume and rijeka makes 447 records: the largest cluster of this family in croatia.

do senj and crikvenica survive on film? yes. familysearch holds župa senj 1734–1920, sv. juraj kod senja 1695–1868, crikvenica 1798–1908 and bakar 1692–1891, all filmed from the croatian state archives in zagreb.

can the dalmatian family's earliest claim be tested? yes. omiš parish registers run from 1588 on film, two years before gaspar de franceschi appears there in 1590. imotski has podjezerja 1693–1733, spanning the siege, and imotski-glavina from 1731.

are ovaro's parish books online anywhere? no. familysearch holds only the napoleonic civil registration for ovaro's frazioni, mione included. the church registers before 1806 are not filmed and not in any portal.
the deaths that ought to exist and cannot be found

every person below was read off a register page by eye — they exist in no index anywhere — and every one of them is unfinished. the archive can say when they were alive and who their father was, and cannot say when they died.
this page exists because the alternative is worse: a site that lists 1,058 people and quietly lets the reader assume they are equally well known. they are not.

most of these are findable. they died in a book this archive has open — the vodnjan liber defunctorum, film 005497894, images 471 to 575 — and about a third of it has been read. the rest is time, not luck.

one roll holds the baptisms of all five of anton rudolf and ursula's children — josip petar 1911, petar vid 1913, anka nera 1915, zdravko 1921 and ivan anton 1925 — and this archive has not one of them.

familysearch's crikvenica films stop at rođeni 1896, cut at the hundred-year line as it stood when they were made, so every one of those five births falls after the end of the only collection the archive can reach for free. the supplementary collection does not stop there. this is the single most overdue book in the archive: five baptisms, one reel, and the parents named on every one of them.

the archive already wanted two other books from the same collection — the twentieth-century status animarum (zm-34j/251, m-5976), which is a household census that would give the whole family on one page, and marriages 1909–1947 (the same zm-34j/362). all three should go in one request.

errands 35, 36 and 37 are three separate asks to the same office. they were drafted separately because they were found separately; they should not be posted separately. this row is the single letter that carries all three, and it is the one to send.

⭐ why now. as of 11 october 2026 the family's two reels are read end to end — the gologorica baptisms, its deaths, all four status animarum, cerovlje and both gračišće baptism books. there is nothing substantial left on them. everything the archive now wants is off-reel, and it is all held at pazin.
what the letter would settle, in one line each:
zm34k-216 the baptisms of joanna (1818) and francisca (1819), the two defranceschi brides out of gračišće houses 4 and 5 — and whether they were cousins
vol. iv the last open death-year collision (antonio, 1913 against 1918) and eight deaths this archive has only from a census clerk's note
zm34k-217 house 4 — the one of the two intermarrying gračišće houses this archive cannot see
⚠ it also says what is not wanted, which keeps an archivist from hunting a ghost: an aloysius defranceschi dying 25 november 1870 does not exist — that date is his wedding.

⚠ a partial substitute for part 2 has since turned up — the 1894 book carries an «extrema unctio» register for 1907–1909 — but it covers three years of a thirty-seven-year gap and holds no defranceschi, so the request stands.

⭐⭐⭐ 11 october 2026 — a fourth request, and it may be the most valuable of them. looking for one woman's father, this archive checked where the gologorica marriage register is. the two reels hold exactly one, inside the composite at m01068953–m01069007: «notatio personarum matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ julij 1770», running to february 1788. there is no gologorica marriage register after february 1788 on either reel — a hundred and thirty years of marriages off-film, and this archive had not recorded the gap.

⚠ it is not abstract. nearly every marriage date found this week came from a matrimonii column in a census, never from a marriage entry — aloysius × joanna 1870, franciscus × clotilda 1859, leonardus 1871 and 1883, ruža's three, beatrix 1887, clotildis adelaidis 1890, rosalia × bubić 1869. a census gives the date of a marriage; a marriage entry gives the parents of both parties. that is what this archive keeps running out of.

⚠ 11 october, later — a partial substitute exists for requests 2 and 4 both, and it argues for the letter rather than against it. the baptism register's margins carry death crosses running to 1954 and «extr. za ženidbu» notes dating marriage certificates. they are annotations, not entries: a death cross gives a date and no cause, age, house or officiant; a marriage extract dates the certificate, not the wedding, and names neither spouse. they are enough to show what the missing books would hold, and not enough to replace them.

in english, so the letter can be checked before it goes. it says: the family already holds and has read microfilms zm34k-214 and zm34k-215, and asks for three things. (1) the continuation of the gračišće baptism register after may 1808, which should be on zm34k-216, frames m01070239–m01070310, naming five entries wanted by date and house. (2) the gologorica death register that follows signatura 5.2 — «vol. iv», named on the last page of its predecessor — with its shelf mark, whether it is filmed in the zm34k series, and eight named deaths from 1880 onward. (3) the status animarum pages for gračišće house 4 from zm34k-217, the reel that supplied frame m01072071 (house 5) in june 2021. (4) the gologorica marriage register for the years after february 1788, where the filmed one stops — its shelf mark and whether it is filmed in the zm34k series. it closes by asking the price, the method of payment and whether a form is required, and states the research is non-commercial.

državni arhiv u rijeci — the trsat parish death register 1803–1815
trsat parish death register 1803–1815 (familysearch has 9r2f-znp to 1803 and 9r2f-zng from nov 1815, nothing between) · bakar deaths 9r28-dpv, aug–dec 1808, already read: nil

answered 6 november 2026 by the rijeka state archives (doc for what they say; letter klasa 611-03/26-42/2184, urbroj 126-02-01/1-26-2, signed by the head, markus leideck; it reached david's e-mail on 9 november): the archive «carried out the research» and found that in the death register of the parish of st george, trsat, no death of the said josip defranceschi, parish priest at draga, is entered for 1803–1815. it holds digital copies of that book and does not know where the original is kept. the trsat friary had said on 5 november that the parish holds only post-war books. what this is and is not: a statement by the archive, giving no spellings tried, no pages and no entry numbers, so it is their nil, not one walked here (the digital copy has not been read by this archive); and a priest of draga may be entered under another form of the name or under his office alone. his burial is therefore still not found: not bakar (august–december 1808, read), not trsat (per the archive), not draga (no death book before 1815).

josephus (josip) defranceschi, parish priest of draga 1798–1808, has no burial. every draga book on familysearch has been read for him (births, marriages, deaths, 4 november 2026) and none holds it. what is documented (doc): he writes the draga baptism book until 13 september 1808; on 29 september 1808 a trsat franciscan marries a couple «de licentia m.r.d. parochi dragensis, qui actu infirmitate … josephi defranceschi» with the foot note «ob impotentiam dni parochi»; and his successor xanich calls him «mei praedecessoris parochi defuncti» in 1827. so he died in the last days of september 1808 (inf). the draga dead were buried at trsat and bakar (no cemetery at draga until 30 september 1855). bakar, august–december 1808, is nil. trsat's death book is on familysearch for 1737–1803 and from november 1815, but not for 1803–1815: that gap is the question.

this is a follow-up to errand 4, which asked this office about hr-dari-254 and hr-dari-382 and has no reply recorded. if that letter is still waiting, send this one as its second paragraph rather than as a second envelope. the franciscan letter, errand 40, asks the same question of the convent; the book may be at either.

the burial of josephus defranceschi, september 1808 — and the franciscans who served draga in his illness
franjevački samostan majke božje trsatske, trsat (rijeka) — the convent's own books
the trsat franciscans' parish death book 1803–1815, or the convent's own register of burials and services · fr ruffinus czohar and fr hyacinthus rigetti, who served draga in 1808

answered 5 november 2026 by the friary itself (doc): the parish of st george holds registers only from after the second world war; everything earlier is at the state archives in rijeka. the rijeka state archives then reported on 6 november that the trsat death register 1803–1815 has no entry for him (see errand 39).

why the convent and not only the state archive. the friars did the parish's work while the priest was ill: fr ruffinus czohar marries at draga on 29 september 1808 on his licence, and fr hyacinthus rigetti signs the draga baptism book as «v.p.» (vicar) from 21 september 1808. a friar who buried a priest of draga would have written it in the convent's book, and a church book is not bound by the state's closing rules. it is an inf that the burial is at trsat; the convent may simply say it holds nothing, which is also an answer.
sister to errand 39, the same question put to the rijeka state archives. send both, or send this one first if the franciscans are quicker.

zdravko defranceski's stone. he died at horsham on 22 december 1979 — twenty years before the date the family carried. this archive has the date and no photograph.

/worklist/.title: The work list — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 320 items · 164 open · 26 waiting on somebody else

the one register this archive did not have. findings go to the searched log, errors to the corrections, unanswered questions to the open questions, missing people to the gaps, and letters to the errands — but what we are actually going to do next lived only in the conversation, which is the one place that does not survive.
every other register here answers «what do we know?». this one answers «what is being done?», and it exists because that question was being carried in a chat window.

the 95 open items are at the top, in the order a reader should take them — 74 of them running or next, 21 blocked on a person or an institution. below them is what is finished, and what was struck for being founded on a mistake — kept and struck through rather than deleted, the same way this archive treats a retracted claim.

five states, and an owner on every row. running means somebody or something is at it now. next means it is ready to start. blocked means it waits on a person or an institution, and the owner says which. the dates are there so that something blocked for five weeks does not read like something raised this morning.

286. next — ready to start david, to approve the design (then a record atlas session)
record atlas errands: one shared module, so any archive or visitor sees who holds the book, what they need and what others were told — decide the data model and the privacy line

why this is worth doing, and where it is not. the errands are already the same job in every archive: a gap that reading cannot close, a holder who can, a letter, a wait. they are kept in each archive's own errands.json (40 here, 27 unsent; the atlas keeps four of its own), so the same holder is written to by several archives who never learn from each other's replies: the postal address dari wanted on 5 november is a fact every later letter to rijeka should already carry. the atlas already receives research sessions and already will know who holds what (rows 283–285); the errand is the missing third thing, and it is the one that turns the catalogue from a reference into a service: a researcher at any archive, or any visitor to recordatlas.org, sees who holds the book, what they need, in what language, what others asked, and what they answered.

what may and may not leave an archive. the line already drawn for the atlas (surname strings and counts, no given name, no full date, no relationship, no identifier, nobody living) holds, and it decides the design: the letter stays where the person is; the atlas holds the shape of the ask. a shape is holder · register (place, faith, kind, years) · what is asked (does it exist, where is it, a transcript, a scan, permission to publish) · state · outcome · dates · evidence link. the person's name, the reason and the draft stay in the archive that drafted the letter. letters are generated in the archive, from a template and a holder profile pulled from the atlas; the atlas never holds a draft with a person in it.

three guardrails, which are the reasons i would say yes and not just «go». (1) nothing sends from the atlas, as today: sending is a person's decision, and a shared module must not become a way to mass-mail archives that answer by hand (dari's office answered ours within a day, and one person reads it). (2) answered once, published for everyone: the module should show «three researchers asked dari for the trsat 1803–1815 deaths; reply of 5 november: …» before it offers to draft a fourth letter, and should bundle every open ask for one holder into one letter; that is the load-reducing reason an archive would not mind it. (3) institutional contacts only, from the holder's own page or reply; no named staff, no personal address, no scraping.

what it is not. not a server and not accounts: recordatlas.org is static and my-research is local to a browser, which is the right default for other users (their errands stay in their browser or an exported file; the atlas's json is what they read). writing back is for sessions, through a script that publishes only the published file from a fresh clone, as publish-research-sessions.py does. a visitor's «tell the atlas the answer» is a later, optional, reviewed step (a form that opens a pull request), never a live database.

order of work, one row each below. (1) the data model and the privacy line, agreed by david; (2) the atlas errand catalogue and the sync script, after the custody tool; (3) bundled letter packs and templates by language, with the holder's required fields as a checklist; (4) the public module on recordatlas.org, local-first; (5) outcomes written back, with turnaround and fee statistics and the skill that ties it together.
