✔ site/public/atlas-data.json is generated — it was reverted as drift about a dozen times, and the revert was restoring a dead link
⚠ a file that regenerates on every build was being treated as noise, and reverting it kept a wrong link published.

site/public/atlas-data.json is not hand-written. it is built by npm run publish:index — the first step of npm run build — from src/data/atlas.json, src/data/movements.json and src/data/mymap.json, written as one line of minified json. because it is one line, git diff shows the entire 400 kb file as changed when one character moves, which is exactly why session after session read it as meaningless build noise and ran git checkout on it.
the whole of the drift, parsed and compared field by field, was one href:
committed public/atlas-data.json /research-log/
src/data/atlas.json, and every fresh build /searched/

and /research-log/ is not /searched/. it is a redirect stub, and it points at /open-questions/. so a reader who clicked the dachau pin on the atlas to see what had been searched was bounced to the open questions instead — a silently wrong destination, not a broken link, which is why nothing caught it. the href was corrected in src/data/atlas.json at some point and the published artifact never caught up, because the catch-up was reverted every time it appeared.
fixed by committing the regeneration. ⚠ site/public/* is shared ground; done with --allow-shared.

⭐ for the next session, so this does not cost another dozen reverts: if git status shows site/public/atlas-data.json modified after a build, that is not drift — it is the artifact catching up with src/data/, and it should be committed. to see what actually changed, do not read the diff — parse both sides and compare: json.dumps(…, indent=1, sort_keys=true) on each, then difflib. that turned a 400 kb diff into two lines.

every sweep this archive has run searched the surname. nine spellings of it, systematically — defranceschi, de franceschi, defranceski, de franceski, defrančeski, defranzeschi, franceschi, and the two australian manglings zorafko and zdrafko. that is why the australian and arolsen files were found.
the given name has never been varied once. out of 312 rows in the research log, eight mention searching by a forename and all eight are a hunt for one named person, not a sweep.

that is a hole with a shape. fiume was a corpus separatum of the crown of st stephen and its civil registration went over to hungarian in 1895: a clerk there wrote jános, not giovanni, józsef, not giuseppe, péter, not pietro. hungaricana is free and this archive already uses it. the same for the austrian sets and johann, josef, franz, andreas. sixteen hungarian forms are already sitting in the records here, unrecognised until today — and they got in by accident, not by being looked for. the seven columns are a search plan that has never been run.
run on 20 september, and the answer is a clean methodological finding: for this name the magyarised forename is a dead end, but the magyarised word order is not.

sixteen hungarian forms were put to hungaricana as phrases, surname first as hungarian requires. fourteen returned nothing at all — gyula (julius), antal (anton), jános (ivan/johann), bálint (valentin), vincze, károly, mihály, józsef, miklós, alajos (alois), tódor (theodor), lajos, istván, ede (eduard).

two returned, and the pair explains the other fourteen. «defranceschi ferencz» gives 4 hits — the fiume harbour master's pension, his orphan francziska's grace allowance twice over, and a budapest directory of 1848. «defranceschi péter» gives 1. the rule behind it: the hungarian state printed its sentences in hungarian and its service lists in german, so the surname inverts but the forename mostly does not. ferencz is the exception because it is a spelling, not a translation — hungarian cz for german z in franz.

the control matters more than the zeros. fourteen nils would mean nothing if the method could not produce a hit; ferencz returning four known records is what makes the nils evidence. the sweep was run because the search log showed 312 rows in which the surname had been varied nine ways and the forename never once.

and it was not empty. péter turned up a fourteenth man for the imperial roll — «beim husz. reg. nr 8 · defranceschi peter dr · beim garnisons-spitale», militärschematismus 1867, a regimental physician and the second doctor on a roll that had one.

where a cardiff crew agreement of 1876–77 actually is — answered: three places, and the ship's number is the key to all three
two things are now settled and the third is the whole job.

settled: the crew lists are catalogued to the person, and further back than expected. «ship: belgravian; official number: 98611. william g s nash; rank/rating, master; age, 57; place of birth…» — and not only in the 1915 series: bt 99/1302/37 is 1881 and bt 99/1718/16b is 1891, both with name, rating, age and birthplace. this archive's first explanation of the blank — that shipping is catalogued by vessel and year rather than by master — was simply wrong, and is retracted.

open: kew holds only a fraction of the nineteenth-century agreements — the bulk went to the maritime history archive at memorial university, newfoundland. emerico married at cardiff in q3 1876 and the aquilone cleared the bute docks for guadaloupe on 11 december 1877. establish which repository holds cardiff-registered agreements for those two years, and write to whichever it is.
answered on 20 september from kew's own catalogue, and the question had the wrong shape. it is not «kew or newfoundland». it is three repositories and one number.
the national archives, bt 99 — its series description says it plainly: «a ten per cent sample of agreements and crew lists (with log-books where they survive) for the years 1861-1938».

maritime history archive, memorial university of newfoundland — catalogued in discovery as an external holding: «registrar general of shipping and seamen, crew lists, agreements and official logbooks (c70% of total)», 1863-1938.
county record offices in the british isles hold the rest — for a cardiff-registered ship that means glamorgan archives.

and the finding aid that resolves which: mf17 at kew, «index to location of crew agreements and logbooks of vessels (microfiche)», 1863-1913 — produced, pointedly, by the maritime history archive itself. its entries are «arranged according to the official number of the vessel, the vessels are not named».

so the chain is fixed and its first link is missing. ship's name → official number (from the mercantile navy list) → mf17 → the repository → the agreement, which names master, crew, ages and birthplaces. every bt 99 piece in the catalogue is titled by official numbers alone, which is why searching the surname returns nothing and always will: the index is of ships, not men.

which makes the cardiff marriage certificate the hinge of the whole maritime thread. gro cardiff, q3 1876, vol. 11a p. 428. if emerico's occupation is given as master mariner, and better still if a vessel is named, the official number follows from the mercantile navy list and mf17 says where to write. without a ship's name there is nothing to look up, in any of the three places.

each year closes in the priest's own hand — «u crikvenici dne 31 prosinca 1886», and so on — so these are whole years, not samples. 1881 and 1882 were read on the way in and are clean too.

what that settles. anton rudolf was born at klenovica on 20 january 1890; his parents josip defranceschi and anna kalanj must therefore have married by 1889. ledenice marriages stop in 1882. crikvenica was the one vinodol marriage register on film that covered the gap, and the seven years that matter are now read and they are not in it.

so the marriage is not at crikvenica, and the search moves to three named places: the parish that actually served klenovica — novi vinodolski — whose register is the obvious next order; ledenice after 1882, whose later volumes are not on this film and must be asked for from the matični ured; and bribir or grižane, the two neighbouring parishes whose people marry into crikvenica on these very pages. this is a redirection built on a complete reading, not on a sample.

the village these pages describe is worth recording for its own sake. ninety-three marriages in four years among car, kalnić, škiljan, kristofor, vračić, bernjac, kovrić, jurinčić, veljačić, matejčić, manestar, brozičević, župan — marrying each other, house number after house number. the outsiders are countable on one hand and each one is an occupation: mirko car, master mariner (1885 no. 24); adalberto radil, a baker (1885 no. 26); ivan vinko grohovac, temporary schoolmaster from grohovo by rijeka (1886 no. 4); eduardo janić of bakar (1886 no. 7); josip car, clerk at the royal tax office at karlovac (1883 no. 19); and marija-eva pilz of gospić (1886 no. 10), the only german name in four years. a defranceschi would have stood out exactly as these do — which is why the negative can be trusted.

read so far: 45 of 272 images. the declared strength for 1883–1886 is the couple columns on every page — both surnames, occupation, house number — plus the parents' and witnesses' columns on image 150. the parents' and witnesses' columns for the rest of 1883–1889 are a second pass and are still owed; a defranceschi could in principle stand there as a father or a witness without appearing as a bride or groom.
second pass done. 1883–1889 is now read on both pages — every column of every entry — and the name is not there.

the right-hand page of this register carries parentum nomen (both sets of parents, with the mothers' maiden names), testium nomen (two witnesses with their fathers' names and trades), the celebrant, the banns and dispensations, and the observationes. twenty-five right pages were read to finish images 132–157; 150 and 158–160 had been done in the first pass. 144 marriages, seven years, four columns of names each, and no defranceschi anywhere in them — not as a groom, not as a bride, not as a father, not as a mother, not as a witness.

that is the strong form of the negative. a man can marry out of a parish and never appear in its register; he cannot easily be a father or a witness there either without leaving a trace. josip defranceschi is absent from crikvenica in all four roles across the whole window in which his son was conceived and born. the marriage, and the family, were somewhere else.

things the right pages gave that the left ones could not. the parish had three priests, not one: aleksander car signs almost everything, but vč. g. mate škiljan, umirovljeni župnik — a retired priest — takes services on images 148, 149, 153 and 155, and lovro zenac, kapelan grižki, comes over from grižane for 1885 no. 24. two marriages needed military permission — «dozvolom vojničke oblasti», from rijeka (1884 no. 16 and 1886 no. 6), which means a serving soldier. and the witness column is where the village's professional class shows up: josip šanvić, obćinski bilježnik (parish notary), mate car, obćinski pazitelj and kr. lučki pazitelj (harbour watchman), a trgovac, and on 1888 no. 12 narcisio kamin, professor of navigation — a nautical school teacher standing witness at a crikvenica wedding.

the scope flag is now on two pages, not one. witnesses spelled «franić» / «frančić» appear at 1888 no. 6 and 1888 no. 18. the declared in-scope list still contains «franceschich», which is the italianised form of that same croatian patronymic of franjo. ruled on 20 september 2026: «frančić is adjacent, take franceschich off the list». so they are not hits, and the seven-year negative for 1883–1889 stands unqualified. franceschich has been moved to the adjacent forms and taken off the drift chart — correction 110. twelve spellings are the name; six are adjacent.
into the second half: 1890 and most of 1891 read, both pages, on the way to 1908.

1890 is complete — images 161–163, eleven marriages, closed «u crikvenici 31 prosinca 1890». 1891 is read to entry 23 across images 163–167. no defranceschi in either year, in any of the four name columns.

the village is beginning to leak, and the register shows it. where 1883–1886 had five outsiders in four years, 1890–91 already has a bride from senj with the župnik of senj himself standing witness (1890 no. 9), a groom from vrbnik on krk married by permission of the vrbnik parish office (1890 no. 11), a man from sv. križ začretje in the zagorje who is a čuvar na željeznici u rieci — a railway guard at rijeka (1891 no. 14) — and brides and grooms out of grižane and sv. jelena. the railway and the steamer are pulling strangers into a parish that married itself for centuries, and that is the context in which a defranceschi could arrive.

and the bishop came. image 165 carries a seal and a signature across the foot of the page: «vidjeno na kanoničnoj vizitaciji dne 20. svibnja 1891 — juraj posilović, biskup» — the bishop of senj-modruš inspecting the register in person. it is the second visitation mark on this film; there is another, unsigned, in 1881.
53 of 272 images read. 1883–1891 is now continuous and complete except the last stretch of 1891. still to do: 1892–1908 (images 168–272) and 1859–1882 (images 4–123).
1891 and 1892 complete; 1893 begun. 59 of 272 images.

1891 closes at 24 marriages (images 163–168) and 1892 at 23 (images 168–172), each signed off by aleksandar car on 31 december. 1893 is open at entry 5. no defranceschi in any column of either year. 1883 to 1892 is now ten unbroken years.

the outsiders have stopped being a trickle. in 1892 alone: a joiner from vrbnik on krk; dragutin gaus, another joiner, married by leave of the royal hungarian ministry of defence; and — the first of its kind in this book — marko pavletić, an innkeeper, marrying zuzana rotter of nádasd in hungary, the pair of them entered as «necatolik». a hungarian protestant bride in a vinodol parish register is the clearest sign yet that crikvenica had stopped being only a village and started being a resort on a railway.

that changes what the negative is worth, and the change runs the right way for this search. the closed-village argument that makes the 1880s nil so strong gets weaker each year — but the reason it weakens is that strangers with foreign names were arriving and being written down. if a defranceschi ever came to crikvenica, this is the decade the book would show it. so far it does not.
1893 and 1894 complete, 1895 read to entry 20. 71 of 272 images. twelve unbroken years, 1883–1894, and still nothing.
1893 closes at 23 marriages, 1894 at 18. no defranceschi in any column of either.

the register itself improves from 1894 — the clerk stops writing ages and starts writing exact birth dates for bride and groom, which is why these later years would identify a man rather than merely name him.

and the arrivals keep widening. a pharmacist from kraljevica (1893 no. 17); a man from bag — karlobag (1893 no. 14); a bride from grosuplje near ljubljana whose mother was a kropf (1894 no. 15); a groom from lič with a railway watchman at rijeka standing witness (1894 no. 16); a wedding performed at kraljevica by its own chaplain (1895 no. 19); and a post-and-telegraph official from gospić married with tomislav plem. budisavljević — a nobleman — as witness (1895 no. 20).
the parish is now marrying pharmacists, telegraph clerks, railwaymen and a slovene bride. it is exactly the population a defranceschi would have belonged to, and he is not in it.
1896 and 1897 complete, 1898 read to entry 24. 89 of 272 images. fifteen unbroken years, 1883–1897.
1896 closes at 22 marriages, 1897 at 26. no defranceschi in any column of either.

one old error corrected on the way past. a previous session logged image 200 as «1897 nos 1–2». it is «godina 1898» nos 1–5 — the names it recorded (zenić/kovrić, župan/župan) are right, the year was misread, the same flourished-digit trap that turned 1888 into 1877 and 1883 into 1885. the log now carries the correction.

and the town has finished changing. 1898 alone gives a hotel supervisor, a professor, a bank director and the municipal treasurer standing as witnesses, a telegraph worker at rijeka, a merchant from rijeka named benvenuto vekil — an italian forename at last — and a page on which nearly every groom is a zidar, a mason. crikvenica in the 1890s is a building site with a hotel on it, and its register is full of masons, carpenters, tinsmiths and hotel staff drawn in from krk, ljubljana, gmunden, karlovac and gospić.

that is the strongest form the negative can take. the parish was no longer closed; it was pulling in exactly the kind of italian-named tradesman this family produced. fifteen years of it, and the name does not appear once.
1898 and 1899 complete, 1900 read to entry 20. 100 of 272 images — and the film is now more than a third read.
1898 closes at 24 marriages, 1899 at 32. seventeen unbroken years, 1883–1899, and the name is in no column of any of them.

a second bishop signs the book. image 210: «vidio na kanoničkoj vizitaciji u crikvenici dne 20. svibnja 1899. + antun» — antun maurović, posilović's successor at senj-modruš. that is two episcopal visitations caught in this reading, 1891 and 1899.

by 1899 the register has become a list of masons. page after page: zidar, zidar, zidar. the grand hotel and the villas were going up and the parish was marrying the men who built them — with a brewer, a tinsmith, a gendarme, a butcher, an innkeeper and a servant named prohaska among the witnesses.

which is the whole point of reading it. zidar is the trade anna kalanj's own brother followed, and it is the trade an immigrant italian-named craftsman would have followed too. seventeen years of masons at crikvenica, and not one of them is a defranceschi.
1900, 1901, 1902 and 1903 complete. 113 of 272 images — twenty-one unbroken years, 1883–1903.
1900 closes at 24 marriages, 1901 at 21, 1902 at 26, 1903 at 28. no defranceschi in any of the four name columns of any of them.

1902 has a five-month hole in it that is not a gap in the reading. the book runs from 19 february straight to 22 october — no marriage at all between them. that is lent and then the building season: in a parish of masons and mariners, nobody marries while the work is on.

the catchment is now continental. these four years bring in a groom from kowalówka in galicia, josip elia schmidt, son of an officijal, marrying a car of crikvenica (1902 no. 25); a carpenter from gödöllő and a railwayman from darázsfalva, both in hungary; a man from krupa in bosnia; a groom from medjimurje, parish prelog; one from ovba in ungarija; and a crikvenica joiner whose domicile is entered as «u poli» — pula — married by leave of the pola parish office. three entries of 1903 are in a second hand with a different celebrant and the religion column marked «p. kt.», a non-catholic rite written into the catholic book.

one line is worth recording even though it is not our name. 1901 no. 10, image 218: the groom's origin column reads «landrovac» with «italij[a]» struck through — the only mention of italy anywhere in this book so far. the groom is a blašković, so it is an observation, not a find; but it shows the clerk did write italy in this column when italy was the answer, which is one more reason the seventeen-year silence on the name means what it says.
still to read: 1904–1908 (images 233–272) and 1859–1882 (images 4–123).
1904, 1905, 1906 and 1907 complete. 144 of 272 images — twenty-five unbroken years, 1883–1907, and one page of 1908 to go.

1904 closes at 26 marriages, 1905 at 36 («crikvenica dne 30 prosinca 1905. car, župnik»), 1906 at 45 — the busiest year in the book — and 1907 at 31. no defranceschi in any of the four name columns of any of them.
these four years are where the foreign names finally arrive in force, and they are worth listing because each one is the kind of entry a defranceschi would have made:
josip wolf, a locksmith from novi sad in the bačka, living at crikvenica, marrying a vračić (1907 no. 30);
berti königsberger, son of herman königsberger and a mother née feiner, marrying a car (1906 no. 36) — the first german-jewish surname in the register;
ferdinando sandor mihely kolomarić, a hungarian railwayman routed through zagreb (1906 no. 32);
franjo ivan pagliaga of bakar, son of anton pagliaga, mariner, and vittoria (1907 no. 3) — an italian surname on an italian mother, read at magnification to be sure;
milan caran of korenica, domiciled at pola, entered as istočno-pravoslavne vjeroispovjedi — an orthodox groom married to a catholic bride under naval permission from pola (1905 no. 30);
a dalmatian ex-soldier at pola (1904 no. 1) and a joiner from pag (1906 no. 35);
grooms from gödöllő, darázsfalva, debrecen, nagy torda, nedelišće, vrbovsko, novi vinodolski, medjimurje and matarija;
and italianate forenames on local surnames — ninfa brnjac, libera matejčić, emigdio milan brnjac, matilda car, kalista tracić, roberto paulin, rudolfo car, eduardo brnjac.

that is the test this reading was for. the parish is now marrying a jewish-named clerk, a serbian orthodox sailor, a hungarian railwayman, an italian mariner's son from bakar and a locksmith from novi sad — and writing every one of them down, with birthplace, father's name and trade. an italian-named mason called defranceschi is precisely what this book records when it happens. twenty-five years, and it never happens.

one caution logged against myself: 1907 no. 20 looked at first like «iz italije». magnified, it is «i kalista» — the bride's forename. the correction is in the reading log; nothing was published on the misreading.
still to read: the last of 1908 (images 262–272) and 1859–1882 (images 4–123).
the second half of the film is finished. 1883 to 1908 is read end to end, both pages, and the name is not in it.

1908 closes at 33 marriages (images 262–268), and image 272 is the film's own closing target: «župa crikvenica · hrvatska croatia · matična knjiga vjenčanih 1859–1908 · item 1 · project cro 00008 · roll 28». there is nothing after it.

twenty-six consecutive years — 1883 to 1908 — every entry, every column. roughly 560 marriages, each carrying a groom, a bride, four parents with the mothers' maiden names, two witnesses with their fathers' names and trades, the celebrant and the dispensations. no defranceschi stands in any of those roles, in any year.

the last three pages are not entries at all, and they are worth having. images 269–271 are blank ruled pages with loose certificates pasted onto them — the parish's own working papers, kept in the back of the book:
a freedom-to-marry certificate of 16 november 1868 for a tomas škrolin-lončar of crikvenica, signed josip medvedić, crikvenički vikar;
another of 22 november 1869 in the same hand;
a medical clearance for a mihovil car, «crikvenica 20/4 66»;

and, dated 22 april 1866, a note about ludoviška car of crikvenica signed «katarina šuvčić, babica» — the village midwife, in her own handwriting. she is not a name this archive was looking for, and she is exactly the kind of person a parish register almost never lets you hear from directly.

and one entry that shows how far the parish would reach when it had to. 1908 no. 17, mate brnjičić and ljuba car, was married on a papal brief — breve apostolicum, roma, 10 february 1908 — dispensing an impediment of affinity in the collateral line. beside it, on the same page, sits an entry struck through diagonally and renumbered: the clerk cancelled a marriage he had written down and gave the number to the next couple.

what is left. the first half — images 4 to 123, the years 1859 to 1882. those years matter less for josip and anna, who cannot have married before about 1883, but they are the years in which a defranceschi grandfather could have come and gone, and the standard for marking this volume read is every page. the reading continues at image 4.
the first half is open, and the book turns out to be in latin.

images 4–8 are the film's own front matter and they are worth keeping, because they give the citation this volume has never had on the site: the register is povijesni arhiv rijeka 275 (k4), inv. 110, matične knjige rimokatolika, župa crikvenica, matična knjiga vjenčanih (1859–1908), filmed at the hrvatski državni arhiv in zagreb on 14 november 1996 by an operator named anita kekić, project cro 00008, roll 28.

from image 9 the register begins, and every entry to at least 1861 is written in latin. leopoldus, josephus, stephanus, bartholomaeus; agricola for every trade; ter promulgati in the banns column; dispensations «in tertio gradu consanguinitatis». that changes what the eye is looking for. in these years the name would be written de franceschi, franceschi or defranceschius — the latin nominative — and not the croatian form the later pages would use. the reading is being done with that in mind.

1859 closes at 15 marriages, 1860 at 12 («sequitur annus 1861» in the priest's hand), and 1861 is open. nothing so far. two names were magnified to be sure they were not ours and were not: a kostrulja that looked briefly like a franč- form, and a groom whose origin appeared to read zara and reads, enlarged, «parochia selcensis» — the parish of selce.
familysearch has flagged these pages «water damage / oštećeno od vlage», and the flag is honest: the ink is pale and the margins are cockled. they are still legible.
1861 and 1862 complete; 1863 read to entry 12. images 4–30 done.
1861 closes at 21 marriages, 1862 at 21, each signed off in the priest's own latin — «sequitur annus 1862», «sequitur annus 1863». no defranceschi in any column of either.

three names were magnified rather than guessed at, because in a latin hand a franc- stem is exactly what a hurried eye invents. 1861 no. 11 looked like frančić; enlarged twice, the surname wraps across two lines as fra-ssich — frašić, which is neither in scope nor adjacent to it. the other two resolved the same way.

what these pages give besides the negative. the trade column, which by 1900 is nothing but zidar, in 1861 says agricola for almost every man — and then begins to admit nauta, a sailor. the religion column, uniform for fifty years afterwards, carries in 1862 no. 10 a second line reading «cath. graeca» beside rom. cath. — the only non-latin-rite marking in the book so far. brides and grooms come in from selce, grižane, zagorje, sv. helena and once from parochia segniensis, the parish of senj — which is this archive's other line. and the dispensations are granted not by a chancery but «ab excellentissimo ac illustrissimo domino episcopo», the bishop in person, for marriages inside the third and fourth degrees of consanguinity: a village marrying its cousins, and the bishop signing it off year after year.
1863, 1864 and 1865 complete; 1866 read to entry 8. images 4–44 done.

1863 closes at 28 marriages, 1864 at 19, 1865 at only 8 — the thinnest year in the whole book. each is signed off «sequitur annus …» over the name of the parish priest, stanislaus katnić, župnik, and image 35 carries an audit line across the head of the page: «presentes matriculae revisae … in crikvenica die 10 oct. 1863 — venceslaus car, curatus.» no defranceschi in any column of any of them.
and in 1865 the first italian name in this register finally appears — in the bride's column, and it is not ours.

1865 no. 7, read at magnification because the hand is small: «d. anselmus susanich, comitatus humani judicii districtus vinodolensis scriba» — clerk of the vinodol district court — of kostrena sveta lucija, marrying maria-anna montanari. one of the witnesses is antonius sokol, negotiator, a merchant. in a book where every other man on the page is an agricola, this single entry brings in a court official, a merchant and an italian surname, all at once.

that is the shape of the evidence, stated plainly. when somebody of that kind married at crikvenica, the register wrote down his office, his district and his wife's italian name in full. it had the vocabulary and it used it. it never had occasion to write ours.

two more near-misses were magnified rather than guessed at and both dissolved: 1865 no. 8 looked like a franc- form at reading size and is joannes ivančić; and an earlier one resolved to frašić. that is now four such checks in the first half, and every one of them has come back a different name.

the trade column has begun to move: alongside agricola it now admits nauta, and twice c.r. miles — a serving imperial-royal soldier married under «indulto auctoritatis militaris». witnesses come from de schola selcensi, the selce schoolhouse. one marriage of 1863 was celebrated «in parochiali ecclesia selcensi ad s. jacobum», in the church of st james at selce.
1866 complete; 1867 read to entry 37. images 4–58 done — a fifth of the first half.
1866 closes at 20 marriages. 1867 is already at 37 and still running, the busiest year yet in this half of the book. no defranceschi in any column of either.

the parish is going to sea. from 1866 the trade column stops saying only agricola: entry after entry now reads c.r. nauta — an imperial-royal sailor — or c.r. miles, and their marriages carry «cum indulto c.r. auctoritatis militaris» or the leave of the inclytus comitatus fluminensis, the county of rijeka. in 1867 alone, seven grooms are serving men. and 1866 no. 12 brings the first ship's officer into the book: «d. thomas brozović, marinae capitaneus» of bakar, married by bakar's own parish priest.

one page is not a record at all. at the close of 1866, image 48, the priest has written across the blank remainder of the spread, in a clear hand and much larger than the entries: «crescite, et multiplicamini; et replete terram. — gen.» — increase and multiply, and fill the earth. then, beneath it, «sequitur annus 1867».
a fifth magnified check: 1867 no. 10 read as franich at reading size and is dračić. five checks in the first half, five different names, and none of them ours.
1867, 1868 and 1869 complete; 1870 begun. images 4–68 done.
1867 closes at 37 marriages — the busiest year of the first half — 1868 at 21, 1869 at 28. no defranceschi in any column of any of them.

the book changes clerk at 1868 and the change is worth noting for anyone who reads after me. from january 1868 the hand is smaller and rounder, bride and groom are written on separate lines, ages are given as plain numerals instead of «an. 24», and the religion column is spelled out in full — romani catholici. rochus katnić, cooperator signs the first year of it; then theodorus marijan, matthaeus butković, and from late 1869 alexander car, parochus.

the second italian surname in the book arrives in 1868, and like the first it belongs to somebody passing through. 1868 no. 16, magnified to be sure of it: antonius benedetti of fiume, mercator, marrying maria pelc of hinje in carniola. a merchant from rijeka and a slovene bride, in a parish that otherwise married car to car. again: the register knew how to write an italian name. it wrote this one.

the genesis line is not a one-off. it appeared across the blank foot of 1866; it appears again at the close of 1869, this time split over both halves of the spread — «crescite et multiplicamini … et replete terram» — before «sequitur annus 1870».

and the sea keeps taking the men. miles marinus, miles maris, nauta — 1869 has four of them in twenty-eight marriages. one witness of 1869 is named in full for the first time: joannes stephanus mažuranić, ludimagister in crikvenica, the village schoolmaster.
the two italian families of crikvenica turn up as witnesses — and that is the sharpest form this negative has taken.
1870 complete at 25 marriages; 1871 read to entry 11. images 4–76 done.
on 10 january 1871 the witnesses to a crikvenica wedding are, in the priest's own words and confirmed at magnification: «emericus benedetti, mercator in loco, & eugenius montanari».
both names have been met before in this reading, and both arrived from outside:
montanari first appears in 1865, when a maria-anna montanari marries the clerk of the vinodol district court;
benedetti in 1868, when antonius benedetti of fiume, a merchant, marries a slovene bride from carniola.

by 1871 they are no longer passing through. benedetti is mercator in loco — the merchant of this place — and the two of them stand together at a village wedding, which is what settled families do. the register names them, gives their trade, and states their residence.

this is the strongest form the argument can take in the first half of the book. crikvenica in the 1860s did receive italian-named incomers; it kept them; it wrote them into the register as grooms, as brides, and as witnesses, with occupations attached. the parish had both the vocabulary and the occasion. across 1859–1871 it never once had cause to write defranceschi.

also on these pages: 1870 no. 16, magnified — dominus vitus lenčić, localis scholae magister, of lokve, marrying maria magdalena planinz. the village schoolmaster, another outsider with a profession, another name written down in full.
a third bishop signs the book — and this one is the earliest.

image 79, across the foot of the 1871 spread: «praesentes copulatorum matriculas … nos in crikvenica occasione nostrae canonicae visitationis revidimus et approbavimus. sic in crikvenica die 13ª octobris 1871.» — venceslaus soić, episcopus segniensis et modrusiensis.

that makes three episcopal visitations caught in this reading of one volume: soić in 1871, posilović in 1891, maurović in 1899. each time a bishop of senj-modruš sat down with this book, went through it, and signed that he had. whatever else is true of this register, it was inspected — which is part of why the silence in it can be trusted.

images 4–80 done; 1871 read to entry 25. the trades keep widening: 1871 alone has a sutor (cobbler), a pictor (painter) from selce, three serving soldiers, and a nauta of portoré — kraljevica under its italian name.

a sixth magnified check: 1871 no. 15 read as a possible franc- form and is matthaeus franović, sutor. six checks in the first half, six different names. and 1871 no. 14, first read as «istria», is «sponsus portoregensis».
1872 and most of 1873 read. images 4–86 done. 1872 closes at only 10 marriages — the thinnest year since 1865.
three entries on these pages are worth having, and one of them puts an italian surname and ledenice on the same line for the first time.

1873 no. 8, magnified twice: «pius devalle, sutor» — a cobbler — his origin written «sponsus ledena[ice]». an italian-surnamed shoemaker out of ledenice, marrying at crikvenica in february 1873. he is not ours, and nothing here suggests he is. but ledenice is where anna kalanj was baptised in 1864, and this is the first time in the whole reading that an italian name and that village appear together. it is logged for what it is: a fact about the place, not a link.

1873 no. 9, magnified: «dominus josephus pauricchi × maria braitenfeld», married in articulo mortis — at the point of death — the union afterwards ratified by the ordinariate on 3 april. a third italian-form surname, a german one beside it, and a ragusa connection in the parents' column. the parish register recorded even this, a deathbed marriage of two outsiders, in full.

and benedetti is still here. he witnesses 1872 no. 7 and again 1873 no. 8, each time written «mercator in loco», once alongside a second merchant, david mansanari. from 1868 to 1873 the same italian merchant family keeps appearing, and the clerk keeps naming it.

also on these pages: josephus jelinić, financiarius, a revenue officer of selce, married under indult of the supreme financial directorate dated 11 november 1871, with vitus cukić, officialis financiarius standing witness. the austrian state is now inside this village register too.
1873 and 1874 complete; 1875 begun. images 4–94 done — the first half is two-thirds read.
1873 closes at 19 marriages, 1874 at 23. no defranceschi in any column of either.

these are quiet years in the book and the entries are almost all car, brnjac, župan, matejčić, benić, ivančić and jurinčić marrying each other across the villages of dolac, draga, supera, sopaljska and ludvić — the same closed circle the 1880s pages showed. the one thing that keeps changing is the witness column, where the parish's small officialdom is now named: a tabernarius communalis in loco — the village innkeeper — a miles pensionatus, a communal officer, and beside them the merchants benedetti and mansanari.
remaining: images 95–123, the years 1875 to 1882.
the montanari, four times across eleven years — and a correction to my own log.
1875 closes at 19 marriages, 1876 at 23 — the priest writes the total himself: «anno 1876 copulati fuere 23. sequitur annus 1877.» no defranceschi in either. images 4–104 done.

1876 no. 20, magnified: «dnus jacobus pezelj, capitaneus maritimus» — a master mariner — marrying a daughter of david montanari. the parents' column gives it plainly: «dftus laurentius pezelj & maria nata zelenčić — david monta[nari] & …»
that is the fourth appearance of this one italian family in the volume:
1865 maria-anna montanari marries the clerk of the vinodol district court
1871 eugenius montanari stands witness beside benedetti, the merchant in loco
1873 david montanari stands witness, «mercator in loco»
1876 david montanari's daughter marries a master mariner

a correction to my own reading, made before it did any harm. the 1873 witness i logged as «david mansanari» is david montanari — the same man, read properly at magnification. the scratchpad log carries the correction.

this is what a family that actually lived in crikvenica looks like in this book: it arrives, it is written down with its trade, it witnesses its neighbours' weddings, and it marries its daughter off to a ship's captain — and the clerk records every stage. eighteen years of the register have now been read on both pages, 1859 to 1876, and our name has not once been written in any of them.
remaining: images 105–123, the years 1877 to 1882.
the register changes language in january 1878 — and that closes the last gap in the reading.
1877 closes at 16 marriages, signed off «sequitur annus 1878. crikvenica 31 decembris 1877. alexander car». no defranceschi. images 4–110 done; thirteen images left.

at the head of 1878 the book stops being latin and becomes croatian. «ljeta gospodinova 1878, dne … siečnja»; poljodjelac where it said agricola; rimo katolik spelled out; ages as «zaručnik 20 godina, zaručnica 22 godine»; status «neoženjen / neudata». aleksandar car now signs as župnik, not parochus, and the observations cite the senj ordinariat and the hungarian ministry in croatian.

why this matters for the search, and not only as a curiosity. the first half of this volume was read looking for de franceschi / defranceschius — the latin nominative. from 1878 onward the same eye must look for defranceschi / defranceski, the croatian form that the 1880s and 1890s pages use. the changeover happens inside this reading, and both forms have now been searched for in the years where each was the one the clerk would have written. there is no seam in the evidence where a differently-spelled name could have slipped through.
and in 1878 the trade that ends this book begins. 1878 no. 7: «mate kristofor, zidar» — the first mason in the register. by 1899 nearly every groom on the page is a zidar; here is the first of them.
also on these pages: mate matejčić, domobranac — a croatian home-guardsman, married under leave of the royal hungarian ministry, the state and its languages arriving together.
the volume is read. all 272 images, both pages, 1859 to 1908 — and the name is not in it.

1880 closes at 12 marriages, 1881 is read to entry 8, and image 123 was the last image of this film that had never been looked at. with it, every one of the 272 images is read, and a check against the log confirms there is no gap: missing images: none.

fifty years of one parish's marriages, on both pages of every entry. groom, bride, both sets of parents with the mothers' maiden names, two witnesses with their fathers' names and trades, the celebrant, the banns, the dispensations and the observations. not one defranceschi, in any spelling, in any of those roles, in any year.

and the one debt this reading declared against itself is now paid. early on i recorded that 1888 entries 16 and 17 had never been seen, falling between images 157 and 158. they have now been found and read: they are the first two rows of image 158, which a previous session numbered 18 and 19.
1888 no. 16 — petar kalnić, of the pomorska oblast na rieci, the maritime authority at rijeka, marrying ivana wessel of ljubljana, 25 october 1888.
1888 no. 17 — mikula car and marija car, radnici, 21 november 1888.

which means a correction to this archive's own figures: 1888 closes at 17 marriages, not 19. the names in that year were right; the count was two too many. it is recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because the point of reading a volume end to end is that the arithmetic can be checked.
what fifty years of this register actually shows

the parish was not closed to strangers, and it wrote every one of them down. across the volume the clerk recorded, with trade and birthplace attached: a district-court clerk and his wife maria-anna montanari (1865); antonius benedetti of fiume, merchant, and his slovene bride (1868); pius devalle, an italian-surnamed cobbler out of ledenice (1873); josephus pauricchi, married in articulo mortis (1873); master mariners, a schoolmaster from lokve, a revenue officer, a galician clerk's son, a jewish-named groom, a serbian orthodox sailor from korenica, a locksmith from novi sad, franjo ivan pagliaga of bakar, son of vittoria — and hungarians, bosnians, carniolans and krk islanders by the dozen.

two italian families settled and stayed. the benedetti appear five times between 1868 and 1880 — arriving from fiume, trading in loco, witnessing their neighbours' weddings, and finally marrying a daughter, jolanda katarina benedetti, in february 1880. the montanari appear four times between 1865 and 1876, ending with david montanari's daughter marrying a master mariner.

that is the shape of the negative, and it is as strong as a negative gets. this register had the vocabulary, the occasion and the habit of writing italian names down in full. it did so for two families over two decades. it never once had cause to write ours.

seven look-alikes were magnified rather than guessed at — frašić, koštrulja, ivančić, dračić, franović, marohnić and one origin that read as zara and is parochia selcensis. every one came back a different name. and the volume changes language inside the reading — latin to 1877, croatian from january 1878 — so both de franceschi and defranceschi were searched for in the years where each was the form the clerk would have used. there is no seam where a differently-spelled name could have slipped through.
what this closes, and what it does not

it closes crikvenica. the marriage of josip defranceschi and anna kalanj is not in this book, and neither is any other bearer of the name, in fifty years. that is not a sample; it is the whole volume.

it does not close the question. anton rudolf was born at klenovica on 20 january 1890, so his parents married by 1889, and the search now stands where this reading has left it: novi vinodolski, the parish that actually served klenovica; ledenice after 1882, whose later volumes are not on film; and bribir or grižane, the neighbours whose people marry into these very pages. those are letters to write and registers to order, not films to read.
131. done — finished and published this archive
the kriegsarchiv says the army records may already be digitised — and nobody has looked

vienna answered the 14 september enquiry by quoting for the sailors and declining the soldiers, and the decline is the more useful half. for angehörige der landstreitkräfte the kriegsarchiv points at its own «kriegsarchiv forschungstipps (faq)», saying it already holds numerous tips for self-study online «worunter auch alle bereits digitalisierten bestände fallen» — including every holding already digitised.

four men of the name are waiting in that half. theodor defranceschi, k. k. landwehr, fähnrich (nichtaktiv), 27th regiment, seniority 1 january 1907. alois defranceschi, k. u. k. heer infantry cadet, in the rank lists 1916–1918. eduard defranceschi, k. k. line infantry, cadet 1859 and unterleutnant 2. klasse 1863 — and whether that is one man or two is still open. and dr cäsar peschle, landwehr medical officer from 1 august 1895.

what is wanted from each is the same single fact: the geburtsort. the printed rank lists give the year of birth and never the place, which is precisely why not one of these men can be attached to a household.
free, online, and never once opened. the paid navy search on julius and valentin is a separate decision and costs €45 whether it finds anything or not.

done, 20 september, and it went further than the four soldiers. the digitised holdings vienna pointed at turned out to include the whole östa catalogue as a free name search — archivinformationssystem.at/feldsuche.aspx, no account. one query returns 99 records on the stem, 53 of them this name: ava 19, fhka 12, hhsta 11, kriegsarchiv 7, adr 4. the full inventory is on the research log.

on the four soldiers themselves the answer is mostly bad news, and worth knowing. officers' qualifikationslisten 1870–1918 are filmed and on familysearch (hauptreihe a–z), but lists of officers who took successor-state citizenship after 1918 were handed over to those states. ncos' and men's grundbuchsblätter were kept decentrally: for the küstenland — trieste, istria, görz-gradisca — birth years 1860–1900 are at the archivio di stato di trieste, not vienna; and for the lands of the hungarian crown, including croatia-slavonia, none survive at all. theodor, alois and dr peschle are therefore to be sought in trieste or zagreb before vienna, and that is a finding the €45 would not have bought.

eduard, 1859–1863, is the one still fully open in vienna — the pre-1868 abgangs-verzeichnisse are name-searchable online for all truppenkörper and the grundbuchblätter themselves are browsable, both filmed by familysearch. that is the next sitting, and it is free.
132. next — ready to start this archive 53 days
the flag patents — the name is in the habsburg merchant-marine registers from 1759

erteilung der flaggenpatente, scontrini und passavanti, nach namen — a hofkammer series that registers who was allowed to fly the imperial flag, arranged by name, and the entry reads «… fiumaner handelskompagnie 1751-1787 … franceschi 1759-17.. …».

this archive has an at-sea page built out of masters' certificates and a cardiff marriage, and it starts in the nineteenth century. a flag patent is the licence a shipowner held. if the name is in this series from 1759, the family's maritime life is a century older than anything published here, and it is documented in vienna rather than inferred.

the company named beside it matters too. the fiumaner handelskompagnie, 1751–1787, is the fiume trading company — the very port this archive keeps circling. the signature, pulled the same afternoon: at-oesta/fhka nhk kommerz lit akten 946 — carton 1752–1791, former reference 5.377 / r.nr. 637, faszikulatur 113 f, protection expired 1821, public and permission-free. and the dates are exact: franceschi 1759–1770.

the series is the point. kommerz litorale, 1705–1813 is the hofkammer's commerce administration for the austrian littoral — trieste and fiume. a flaggenpatent is the licence to fly the imperial flag on a merchant ship; scontrini and passavanti are the clearance papers that go with it. so a franceschi was licensed to trade under the imperial flag out of the littoral between 1759 and 1770 — a hundred years before the earliest master's certificate on the at-sea page, and sitting in the same carton as the fiumaner handelskompagnie, 1751–1787.

22 september 2026 — checked in the re-run, and it is still one carton and still the only one. at-oesta/fhka nhk kommerz lit akten 946 is the sole flag-patent record of the name in the whole catalogue; the contains re-run that turned up nineteen other files added nothing to this one. it remains an order, not a read.
133. next — ready to start this archive 53 days
a copy of the arms, dated 13 may 1825, in the austrian nobility archive
the arms page rests on a lintel and a stone. the adelsarchiv holds paper.

at-oesta/ava adel haa ar 251.11 and 251.12 are adelsbestätigungen of 24 may 1825 for «franceschi, niklas, markus, johann baptist, de» and «franceschi, mark anton, de» — the genitive spelling, in scope. ar 251.13 confirms vinzenz franceschi, 25 june 1830; ar 251.14, philipp, 1838–39.

and ar 251.15 is the one to open first: a request of 1897 for «ausfertigung eines adelszertifikates und einer wappenkopie, dato 13.05.1825» — a copy of the coat of arms, made from an 1825 original. behind it sit ar 251.9 (jakob von franceschi, dutch knighthood, 1608), ar 251.10 (thomas von franceschi, 1610) and raa 119.29 (michael angelo franceschi of lucca, 1550, adelsstand, wappenbesserung).

one honest deflation, checked before publishing it. ar 251.15's own catalogue entry reads «wappen: nein · siegel: nein» and extent: fol. 1–6 — so the 1897 file is the request for the certificate and the arms copy, not the drawing. the arms it refers back to are the 13 may 1825 original, and that is what would have to be traced.

a fifth document may matter more than all of them. at-oesta/hhsta ka vertrauliche akten 56-1-49 — «nr. 49: marchese johann maria gravisi, nicolaus de franceschi», 1825, fol. 229–243, fifteen folios in the confidential files of the kabinettsarchiv. the gravisi were marquises of capodistria. a de franceschi named beside one of them in a confidential imperial file, in the same year as the nobility confirmations, is istrian politics rather than genealogy — and this archive has never had a document of that kind.
whether any of these is this family is exactly the question. all are public and permission-free.
134. next — ready to start this archive 53 days
pietro franceschi wanted a post at almissa in 1828, and almissa is omiš
at-oesta/ava justiz ojst js ds 83.1.14 — «franceschi, pietro, praktikantenstelle in almissa», 1828–1843. almissa is the italian name of omiš, and the omiš line is one of this archive's six.

it does not stand alone. the austrian justice administration holds a cluster of dalmatian officials of the name: js ds 80.3.4, franceschi, antonio, 1843; jm präs. a 140.14, «franceschi, giovanni pietro de, personalstandesausweis», 1876–1881; and jm präs. a 134.22, carl dragutin defranceschi, born 29 july 1883 at zara, judge at the district court of šibenik, 1909–1918.

four men of the name in the courts of dalmatia across eighty years — omiš, zadar, šibenik. a personalstandesausweis and a prospetto dello stato personale both give birthplace, parents and career. found 20 september; none of the four is in this archive.

22 september 2026 — the cluster grows and one of them has a birthplace. the östa catalogue, re-run with the «contains» operator instead of the form's default, adds josef franceschi, korporal — «geburtsort: almissa, dalmatien» (at-oesta/ka marine nma pers verev kl-gagorangkl 725). a man born at omiš, in a state record, is new here.

and this roster already carried, from the familysearch index, an antonio franceschi born 1801 and buried at almissa in 1877 and another born 1818, buried there in 1888. so the omiš cluster is now documented from two directions — the parish index and the austrian service records — without either knowing about the other. no kinship is claimed between them. all are on the roster.
135. next — ready to start this archive 53 days
johann defranceschi of gallignana, born 1833 — a sailor out of the origin parish
gallignana is gračišće, the istrian parish this family comes out of and whose registers open in 1644. the kriegsarchiv holds three files on a man born there in 1833 and none of them was known here.

at-oesta/ka marine nma pers offbea akten mgbbl 2651, verev kdi 219 and verev kl-mardi 76 — defranceschi, johann, geb. 1833, geburtsort gallignana. the rank moves across the three: marinediener 4. klasse on one, 1. klasse on the other two, so a career is legible from the catalogue alone. the protection term on the last expired 31 december 1933; all three are marked public, no permission required.

a marinegrundbuchblatt gives birthplace, parents, religion, marriage and children. for a man born at gračišće in 1833 that is a household — and the gračišće baptism of 1833 is what would match against it.

20 sept 2026 — both searchable routes tried, both empty, and one of them does not exist. the index holds forty-five defranceschi births for 1825–1842 in croatia and not one is at gračišće; there is no johann or giovanni born 1833 in the set. and gračišće is not on film — it is not a parish in the collection, only pazin, stari pazin and lupoglav are, and this archive's own atlas has carried nfilms: 0 for it all along. the sentence that said otherwise has been corrected.

the route that works is a named request to dapa pazin — johann/giovanni defranceschi, gračišće (gallignana), born 1833 — the same shape of request they answered once before for 117 kuna. that can go in the same envelope as the östa order for mgbbl 2651, and between them a marinegrundbuchblatt and a baptism would give the man two independent households.

22 september 2026 — the three files disagree about the village, in a useful way. read at the detail level: verev kdi 219 gives «gallignano, istrien» and marinediener 4. klasse; mgbbl 2651 gives «gallignana, küstenland» and 1. klasse; verev kl-mardi 76 gives «gallignana, istrien, illyrien» and 1. klasse. one man, one village, three clerks and three administrative vocabularies — istria, the littoral, illyria — which is the habsburg reorganisation of this coast showing up inside one sailor's paperwork.
he is now on the roster with all three signatures. the route to his baptism is unchanged: a named request to dapa pazin, because gračišće is not on film.
136. running — a machine or a person is at it now this session 53 days
svetvinčenat — the castle the name never left, and antonio's exemption of 1780

this archive has six lines and none of them is san vincenti. atti 48 (2018), from the centro di ricerche storiche at rovigno, says something no source here has ever said: «il cognome defranceschi era stato l'unico ad avere nel castello di san vincenti una continuità…» — of all the surnames in the castle of san vincenti, this one alone was continuous.

and it acted as a body. «guidati da antonio defranceschi, nel 1780 avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata» — led by antonio defranceschi, in 1780 they got themselves excused from armed defence duty. that is a household group with a spokesman and a privilege, in a named place, in a named year.

svetvinčenat is twenty-five kilometres from gračišće and it is in the same pazin county this archive's oldest registers come out of. whether it is a branch, the parent stock, or an unrelated household of the name is exactly the question a one-name study exists to ask.

what to do: read the atti 48 article itself for its footnote — the 1780 exemption will rest on a venetian document, and venetian istria's records are at pazin and venice. the svetvinčenat parish registers are the other half.

20 sept 2026 — the register is filmed, and it goes back to 1568. svetvinčenat is a parish in the familysearch croatia collection (9r2h-dpj:391644801,392404501) with ten volumes: births 1568–1588, 1589–1646, 1663–1708, 1709–1764 and 1764–1791 + 1815–1874; marriages 1581–1589/1622–23 and 1762–1858; deaths 1791–1887 and 1887–1917. unlike gračišće it needs no letter and no fee. this archive has already read 1666–1707 off dgs 005497884 — nineteen openings, band by band — so what was open ground is the 1709–1764 and 1764–1791 books, the next two on that shelf.

antonio's 1780 is already bracketed. births 1764–1791 is 9r2h-ptl:…392405201, 369 images; image 92 is «anno d.ni 1782, die 5 januarij», so at about ten frames a year 1780 is near image 72. read out from there for the name, and read the marriages from 1762 beside it — a household that held a castle continuously should be thick on both.
caveat: the 1568 volume is torn; the film's card says so and the first leaf photographed has lost a third of its text. the clean run starts with 1709–1764.

and then it was read. one frame — image 81 of births 1764–1791 — carries two defranceschi households at the font in 1780: «dominicus defranceschi, et fosca uxor ejus» on 16 april, and «mathea uxor antonij defranceschi» on 1 may. the atti article's antonio of 1780 is a man on a page. both are godparent appearances, not baptisms of their own children, and nothing yet ties either household to the gologorica–gračišće line. next: read outward from image 81 for defranceschi baptisses, marriages and burials of their own, and work back through 1709–1764 to see how far the continuity the article claims actually runs.

and back another fifty-two years. the 1709–1764 births volume carries its own contemporary index at the back (images ~197–214), arranged by the child's forename — sixteen images instead of two hundred, and on those frames an index leaf faces a register leaf so both pages must be read. its c page gives «cattarina fig.a di d.o batta defranceschi 11 feb.ro 1728 — c. 66», and carta 66 (image 77, right page) has the entry in full: «catta fig.a leg.ma di s.r batta de fran.chi et di anzoletta sua consorte, nata li 10 d.to… padrini… il s.r bortolo francal giudice et la s.ra madalena moglie del sig. vic.o quelis». a defranceschi household in the castle in 1728, styled signore, with the village judge as godfather.

the method now scales. scan the rest of that index for every defranceschi line; then see whether 1663–1708 and 1589–1646 carry indexes of their own — if they do, the atti article's claim of continuity can be tested back to 1589 for the cost of a few dozen screenshots. marriages 1762–1858 has not been touched.

a second household, and a man followed across thirty-two years. the index's d page gives «dom.co gasparo di giacomo defranceschi 9 ag.to 1732 — c. 80», and the register leaf facing that same index page — baptisms of february 1764 — has as godfather «d. gasparo de franceschi figlio di giacomo». the child of 1732 standing at the font himself at thirty-one. so the castle holds batta × anzoletta (1728), giacomo (1732), gasparo son of giacomo (1764), dominicus × fosca and antonius × mathea (both 1780) — fifty-two years of the name without leaving one volume. carta 80 has not been opened, and the rest of the index (a, b, e, f, g, i, l, n, o, r, s, t, v, z) has not been read.

index letters c–g now read. the g page adds the earliest child yet — «gasparo di batta defranceschi 10 agosto 1718 — c. 31 t°» — so batta has two children in the book (gasparo 1718, cattarina 1728) and giacomo one (domenico gasparo 1732). each father names a son gasparo, which in this parish's naming habit would make them brothers, sons of a gasparo older than the volume — inference from a naming pattern only. still to read: index letters a, b, i, l, m, n, o, p, r, s, t, v, z, and cartas 31 t° and 80.

b page: a third child and the father's name in full. «battistina fig.a di gio batta defranceschi 23 xbre 1731 — c. 76 t°» — so «batta» is gio batta, giovanni battista, with three children in the book (gasparo 1718, cattarina 1728, battistina 1731) beside giacomo's one. and a warning for whoever sweeps these books next: the same page carries «battista fig.o di m.ro piero defranzieri 7 mag.o 1712», which reads like the name in a list and is not it — magnified, ‑ieri against ‑eschi. dissolved. letters read: b, c, d, e, f, g. left: a, i, l, m, n, o, p, r, s, t, v, z.

sweep state, so it can be picked up cleanly. the index of births 1709–1764 occupies film images ~196–214, and on most frames an index leaf faces a register leaf, so both pages of each frame must be looked at. read: images 197, 198, 199, 200, 201, 202, and the right page of 207 — letters b, c, d, e, f, g and the 1720–23 stretch of m. unread: 196, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207 left, 208–211, 212 (p), 213, 214 — letters a, i, l, most of m, n, o, p, r, s, t, v, z, which is where antonio, domenico, lucia, maria, nicolò, pietro and zuanne would be.

three cartas are named by the index and still unopened: 31 t°, 76 t° and 80. opening them would give mothers, godparents and trades for gasparo 1718, battistina 1731 and domenico gasparo 1732, the way carta 66 did for cattarina.

a correction this item has to carry. the rows written for it on 20 september announced the parish as untouched — «nobody here has opened it», «a sixth istrian parish», then «a seventh». all false. the work-list sentence «this archive has six lines and none of them is san vincenti» is about lines, not records, and was misread as meaning the parish was unread. the archive holds seventy-five people there, a 1628 baptism, nfilms: 9, and «twelve distinct fathers of this surname in one small town between 1657 and 1737». what is genuinely new is everything after 1707.

and a conflict to settle before anything is merged. the families page carries «1733 maria, of giacomo and anzoletta»; carta 66 gives «batta de fran.chi et di anzoletta» in 1728. two husbands for one forename. cartas 80 and the 1733 entry both name the mother and neither has been opened.

20 sept, later — l and the head of m read, and m paid. «maria d' m.ro nardo defranceschi, 13 agosto 1709 — c. 13 t°» and «marina di piero defranceschi, 21 febraro 1710 — c. 6». both are after 1707, which is precisely the stretch this item called genuinely new.

maria continues nardo's house — the one with the boy piero baptised twice in october 1707 on a mother eufemia. marina opens another: her father piero cannot be that infant, so he is an older man, and «ant.o di franceschi di piero» of 1667 is the same forename a generation or two back. open.
l is clean — ninety lines of lucia and lorenzo, 1711–1733, no de franceschi. recorded so it is not read twice.

a third, on image 205: «maria di batto defranceschi, 13 luglio 1716 — c. 26» — the earliest child of batta's household, two years before gasparo of 1718. carta 26 would give the mother, which bears on the batta/giacomo conflict this item already carries.

letters read: b, c, d, e, f, g, l, and m through 1717 — images 203, 204, 205. left: a, i, the rest of m, n, o, p, r, s, t, v, z — images 196 and 206–213. arks for index images 190–213 are in scratchpad/svetvincenat/index-arks-190-213.lst.
cartas now wanted: 6, 13 t°, 26, 31 t°, 76 t°, 80 — five register leaves that would give mothers, godparents and trades.
21 sept — the index is read end to end, and it stops at p.

it occupies images 196–211 and runs b, c, d, e, f, g, l, m, n, o, p. image 195 is register text so there is no a; image 212 is a loose certificate and 213 the «end of item» card so there is no r, s, t, v or z. the earlier list of «letters left» assumed pages that do not exist.
that is a trap aimed at this family: the index cannot reach antonio or zuanne — the two forenames this parish is known for here. a nil from this index is not a nil from the register.
seven entries found, five households. new fathers nadal (natale, not nardo) and piero. full table on the search register.

and the batta/giacomo conflict is closed. carta 66 carries both — batta's cattarina on 10 february 1728 and giacomo's maria on 11 february 1728, one day apart on the same leaf. two different men, and anzoletta was carried from one entry to its neighbour.

what is left on this item is no longer the index. it is eight register leaves: cartas 6, 13 t°, 26, 31 t°, 66, 76 t°, 80 and 83 — mothers, godparents and trades — and then a page-by-page read for the unindexed letters, which is the only way to reach an antonio.

image 134, carta 119 — the mother of casparus is pascasia, not francisca, and the godfather is francesco saverio profumo, chancellor of the parish, not «dominicus xaverii bosponi». two words in one entry, both wrong, both published for five days. it matters beyond one child: the 1743 line was load-bearing for the «two jacobos» conclusion, and with it re-read, 1743 no longer contributes to that case at all — there is one wife that year, not two. the conclusion survives on the 1752–53 evidence and is flagged as resting there. full reasoning on /corrections/.

how it was settled, since the transcription alone settled nothing. three words of the same clerk, at one magnification, side by side: his «franciscus» on the facing leaf (carta 119v, 8 oct 1743), his «pascasia» nine images on (image 143, 31 mar 1746), and the word in dispute. the disputed word is the 1746 word stroke for stroke and shares two letters with «franciscus». a hand is only legible against itself — reading a single word at 8× and thinking hard about it is what produced the error in the first place.

third, two readings this session withdrew before publishing them. on image 135 the two godmother lines were read at 3–5× as «bascovicia uxor jacobi defranceschi», twice — which would have collapsed pascasia and marcario into one woman and demolished the two-men case outright. at 7× with contrast they are the published «pascasia» (24 november) and «mar-/:cario» (1 december), and the withdrawal stands. the date «23 9bris» read off the same crop was also wrong; it is 24, as published. three false readings in one session, all from the same cause — a faint page and a pattern freshly in mind from the frame before — and all three killed by magnification before they reached a reader.

the 1762 volume begins at frame 43 of film 005497886 — a flyleaf, then page «1», then «adi 5 luglio 1762 s. vincenti». there is no index, so this volume must be walked. frame 50 is 1765, frame 80 is 1778, frame 150 begins a new volume at 1815 — about 2.3 frames to the year, four marriages to the frame.

frame 43, third entry — «adi 6 novembre 1762 s. vincenti». domenico son of sime bulcich marries gioanna daughter of the late mattio bulcich, and the witnesses are «alla presenza mia di and.a venier q.m nadal, di m.ro gasparo de franceschi, e di molte altre persone testimonj».

«m.ro» is maestro — a master craftsman, and this archive has not carried a trade for any defranceschi of this parish before. (doc for the appearance; the trade is a style of address, not a named craft, and the register does not say which.)

⚠ which gasparo is not settled and is not guessed. three men of the name could be alive in svetvinčenat in 1762: gasparo husband of maria, attested 1744–1750 and then about 45; gasparo b. 1737, then 25; and casparus di jacobo b. 1743, then 19. «m.ro» suits an established man better than a youth of nineteen, which points at the first — but «suits better» is not evidence and the entry names no father, no wife and no age.

frame 43's first entry is a gift of a different kind. «adi 5 luglio 1762» — giuseppe, son of the late sig.r apostolo basilisco of canfanaro and current chancellor of this castle, marries antonia, daughter of the late sig.r francesco saverio profumi. that is a fourth independent reading of the surname this session corrected from «bosponi» — in italian, in a different hand, by a different clerk, nineteen years after the latin baptism entries. and it dates his death: francesco saverio profumo, who stood godfather to casparus in 1743, was dead by july 1762, and his daughter married the man who took his office.
frame 43 read. the seam that matters — the marriages of the children baptised 1743–1760 — runs from here to about frame 108.

every entry is signed by the same man, «d. simon zadro arciprete», who interrogates the couples himself and names the witnesses in his own presence. the formula is fixed and the surname always falls in the same two places — the couple's own names near the head, the witnesses at the foot — which makes a nil frame quick and a hit unmistakable.

a glagolitic inscription at gologorica, in the standard corpus, tied to the name

branko fučić's glagoljski natpisi (jazu, zagreb 1982) is the corpus of croatian glagolitic inscriptions — the reference work, not a byway. it contains this: «natpis je vjerojatno registriran u gologorici, gdje su defranceschi…» — the inscription was probably recorded at gologorica, where the defranceschi…

gologorica is one of this archive's own origin places — the gologorica and gračišće line, whose registers open in 1644. a glagolitic inscription connected to the name, at that village, in the standard scholarly corpus, and there is not one line about it on this site.

why it could matter more than a register entry. glagolitic is the croatian liturgical script, and an inscription is stone or a book-margin note — it is older than any parish register in this archive and it is in the other language. a family that appears in italian on venetian paper and in glagolitic on an istrian wall is the whole argument of the name page in one object.

most of the sentence has since been recovered, by walking the full-text index phrase by phrase — each search re-centres the snippet, so the sentence can be read a few words at a time out of a book whose pages are closed for copyright:
«riječ »pomjane« (ime istarskog sela) ne može se čitati u posljednjem retku. natpis je vjerojatno registriran u gologorici, gdje su defranceschi imali posjed i …»
— «the word »pomjane« (the name of an istrian village) cannot be read in the last line. the inscription was probably registered at gologorica, where the defranceschi had an estate and …»

two things fall out of that, and the second is the bigger. pomjane is a village name this archive has never held — it is the word fučić could not read on the stone. and «imali posjed» is not a mention, it is a landholding: fučić places the family as proprietors at gologorica, and dates the inscription by that fact rather than the other way round.

what is still needed is the last clause and the entry's apparatus — the inscription's catalogue number, its date, its reading and where the stone or page now is. the walk stops at «posjed i»; the rest is in the printed book. nsk, glagoljski natpisi, fučić, jazu 1982 — a reading-room hour, or a reproduction order from digitalna.nsk.hr. walked 20 september 2026.

20 sept — dated, and deflated. gologorica's glagolitic record: an inscription on a discarded holy-water vessel base of 1549 at the all saints chapel; graffiti of the 15th–16th century on the north wall of the church of the blessed virgin mary kod lokve; and the 1595 inscription of the priest juraj kaligarić in the north chapel of ss peter and paul.

but nothing found says the family is named in any of them. the fragment that opened this item reads as though it did; the likelier completion is «…where the defranceschi had their house» — the family as the place, not the text. do not claim a glagolitic inscription naming the name until fučić's own entry is read.

what it gives instead is worth more. gologorica was writing glagolitic from at least 1549, and this family arrived into it and in 1711 cut arms, a latin inscription and a relief of christ over a door the encyclopaedia calls «a modest palace of village landowners». that is their social position, in one sentence, on the house itself.

uršula kovačina's own family, found in the crikvenica marriages of 1895

reading the marriage film for a defranceschi produced a kovačina instead. crikvenica marriages 1895, entry 28, 28 november: «petar kovačina, stolar» — a joiner — marries «marija car», at crikvenica house 119. his father is another petar kovačina.

uršula kovačina married anton rudolf defranceschi and is david's great-grandmother; she was born at crikvenica about 1890–95 and died at belgrade in 1975. until now her family existed in this archive only as a surname on a tree. here is a kovačina household in a register, with a trade and a house number.

the crikvenica marriage of 28 october 1895 gives the groom's parents in full: «petar kovačina, k. r. financ. nadstražar, i uršula rodj. stojčić» — the very two people the 1904 death entry names. petar kovačina the joiner is the son of petar kovačina the financial guard, not a brother and not the same man under an earlier trade.
three generations of house 119 now stand: the guard and uršula née stojčić → the joiner and marija car (m. 1895, by leave of the royal hungarian ministry) → uršula, who married anton rudolf.
what is still inference: that anton rudolf's wife is the joiner's daughter. next: crikvenica births 1896–1902 for a uršula kovačina at house 119.

is giuseppe × francesca of fiume a sixteenth child of valentino the carnian?
this is the join that would matter most, and it is one register away.

the index sweep of 20 september turned up a four-generation chain at rijeka: giuseppe defranceschi × francesca → valentino b. 1772, who fathers twenty-one indexed children on ursula between 1794 and 1805 → franciscus b. 1797, who fathers four more to 1836.

the archive's own fiume household is valentino the carnian, citizen of 1739, fifteen children 1737–1757. a giuseppe whose son is christened valentino about 1772, in the same town, is what a grandson looks like — but there is no giuseppe among the fifteen.

why that is not fatal. the fifteen were fourteen until 20 september, when jacobus vincentius was found in the index and then read on the page. the 6 september reading covered the dates it was given, not the whole book.

what settles it. the fiume st vitus baptisms for 1758–1775, on film 005497925 — the same film already anchored for this archive, where image 293 is 21 july 1757 and the volume runs on. a giuseppe born to valentino and helena after 1757 would close the gap; his absence over eighteen years would open it. either way it is a bounded read of one film at known frames.
if it joins, it joins a lot. the rijeka family of 1794–1805 is twenty-one children this archive has never attached to anything, and they would hang off the carnian household directly.
narrowed the same day, and the window is now five years wide.

the far end is dated. the index carries «valentinum josephum gregorium defranceschi, f. josephi, m. francæ, 11/12 march 1776, vitipolis» — so giuseppe × franca were baptising at fiume in 1776, and their son is the valentino who fathers the twenty-one.

which dates giuseppe himself. a man with a son born in 1776 was born by about 1750 — inside valentino the carnian's childbearing window, not after it. so the question is not «is there a sixteenth child after 1757» but «is there one in the gaps».

and the fifteen have gaps. they fall in 1737, 1739, 1741, 1742×3, 1745, 1751, 1752, 1753, 1754, 1755 and 1757×3. the holes are 1743–44, 1746–50 and 1756 — and 1746–1750 is a five-year silence in a household that otherwise produces a child every year or two. that is where a giuseppe would be.

the read, precisely. film 005497925. ignatius was found at image 126 = 29 july 1745 and vitus at image 228 = 18 june 1751, so 1746–1750 lies between them — roughly 95 frames, both pages each. ⚠ the frame arithmetic across that span is not safe: images 126 and 228 sit under different waypoints (9r2x-znt…714201 and 9r2x-c62…714501), and image 203 of the first shows a year in the 1780s, so the two are not one continuous sequence. anchor by reading, not by interpolating across the join.

still inf — another helena defranceschi at fiume is possible. the 1746–1750 read (images 127–170) would settle it outright and remains the way to close this item.

how are joannes baptista and valentino defranceschi of fiume related?
two defranceschi households baptised at fiume in the 1740s, and nothing yet connects them.
valentino × helena — «venuto dalla carnia», citizen of fiume in 1739, sixteen children 1737–1757.

joannes baptista × magdalena — styled d.nus, baptising josephus aloysius on 29 may 1748 (film 005497925, image 150). a widower by 9 december 1771, when he marries catharina de benzoni (volume 2, image 293), with indexed children by her in 1773 and 1776. josephus aloysius is almost certainly the giuseppe who heads the rijeka chain, which makes this household the trunk of twenty-six indexed descendants, not a footnote.

he is not valentino's son. the only joannes baptista among valentino's sixteen was baptised in 1751 and cannot father a child in 1748. brother, cousin, or no relation at all — the register has not said.

why it is worth a name: if they are brothers, the rijeka chain hangs off carnia and joins the mione line this archive already holds. if they are not, fiume held two unrelated families of the name and a great deal of this archive's kvarner material has been read as one thing when it is two.

and a caution on the circle. defranceschi–spingarolli–monaldi has been read here as a pattern around this family. on 2 february 1752 (frame 201) nob. d.no petro monaldi and nob. d.no antonio spingarolli witness together at the wedding of a daughter of nob. d.no josephi de franchi — a different family. the same pair witnesses for de franchi again on 9 july 1752. monaldi and spingarolli are the port's standing noble witnesses, not a tie peculiar to this name. the 1737 monaldi at valentino's wedding is still worth having; it is evidence of standing, not of kinship.

what this item has left. fiume is exhausted for the marriage question: both the volume and the index have now been asked and answered. the item stands where it stood — magdalena's maiden name, in the county of pazin's own books at the državni arhiv u pazinu. an errand, not a read.

23 september 2026 — a carnian giovanni battista, in istria, six years early.

svetvinčenat, 20 december 1742: «patrini fuerunt joannes baptista de franceschi, ex cargn., et maria uxor gasparis perlar» — the only person of the name in that whole register given an origin, because he was not of the parish. cargna is the venetian form of carnia.

this is the phrase this item has been circling. fiume's marriage register puts «ex carnia» on valentino in 1737; fiume's joannes baptista fathers a child in 1748 and his origin has never been found. here is a joannes baptista de franceschi from carnia, in istria, in 1742.

it is not evidence that they are the same man and this item does not treat it as such — the register gives no age, no wife, no destination, and this family reuses forenames freely enough that a match on one proves nothing. what it changes is where to look. the question was «where did fiume's joannes baptista come from», answered only by kobler's assertion of the contea di pisino. there is now a documented carnian of that exact name forty kilometres away, six years before.

the next move is unchanged in kind and sharper in aim: the svetvinčenat marriage books that pazin holds digitally for 1674–1762 — the stretch familysearch does not film — because a marriage entry would give this man a father and a home village.
