145. done — finished and published david
the living rule, applied to strangers as well as relatives — the rest of the site
the roster has been tested against the dates. the other pages have not, and the answer is david's rather than this archive's.

the rule as published is «living relatives are named and nothing more» — written for family, and applied by a hand-set flag that could only ever catch people david knew to name. on 22 september the roster was tested mechanically instead and eight strangers born 1931–1946 with no death recorded came out; they now print name and place only.
the same test has not been run on the narrative pages, and they hold more. on the diaspora page alone:

the philadelphia family of 1954 — «bosiljka defranceski, born 1918, with brank born 1942 and two younger children, jela and mojuil». brank would be in his eighties; the other two are 80 or younger with no death recorded, so under the standard of 16 october 2026 they are named and not dated (this note carried their birth years until 25 october 2026).
nelida albina, born 9 september 1931 at mercedes — a full date, from an argentine baptism ark.
angelo born 17 may 1927 and eugene born 5 september 1930 at clarksburg, west virginia.
every one of them is out of a public index, and every one is somebody's private business if they are alive.

the decision, plainly. does the rule cover only the family, or everybody this site names? if it covers everybody, the dates come out of those findings and the findings get thinner — the 1954 philadelphia arrival is largely made of those dates. this archive has not made that call and will not make it quietly, because unlike every other question here it is not about accuracy. the roster fix was done because the notice at its head made a claim that was untrue; extending it further changes what published research says, and that is david's to decide.
22 september 2026 — decided, by david, the same day it was put to him: the rule is about his relatives, as written.

«family only.» a person this site names from an already-public index keeps the dates that index publishes — withholding them here makes nobody more private and takes the substance out of the finding. the 1954 philadelphia arrival, the clarksburg brothers, the dignano household in the refugee papers: all keep their dates.

three roster rows were put back the same hour. giordana, maria and claudio of the dignano household had been held as possibly living for about ninety minutes; they came out of the arolsen collections, not the family tree, so under the decision they keep what the file says. five rows stay held — nelida albina, feliciano, richard, assunta maria and daria — because those are people in david's own tree, and that is exactly who the rule is for.

what survives from the exercise, and is worth more than the eight rows: the test itself. a hand-set flag cannot express «this person may be alive» — it can only record who somebody remembered to mark. living-audit.py now runs the arithmetic first and prints anyone born within ninety-five years carrying neither a death nor a flag. today it prints none. when the next import adds one, it will say so before anybody has to notice.
146. done — finished and published this archive
73 hosts the archive links to and never names in its bibliography
check:sources is running on every build as of 22 september, and the first thing it says is that this archive cites seventy-three hosts it has never described.

among them: cemla.com (the argentine arrival index), collections.arolsen-archives.org (which produced the dignano household), arhinet.arhiv.hr (the croatian state archives' catalogue), archives.isula.corsica, archivesenligne.meurthe-et-moselle.fr, digitalna.nsk.hr, data.onb.ac.at, croatianroots.com, chan.archivesnationales.culture.gouv.fr.

why it matters on a site whose whole argument is provenance. the bibliography is where this archive says what a source is, what it gave, and where it is weak. a host that appears only as a bare link in a table is a citation with no account of itself — the reader is asked to trust a domain name.

the work is to write them up, not to delete the links: each needs a line saying what the body is, what this archive got from it, and whether it is free, paywalled or behind a bot check. ten of the eighty-five already listed have no way to reach them at all and say so, which is the standard the seventy-three should be brought to.
the check reports and does not fail on this, so the number is a ratchet to drive down rather than a blocker.
done, 27 september. check:sources no longer reports a single host. the count went 73 → 57 → 41 → 31 → 0 across four passes, and the bibliography went from 92 entries to 155.

the material was mostly already written, and copying it would still have been wrong. forty-six of the seventy-three hosts already had entries on the research register saying what was asked and what came back. a generator turning those into «this archive has gone to it n times, see the register» would have passed the check and produced exactly what the item complains about — a citation with no account of itself. so they are written, one at a time.

five of the seventy-three were never sources, and giving them their own lines would have satisfied the check while misdescribing the archive. sg30p0.familysearch.org is familysearch's own image server; data.onb.ac.at is anno's permalink host; and artgallery.yale.edu, armchairgeneral.com and purl.org appear only inside the credit field of a wikimedia commons image record — they are a licence's attribution chain, not bodies this archive consulted. each now sits on the entry of the source it actually belongs to. geneanet had two entries proposed and kept one: one body, one line.

what the pass turned up, beyond the writing. žminj's own municipal history describes the «carnielli» of istria — men who spent part of each year back at agrons near ovaro and married only girls from there — which is the pattern this whole archive is trying to document, stated locally, and pointing at the same comune the antenati survey reached independently. udine's notarile antico b. 2979, the protocols of gio. batta franceschi, notary at mione 1737–1783, is the best unread paper for the carnic question and needs a letter rather than a search box. and the museu da imigração at são paulo is not blocked but broken — every query returns http 500 — so the brazilian arrivals are unread rather than absent.
147. done — finished and published this archive
36 groups of rows that may be one person recorded twice — and 57 that are certainly not

minting the frozen person ids on 23 september reported 48 collisions on name and birth and death, and this archive called them «probable duplicates» in writing without looking at one of them. looked at on 27 september, that was wrong twice over: there are 33 groups, not 48, and not one pair is identical — every group differs in place, source or line.
splitting them by place separates the two halves cleanly.

17 groups / 41 rows sit in different parishes — a pietro of 1734 at svetvinčenat, another at bale, five more at vodnjan; an antonio of 1753 dead the same year at rijeka, at spalato and at vodnjan. these are not duplicates and must not be merged. a one-name study that did not produce them would be hiding something: the same saint's day, the same naming custom, the same decade, eight parishes.

16 groups / 34 rows share a name, dates and place. those are the candidates, and the source pairs say why: burial + myheritage, household + read, grave + myheritage, household + myheritage — one person entered once from a record and once from the live tree is the classic shape. the list: cristoforo 1824 vodnjan (3), domenico 1803 vodnjan (3, all read), bortolo 1756 šterna, leonardus 1766 gologorica, pietro and domenica of vodnjan, franz 1822, giovanni 1829 and stefano 1831 vodnjan, julius 1833 rijeka, giovanni 1845 ližnjan, joanna 1848 gologorica, angelo 1851 pola, matteo 1874 poreč, giacomo at broken hill.

nothing has been merged. each one is a judgement about two records and a person, not a string comparison, and the id minting deliberately froze both rows rather than guessing — a merge performed by a script is a person deleted by a script. domenico of 1803 at vodnjan is the one to start with: three rows, all from read, all one town.

corrected within the hour, and the correction is bigger than the finding. the count above — 33 groups, 16 candidates — was produced by grouping on the exact name string. in an archive whose founding premise is that the name varies, that is the wrong key.

«antonio de franceschi» and «antonio defranceschi», both born 1704, both at svetvinčenat, one from a record and one from the live tree, were two separate groups — because of one space. they are the plainest duplicate signature in the file and the check walked past them.
folding the surname the way this archive's own namefold does — stripping de/di/del, collapsing every spelling of the name to one token, dropping married names in brackets — gives:
93 groups, 228 rows colliding on folded-name + birth + death
36 groups / 75 rows share a place as well — the duplicate candidates
57 groups / 153 rows are in different parishes — coincidence, and correct

twenty-six candidate groups were invisible to the exact-string check, among them mattia 1669, zuana 1688, batista 1692 and antonio 1704 all at svetvinčenat; a run of vodnjan people from 1816 to 1833; and pairs where one row carries a married name in brackets — anna defranceschi and anna defranceschi (baichin), catarina and catarina (kisdaris), veneranda and veneranda (demarin).

still nothing merged. but the size of the job is twice what was published an hour ago, and the reason it was understated is the same fault as everything else this week: a check keyed on something other than the thing it was checking.
adjudicated, 27 september — and the archive was already holding the proof.

thirty-six groups share a folded name, a birth year, a death year and a place. the question was always which of them are one person written twice. the answer was in the ark field: where two rows carry the same familysearch ark, they are the same record entered twice, and that is proof rather than resemblance. nothing had ever compared them.

eighteen pairs are proven duplicates by identical ark — mattia 1669, zuana 1688, batista 1692, antonio 1704 and maria maddalena 1825 at svetvinčenat; domenica maria 1816, domenica michiela giovanna 1818, stefano matteo 1822, pasqua 1825, lucia 1826, pietro 1828, giovanni 1829 and maria 1833 at vodnjan; pietro antonio 1810 and cattarina 1811 at paluzza; aloysius 1790 at vižinada; natale mattio 1816; franco at rovinj. in every one, a register row and a myheritage row describe one child.

seven pairs carry two different arks and are not proven either way — mariam 1632, bortolo 1756, anna 1799, elisabetta 1810, gregorio 1822, julius 1833, giacomo d. 2012. four of these pair a 6ybr/6ybt ark against a 6b47 one, which looks like two collections indexing one event — but looking like it is not being it, and each needs the register.

seven have an ark on one side only and rest on circumstance: joannes baptista 1752 and joanna 1848 at gologorica are identical in every field and are almost certainly a double insert; marianna 1809 is the mione child buried in the 1810 «morti» at about a year old; veneranda is the same wife of antonio demarin twice.

ten pairs are distinct men and women whose rows say so in their own notes — the three cristofori of vodnjan, the fiume shoemaker giovanni q.m pietro, the two elene of svetvinčenat, the two giacomi, and the three peters. these must never be merged, and the folded key would have merged them.
full table: data/duplicate-adjudication.json. nothing is merged yet.
the eighteen are merged, and not one address moved.

deleting a duplicate row would delete a url, and these pages have been published and linked since 23 september — which is the whole reason the person ids are frozen and never derived from a birth year. so the duplicate keeps its page and the page says what it is: a pointer to the person, with the ark that proves it. everything the duplicate held was folded into the surviving row first — twenty fields, including every myheritage id, so nothing now exists only on the page that points away.

a pier in rijeka carries the name, and nobody has said which man it honours
there is a pier in the port of rijeka called «de francescijev gat», and this archive does not know who he was.

what it is. arca adriatica, entry 13548 — «pristanište zichy / de francescijev gat», «pier zichy / pier de franceschy». a stone-block pier in the rijeka port basin, between the istrian pier to the east and the vienna pier to the west: east face 150 m, west face 134 m, south face 80 m, about 6 m alongside, with stairs down to the water and rail-mounted cranes — a 300 kn heavy-lift on the east side, two 30 kn mobile cranes on the west. it is working port infrastructure, not a monument.

what the source is. arca adriatica is a virtual museum of adriatic maritime heritage built under an eu interreg italy–croatia project — primorje-gorski kotar county, malinska-dubašnica, the kvarner county tourist board, the house of batana at rovinj, cervia, cesenatico, san benedetto del tronto, ciheam bari and ca' foscari university of venice. an institutional register, not a hobby page — and it classifies the pier as immovable material cultural property.

⚠ what this archive already had, and what it still lacks. this is not new: /searched/ has carried it since september under «defranceschi bridge, rijeka», which established that there is no bridge — there is a pier, formerly mol zichy, and two things the register itself does not say: the first iron-and-concrete building in the port went up on it in 1882, and the first electric light in rijeka was lit on it — by zipernowsky, with lamps borrowed from the torpedo factory. what no source says is who the de franceschi was. until today that question sat in a search log with no worklist row behind it, which is why it has not moved.

searched 28 september 2026 and nil, with the terms named: on the portal stare hrvatske novine — franceschijev → 0, francescijev → 0, molo de franceschi → 0. zichy → 1025, but that is the hungarian magnate family in political news and not the pier. the portal's runs mostly end about 1925, so if the renaming is italian-era or post-1945 it would not be there at all.

the shape of the question. «de francescijev» is an italian surname put into a croatian possessive — a name inherited and adapted, not one coined in croatian. that points at the name arriving before the croatian period, i.e. under hungarian fiume (when it was zichy) or italian fiume, 1924–45.
⚠ a third candidate, found the same afternoon — and it was already in this archive's own files.

ferencz defranceschi, révkapitány — port captain — in the service of the fiume maritime authority, to 1857. the hungarian parliamentary pension schedule of 1872 credits him with 42 years, 10 months and 5 days of public service and a pension of 1,050 forints from 1857, which puts him into state service about 1814; the later accounts style him m. kir. révkapitány, royal hungarian. his daughter francziska was still drawing a 65-forint orphan's kegydíj in 1900.

why this is the strongest of the three. a pier in fiume harbour is port infrastructure, and the man it honours would most naturally be a port official of fiume — not an istrian historian and not an unidentified shipowner. ferencz is a documented port captain of that exact authority, serving through the decades before the harbour was rebuilt, and the pier's own hungarian-era name, mol zichy, sits in the same administration.

⚠ and it is still not evidence. *no source yet found connects ferencz to this pier or to any pier. the case is entirely circumstantial — the right office, the right port, the right era — and this archive has spent today learning what happens when proximity is mistaken for proof. ⚠⚠ two rendering defects found in the frame pipeline — a black frame that looks like a blank page, and a mislabelled frame that overwrote a good one
both found in ten minutes of the medulin births book, and both would have put false readings into this archive.

1 · the black frame. the render snippet drew document.images[0] to canvas without waiting for the image to load. after a navigation the image is sometimes not yet decoded, and the canvas then yields a pure black page of perfectly normal dimensions — 28 kb, right aspect ratio, nothing on it. frames 8 and 10 came back that way and would have been logged as read and empty.
caught only because the left and right halves were byte-identical — 28,217 bytes each. two halves of one opening are never byte-identical.

the fix: the snippet now awaits img.onload when !complete || !naturalwidth, and throws image not loaded if naturalwidth is 0, so the failure is loud rather than silent. the standing check: after every decode, compare the two halves' byte sizes; identical means refetch.

2 · the mislabelled frame. a batch's first action re-rendered the frame the browser was still sitting on, and the output was labelled as the next frame — overwriting a good capture with a duplicate of its neighbour. caught by the same size check: f10-r and f11-r both 912,167 bytes. the standing check: md5 every half-page and assert no duplicate hashes across the whole book, not just within a frame.

this is the same family as the ližnjan crop that cut every page and the two «blank» medulin openings that were full pages. the rule it keeps proving: an absence produced by this archive's own tooling is not an absence in the record, and the only defence is a check that fails loudly rather than a page that looks plausible.

⚠⚠ the subdomain migration: five traps, found by five archives in one evening — and one of them was mine to cause

this archive moved to its own domain and then told four others how to do the same. the recipe was wrong in two places, and the sister archives found both. recorded here because the knowledge is worth more than the move.

1 · the cname trap. these sites deploy by actions uploading site/dist. github writes a cname when you set the domain in the ui, but any later actions deploy that does not carry one silently detaches the custom domain. it must live in site/public/cname.

2 · base "" not "/", and then base stops being a key at all. every consumer derives it as (import.meta.env.base_url || "/").replace(/\/$/, ""), which yields "". but that was only half of it. socialhead identified the archive by ring.archives.find(a => a.base === base). that was unique while every archive was a project site. the moment a second archive moved, five entries shared base "" and find() returned the first — this one — so falco, blažević, lerena and d'arcy were each building with this archive's name, accent and canonical. a wrong canonical is the one seo error that de-indexes the page it sits on in favour of the domain it names. that was my error: base was a key only by accident, my move made it non-unique, and my recipe told four archives to do the same. fixed by the blažević session in kit e275c14 — kit/lib/ring.js whoami(base) narrows by origin, import.meta.env.site against each entry's url, falling back to the old answer when site is unusable. any archive pinned below e275c14 must re-pin.

3 · the tell i gave was the one field that lies. i told everyone to verify og:site_name. it is masked: socialhead takes site from astro.props first — const name = site || me?.name — and the layout passes the archive's own title, so og:site_name reads correct on a completely broken build. found by d'arcy and confirmed by falco and lerena, each independently. verify on canonical, og:url and theme-color, which have no prop behind them.

4 · never hand-edit package-lock.json. found by lerena. the lock entry carries both resolved and integrity. a string-replace of the sha updates resolved and leaves integrity as the old tarball's hash, so npm validates against the stale hash and serves the old package while every pin on screen shows the new sha. rm -rf node_modules and npm cache clean --force do not help. edit package.json by hand; let npm write the lock: npm install "github:daviddef/thearchivekit#<sha>". ⚠⚠ a correction to this item, same evening. it first said this archive's sed-based re-pin was safe because its resolved is a git+ssh ref and npm re-clones those. that explanation is wrong. the lerena session's lock resolved the same way and npm still served stale content against the old integrity — the re-clone is cache-dependent, not guaranteed. so the rule is unconditional: edit package.json and .kitpin by hand, never the lock, and let npm install "github:owner/repo#<sha>" write resolved and integrity together. this archive's pin happened to be genuine; it was not genuine for the reason first recorded here, and the only thing that actually established it was checking the installed code — whoami in the installed socialhead, ring.js on disk, five base-"" entries in the installed archives.json.

5 · grep, then read each hit. found by falco, who had 18 hits and only three real hrefs: fifteen were github.com/daviddef/thefalco repository urls — correct, the repo keeps its name — and one was prose inside a september correction describing a bug whose symptom was a /thefalco/ url. rewriting that would have falsified the archive's record of its own history. this archive has the same shape: two surviving href="/thedefranceski strings, both inside code comments describing bugs that happened, both deliberately left standing, with a note in url.js telling the next session not to "correct" them.

⭐ and a sharper rule than "keep them", from the lerena session: does the comment describe or direct? a comment that describes a bug that happened is a record and must stand, wrong address and all. a comment that directs the next session — «internal links carry the /thex base» — has become false instruction, and leaving it means the next edit reintroduces dead links. lerena rewrote theirs to state the rule now, the rule before, and the date it changed: the history is kept without keeping the instruction. this archive's two are descriptive, so keeping them was right — but the test is describe-vs-direct, not simply "it mentions the old base".

the pattern across all five: a check that looks at what you wrote rather than at what is actually there will pass on a broken build. the cname you set in a ui, the sha in a lock file, the og:site_name fed by a prop, the grep hit you never read — every one of them reports your intention back to you.

6 · the ordering trap — and it is live right now. my recipe said: i push the config change, you set the domain in github, and the gap is about ninety seconds. the gap is not ninety seconds. it is however long it takes a person to click. and during it the archive's old address serves a site whose every internal link is root-relative and therefore 404s on that host.
measured on the live sites this evening:
thelerena — 113 internal hrefs, 0 based, canonical pointing at lerena.defranceski.com, which does not answer. live broken.
thedarcy — 249 internal hrefs, 0 based, canonical pointing at darcy.defranceski.com, which does not answer. live broken.
thefalco — 308 internal hrefs, 308 based. sound — it has not deployed the move.

⚠ a correction to my own figures, from the lerena session. i first wrote 36 and 72. those were distinct paths — my command piped through sort -u — and i reported them as though they were totals, with the words «every internal link». the totals are 113 and 249. both answers were true of different questions and i labelled one with the other's meaning. lerena's broader pattern, href="/[a-za-z0-9], is the one to use: mine missed uppercase, digits, deeper paths and anchors as well as collapsing repeats. the conclusion did not move — 0 based is 0 based — but a number in this archive has to mean what it says.
theblazevic and thedefranceski — both have their pages cname set and both are correct.
the difference between the broken two and the sound two is one setting in a repository, and only david can set it.

so the ordering in the recipe was wrong — and so was my fix for it. i wrote: «binding the domain first costs nothing, because github keeps serving the previous build until the next deploy.» that sentence is false. i stated it as fact, put it in this record, sent it to four sessions, and then acted on it: i bound five repositories on it.
⚠⚠ what binding actually does: it 301-redirects the project-pages url onto the custom domain. found by the luwinski session and then measured here on the five i had bound:
theluwinski daviddef.github.io/theluwinski/ 301 -> luwinski.defranceski.com
thefalco daviddef.github.io/thefalco/ 301 -> falco.defranceski.com
themazza daviddef.github.io/themazza/ 301 -> mazza.defranceski.com
thebooyzen daviddef.github.io/thebooyzen/ 301 -> booyzen.defranceski.com
and on the host it sends them to, the old build's own paths are gone:
/theluwinski/ = 404 /thefalco/ = 404 /themazza/ = 404
/thefalco/favicon.svg = 404 (so: unstyled, no icon, every link dead)
hrefs still carrying the old base, now all 404:
thefalco 308 · themazza 205 · theluwinski 89

so binding does not quietly stage anything. it moves every existing visitor onto an origin where the build being served does not fit. three sites that were working — falco, mazza, luwinski — were live-broken by my hand, unstyled, with every internal link 404ing, and i had told david and three peer sessions they were «bound and serving old builds, ready for step 4». they were not ready. they were down.

⭐ the real finding, and it is the luwinski session's words: the gap is not eliminated by reordering, it is only moved. push the base change first and the old address serves root-relative links that 404 there. bind first and the old address 301s to a host where the based build 404s. both orderings break the site whenever base is not "/". what closes the window is not an ordering at all: step 4 must follow step 2 as closely as a person can click, and whoever does it must know the window is live-broken, not merely stale. a session that is not ready to push within the minute should not be bound yet.

restored the same evening: cname cleared on all five, all five serving 200 again with styles and favicons, back to where they were before i touched them. the bindings go back on only as the immediate precursor to each archive's own push.

⭐ and the two things a cname does not do, from the d'arcy session. public/cname in the artifact does not bind the domain — d'arcy checked the pages api mid-gap and cname was null with the file sitting in the deployed output. the file keeps a binding from being torn off by a later deploy; it does not create one. my recipe read as though it did both.

⭐ one step still open on every archive, also from d'arcy: the certificate can be issued and https_enforced still false, in which case plain http:// serves 200 instead of redirecting and the 301 off the old github path lands on http:// — two addresses for every page, on the archives whose canonical we just spent a day getting right. only david can tick it.

⭐ a correction owed to the d'arcy session. their move deployed during what i had asked them to hold, and i was ready to write that down as a workflow quirk — a repository that deploys despite a hold. it was not. they held, waited for e275c14, re-pinned, rebuilt, verified canonical / og:url / og:site_name / theme-color / cname / sitemap in a scratch build, and then pushed deliberately. the tell was in my own measurement and i read past it: the canonical i saw said darcy.defranceski.com, which is the fixed build — had it escaped during the hold it would have said archive.defranceski.com, which is the very thing they refused to publish. writing "that repo deploys despite a hold" would have sent the next session hunting a bug that does not exist.

the whole of trap 6, twice over: i reasoned about what github does instead of measuring it, and the second time i had already shipped the reasoning to four archives. the first version of this entry's own warning applies to it — a check that looks at what you wrote rather than at what is actually there will pass on a broken build. i never ran curl on a bound project url until a peer told me to.

⭐ a last measurement, and it undermines single readings of any of this. after i cleared the five bindings, the luwinski session checked and found luwinski.defranceski.com still answering 200 with the old build — 75,716 bytes, right title, right canonical — while the api said cname was null. at the same time david had falco.defranceski.com on screen returning 404. same operation, seconds apart, opposite results. minutes later all five returned 404 and the old project urls were back to 200 with no redirect: the edge had gone on mapping the host header after the binding was removed, and then stopped.
so "the api says null" and "the hostname stops serving" are not the same moment — and the gap is not a stable state you can measure once and file.

if the edge lags on the way out, assume it can lag on the way in. which means «i bound it and the new host answers» may also be a reading taken at the wrong moment — the same shape as the error above, arrived at from the other side. untested, and deliberately recorded as untested: the next archive to move is where it gets tested, with somebody watching.

⚠ 7 · and my all-clear was wrong too — the same fault, a third time in one evening. having broken five sites and cleared the bindings, i checked them and reported: «styles.css 200, favicon.svg 200 — you are back exactly where you were.» the falco session measured its own and found it live and unstyled.
daviddef.github.io/thefalco/ 200
its own href="/_astro/index.b2krsy4p.css" 404 ← pulled out of the served html

ids ever published 1592 · current 1592 · disappeared 0

lerena's distinction is the one that matters: a frozen ledger prevents reordering, and my test asks the reordering question. renaming is different. where a key is derived from a name, a rename does not remove anything — it strands the old address and mints a fresh one beside it, so the count stays flat while a page goes dark. their own sweep found 22 stranded keys of 707, five resolving to nothing, two of them dead since 23 september.
a set difference of zero over a frozen ledger says nothing whatever about addresses the build derives.

and this archive has already been bitten by it once, tonight, and i did not connect the two: the dead /who/ links earlier in this session were exactly this — addresses that had moved out from under themselves, invisible to check-links because the rename had updated every reference, leaving the build internally consistent and externally broken. i fixed them by rebuilding the dossiers and treated it as a forgotten build step rather than as a class.

a hazard i introduced and the luwinski session caught before it did any harm. recorded because the next person to read the migration recipe will hit the same fork.

what i wrote. sending the corrected subdomain recipe round the estate, i noticed that kit/data/archives.json holds seven entries — defranceski, falco, blazevic, booyzen, lerena, darcy, mazza — and no luwinski. i told that session its options were «(a) you are simply missing an entry — then adding one is step zero» or «(b) you do not use the kit ring at all». i did at least say not to add itself without asking david. that caution is the only reason this is a note and not a correction.

what is actually true. luwinski was removed from archives.json on 16 september, at david's explicit instruction. the reason is recorded in that archive's base.astro, above its head tags: the luwinskis are not a branch of the same family, and a ring of sibling links to seven defranceschi-estate archives had no business on those pages. the comment there even names the exact trap — «putting it back to get a favicon would put luwinski into every other archive's ring, which is the thing that was objected to» — and that session says the comment stopped it making the same mistake this morning for an unrelated reason.
an absence from a shared file is not necessarily a gap. it can be a decision, and the decision can be the whole point.

so: the ring is seven and stays seven. luwinski uses sixteen kit components but none of the ring ones — no socialhead, no siblingarchives, no jsonld; its base.astro states site, accent, origin and line as local constants and writes its own head tags. verified by that session by grepping its whole site/src: four mentions of archives.json, all four prose. traps 2 and 3 of the migration list therefore do not apply to it at all.

the general lesson, which is the same one this archive has been learning all evening in a different key. my step zero read a shared file, found something missing, and proposed to supply it. that is the identical fault as the pin that names the right commit over the wrong code, the og:site_name fed by a prop, and the deduped link count reported as a total: acting on the shape of the data rather than on what it means. the file did not need fixing. it needed reading alongside the decision that produced it — which was written down, in the one place a session touching that archive would see it.

now pomer's books, read end to end on 13–14 october 2026, hold a defranceschi household of their own — tomas, magdalena buich and three children from 1843 (house 5) — and a second, of an antonius from ližnjan, in 1886. lucia is tomas's daughter, and her children number nine, 1866–1884 (the index gave six, from 1870), with six dead before nine. the place page, the daughters'-villages line, the register and the ližnjan page now say so; the list has four parishes.

13 oct 2026 maria defranceschi's mother was magdalena buić, not «magdalena davić» — and the row was named for the misreading material

was that maria defranceschi of pomer, who married petrus kirac at medulin on 30 july 1874, was the daughter of the late tomas defranceschi and magdalena davić — read from the genitores sponsae column of that marriage on 13 september 2026 and carried for a month as a named person with her own page.

now the mother is magdalena buich — buić. four entries in the pomer registers write it unprompted: «buich» in the marriage of 16 august 1843, in lucia's baptism of 1844, in michele's of 1847 and in maria's own of 1852; «buić» in lucia's marriage of 1866. the 1847 scribe writes «buich» again in the patrini column of the next row, so the reading is settled against his own pen. the medulin cell, reread, says the same: four glyphs before the accent, a two-lobed b — against the same scribe's single-lobed d in «de-franceschi», one cell to its left — and «davić» needs five. ⚠ how it went wrong, because it will again: the first read was one cell, at one magnification, with no second construction, of a capital that this hand makes in two shapes. the repo rule says a hand is only legible against itself; that comparison was done after the pomer books made it necessary, and not before. the person is unchanged and her page keeps its address — the id is frozen and still says «davic» — but the name on it, in the story, and in the log is buić. her husband and her daughter maria were correct throughout; so was the parish.

12 oct 2026 «the fleet is wrecked in a storm» — drawn as documented on the crete lane, and not in any source on the evacuation material

the crete lane on the lines diagram carried a node reading «wrecked · 1669 — candia falls; morosini's galleys take them off and the fleet is wrecked in a storm», and the lane's confidence was documented.

⚠⚠ five sources on that exact event were read on 12 october and not one mentions a wreck. the closest thing to an eyewitness account — the relation the grand master of malta sent to the viceroy of sicily, published by floristán in 2025 — describes the opposite: a negotiated embarkation stretched over twenty-two days, the grand vizier granting extension after extension while his army waited «con una quietud y una paciencia extraordinaria», and finally offering to forward anything left behind to suda. about 12,000 people left candia. jackson (1887), ortalli & schmitt, pérez negrete's chapter on the war and the ca' foscari thesis on the defence of candia are all silent on a wreck too.

⚠ and this archive's own spine never said it. on /seget/ the candia stop reads «the twenty-one-year siege ends, and the venetians take their people out» — which is exactly what the sources describe. the drawing and the spine were telling two different stories and only the drawing called its version documented.

juraj dobrila was bishop of trieste and capodistria from 29 may 1875 until his death in january 1882 — he had left poreč–pula in 1875. a bishop makes a canonical visitation of his own diocese, so his signature in this book says plainly which diocese it belonged to.

did mione has fifty-nine registers of its own, digitised, free, and open — and this archive has been saying for months that they were not online. the name search was the wrong door. antenati says so itself: «non tutti i nomi sono ricercabili perché solo una parte dei registri disponibili è stata completamente indicizzata» — only part of the holding is name-indexed, and tolmezzo returns nothing by surname. the other form, /search-registry/, browses the registers themselves. ovaro: 271 registers, all held by the archivio di stato di udine, in two fonds — stato civile napoleonico (173) and stato civile italiano, comuni afferenti al tribunale di tolmezzo (98). the series break down by village: · mione (oggi frazione di ovaro) — 59 registers · ovaro itself — 144 · lenzone — 9 · chialina — 8 · cludinico — 8 · and nine more series behind them by type: morti 61, matrimoni 49, nati 39, matrimoni pubblicazioni ed opposizioni 31, matrimoni allegati 28, and eighteen more. by year they run from 1806 through 1871 and beyond — so both the napoleonic registration and the italian civil registration after unification. each result carries its own shelfmark and a «vedi il registro» link — for example registro 1806, nati, segnatura 12995, agrons con cella; 1806, matrimoni allegati, segnatura 185, lenzone. tolmezzo has 452 registers on the same portal, and the other carnian communes are there too. this is the same material familysearch holds and keeps behind «image restricted». the italian state archive has published it itself, and published it open.

did the mione allegati had already been read, and the page that says so is this archive's own. mione 1806 (segnatura 185, six images) is a single marriage file: ignazio di prato of chialina × giacoma de' franceschi of mione, september 1806. it holds the groom's latin baptism of 13 december 1777 — ignatius, son of iacobus son of the late leonardus de prato — the bride's parish certificate of 25 may 1789, and the consent of the groom's mother catterina, widow of the late gio: giacomo di prato, who could not attend the signing. every one of those facts is already on the carnia page. mione 1808 (segnatura 12984) is catalogued as matrimoni, allegati and is not a marriage file at all. it is one image: a covering letter of 17 february 1809 from the municipalità of mione to the civil tribunal of first instance at udine, transmitting the previous year's registers. no names of this family, and no marriage. muina 1806 (segnatura 185, ten images) is the one still worth opening. only its cover sheet was reached: antenati's session then returned «400 bad request — size of a request header field exceeds server limit», which is the cookie growing across a long sitting rather than a block. it clears with a fresh session. and a correction made before it was published. on the first pass this reader transcribed the mione 1806 certificate as «giovanna, daughter of giacomo q. gio: batta, born 1785». all three were wrong. zoomed properly it reads giacoma, daughter of osvaldo q. gio: batta, born 1789. it was caught by checking the archive before writing, which turned up the same certificate already transcribed correctly — and had it not been checked, this archive would have gained a daughter, a father and a birth year that do not exist.

i said dubrovnik was too thin to be a group. it is a household. correction

did this archive said asked whether the rijeka, dubrovnik and bakar groups could each have a page, this archive answered that dubrovnik could not: «it's four people, and the 1829 row has four names in a parent list, which is exactly the tabular-register trap that burned us on francisca. giving it a page would dress four records as a group.» what is true the caution was right and the conclusion was wrong. the trap was real. the answer was to apply the rule, not to walk away from the records. applied, the four resolve into one household across forty-two years. the 1829 row is a marriage, not a birth: four parent names is the signature of the austrian tabular register, whose columns run sponsi, sponsae, genitores sponsi, genitores sponsae. read that way it says matteo persich, born 1829, son of antonio persich and teresa martecchini, marrying a daughter of pietro defranceschi — and the other three records are that couple's children, baptised at dubrovnik in 1853, 1863 and 1871. the children confirm the reading. the first son is antonio, his father's father. the daughter of 23 december 1863 is cattarina teresa vittoria maria, his father's mother. that is the ordinary adriatic naming order, and it is independent of the row that was misread. the lesson is not about dubrovnik. a rule this archive learned in order to avoid a false positive was used instead to avoid looking — which costs more than the error it was guarding against. and two smaller things fell out of it: the surname is martecchini, not martechini — forebears finds exactly one person of the archive's spelling in the world — and it is ragusan, not venetian, which is where this site had filed it on the strength of how it looks. how it happened
found a claim taken back
the atlas was drawing a fifth of what the archive knows, and this site holds two different gračišćes correction

did this archive said the atlas carried 52 hand-written pins and had done since it was built. the dek said «every place this archive can put a document in», which was not true: the roster names 266 place strings attaching 1,440 people to the ground. what is true rebuilt from the roster, the map holds 154 places and 955 people. three things were wrong rather than merely missing. · one town was being drawn several times under different names. almissa and omiš are the same place; so are fiume, vitipolis and tarsatica, which is why the first rebuild put rijeka on the map three times. historic and italian forms are now folded onto the town they name. · this archive holds two different coordinates for gračišće, seven kilometres apart — one in places.json, one in atlas.json. neither was flagged because nothing had ever compared them. the heavier pin keeps the ground and the builder now refuses to draw one name twice. · seventy-three entries name something that is not a town. thirteen say «österreich», five «austria», four «italy»; and four each say «santa maria assunta», «immacolata concezione» and «assunzione di maria santissima» — church dedications written into a place field. those are left off the map and are a data error to be cleaned, not a place to be pinned. how it happened found by building the thing properly rather than by checking it. nothing compares a gazetteer against itself until something has to draw both.
«642 volumes open at page one» — the carnian ones do not open at all correction

did this archive said published this morning: «985 more volumes now open at page one», counting 343 dalmatian and 642 carnian. the carnian half was described exactly like the croatian half. what is true the images of the entire udine collection are restricted. the viewer answers «image restricted — access is typically determined by local laws or the custodian». tested at colza, comeglians and paluzza; all three are shut. the croatian volumes — istria, the kvarner and dalmatia — open normally, which is how the mistake survived a spot-check: the one volume tested end to end that morning was tinjan, and tinjan is croatian. so the honest count is 652 volumes that open and 642 that are addressable but gated. the link is still worth having — it names the exact volume and its register number, which is what a reading-room request needs — but it is a catalogue entry, not a document. how it happened found within hours, by going to do the thing the page promised: reading colza to settle whether ovaro's registers are filed under it. the page said the volume was open; the volume was shut. a link was tested for the wrong country and the claim was written for both.

did this archive said published hours earlier, on finding familysearch's udine images restricted: «settling ovaro now means a family history center, an affiliate library, or the archivio di stato di udine itself — not an afternoon at a screen.» what is true the archivio di stato di udine has published them itself, on antenati, free and open. ovaro has 271 registers there and fifty-nine of them are mione's, catalogued under its own name. the first correction was right about familysearch and wrong about the world. one vendor's gate was mistaken for the state of the record. the reason it was missed is worth keeping: antenati was searched by name, which returns nothing for tolmezzo, because only part of the holding is name-indexed. the portal says so on the results page. the registers were one form away the whole time. how it happened found by retrying a source this archive had twice written off — once as «403s both browsers», once as «needs a reading room» — and by reading the failure message instead of accepting it.

did this archive said published this afternoon: that mione's fifty-nine registers are open on antenati and that «this archive has been saying for months that they were not online». what is true the carnia page already said it, in as many words: «the archivio di stato di udine has digitised the napoleonic civil registers of the comune di mione — fifty-nine volumes… and publishes them openly on the antenati portal.» it had already read the 1809 and 1810 birth books and published four households out of them. what was actually new this afternoon was narrower and should have been stated as such: the 1806 volume had not been read, and it holds a fifth household and a generation above it. the error was mine and it was the ordinary one — i searched the web before i searched the archive. a site of twelve hundred pages will tell you what it already knows if you ask it first. how it happened caught within the hour, by grepping this archive's own data before writing up the register act.

did nothing, under any spelling, in 167 years of the queensland register. defranceski returns zero. defranceschi returns zero. franceschi returns two, and neither is ours — joseph franceschi, who married menichina amedei in 1877, and jacques ange franceschi, a corsican-french name, who died in 1989 to albert franceschi and marcelle. (the two-word «de franceschi» appears to return a hundred rows, but the space defeats the index's exact-match flag and it falls back to fuzzy matching — the results are «de ruyter de wildt» and «de jong de silva». it is not a holding.) and the null is the expected one, which is why it is worth writing down rather than worrying about. this family's only two queensland deaths are mario de franceschi in 2013 and antony de franceski in 1999. the index closes deaths at 1996. both fall outside it by design, not by absence — so this search could not have found them, and finding nothing else means there was no earlier queensland branch. the arrival in brisbane is as recent as this archive says. nobody of this name registered a birth, a marriage or a death in queensland before 1996.

the lesson from the hungarian material applied to the austrian press: the surname as two words, as one, and in the family's own spelling search

did this archive has been searching anno with one hand. anno has a clean json endpoint behind its search page — /anno-suche/rest/search/simple?query=…&from=n — which returns, per issue, the paper, the date, the place of publication, the language and the number of hits inside that issue. run three ways, the surname gives: · «de franceschi», two words — 950 issues. · «defranceschi», one word — 722 issues. this is the only form this archive had ever used. · «defranceski», the family's own spelling — 28 issues, never searched here at all. «de franceski» gives 4 more. the forms overlap but do not contain one another. roughly a quarter of the austrian press coverage of this surname was invisible to every anno search this project has run. who is in it. proximity search — matching words standing within three of each other rather than anywhere in the same issue — sorts it out: carlo de franceschi, 42 issues; camillo, 5; and enrico, 392 — an opera singer working in vienna and salzburg in 1930 and 1931, who is not ours, is now named on the namesakes page, and who accounts for two fifths of everything anno holds under this name. anyone who searches it will hit him first. and a reading queue, which is the useful part. of the 950, 185 issues are istrian or adriatic — il giovine pensiero of pula, l'istria, il popolo istriano, il giornaletto di pola, l'eco di pola, la fiamma, naša sloga, the pester lloyd, and the journal des österreichischen lloyd. those are the papers that would print this family, and they are now listed by date and by how many times the name appears inside each issue. the single best of them is the oldest. journal des österreichischen lloyd, 7 september 1848 — nine occurrences in one four-page issue, published at trieste and vienna. the austrian lloyd's journal carried shipping movements, quarantine and port notices; 1848 is the year ferencz defranceschi was running the quarantine station at martinšćica. that issue has not been read, because anno's page viewer at data.onb.ac.at sits behind a cloudflare check which this archive does not answer.
found anno — austrian newspapers online, searched properly for the first time
working the same seam a second day: variant spellings, and the almanacs of the hungarian crown search

did three offices, a successor state, and a correction to one of this archive's own authorities. the surname searched as one word gives 263 hits; searched as two words it gives another 60, and they are a different set. most of those 60 are hungarian scholarship citing carlo de franceschi's l'istria as an authority — fest aladár's 1891 study of the uskoks and the venetians in the history of fiume leans on him on page after page. that is worth knowing in itself: carlo was standard reading in hungarian historical writing within a decade of his death. the hungarian kingdom's own directories then gave three people: · valentin defranceschi, 1835 — passualist in the polizey-behörde of fiume. the passport officer of a free port, listed among the city's patrician office-holders. the earliest office this archive can put the name in, and a civil one. · ferencz defranceschi, 1848 — főnök of the st francis quarantine institute at martinšćica, the lazaretto of the kvarner, with a clerk, a surgeon-teacher, a chaplain and four guards under him. the same page records the harbour captaincy at buccari as vacant. · «dr defranceschi», 21 december 1918 — south slav representative, addressed by the austrian state chancellor over the removal of the austro-hungarian archives to yugoslavia. hhsta, neues politisches archiv 397. and a correction to the shelf. vjesnik 18 (zagreb, 1916) carries milko kos, publishing twenty unpublished vienna parchments expressly to «fill out and in many places correct franceschi's conclusions on the genealogy of the lords of pazin». camillo de franceschi's storia documentata is cited across this site; on the medieval lords of pazin it must now be read beside kos. kos also quotes camillo admitting he was «unfortunately not in a position to establish a complete and certain genealogy» — which is the best sentence anyone in this family has written about this work.
found hungaricana — the spelling «de franceschi» with a space, and the hungarian kingdom directories
the surname against hungarian state records, because fiume and bakar were hungarian crown land search

did the kvarner name is a family of habsburg maritime officials, and this morning's inference is now corroborated. earlier today this archive read «francisci defranceschi regii» on an 1849 bakar baptism and inferred, from that one word, that the name held a royal office. it does. hungaricana — free, unblocked, full-text — holds the hungarian state's own paperwork for exactly these two towns, and nobody here had ever opened it. · anton defranceschi, 1827, drew the «bauriss der zu buccari befündlichen aerarial salz-einnehmer und controlors wohnung» — the ground plan and section of the imperial salt-receiver's and comptroller's residence at buccari, which is bakar. manuscript, 56 × 45 cm. national archives of hungary, t 62 no 1642, out of e 96 tricesimalia 1827. · ferencz defranceschi, révkapitány — harbour master — of the fiume maritime authority. the parliamentary pension schedule of 1872 gives him 42 years, 10 months and 5 days of public service and a pension of 1,050 forints from 1857. forty-three years back from 1857 puts him into state service about 1814. · francziska defranceschi, «defranceschi ferencz révkapitány árva leánya» — the harbour master's orphan daughter — drawing a kegydíj of 80 forints, renewed in three-year terms, in the state accounts of 1888, 1892, 1894, 1898 and 1900. so her father was dead by 1888 and she was still unmarried and on the state's charity twelve years later. · valentin defranceschi, k. k. kriegs-marine, marine-direktion at pola, in the militärschematismus of 1854, 1855 and 1856 — and valentin is the one forename that recurs through the rijeka households, fathering there in 1742–57 and again in 1794–1805. · julius defranceschi, k. u. k. kriegsmarine — 196 entries across the rank and distribution lists from 1894 to 1909, by then linienschiffsleutnant. a whole naval career, free, page by page, not yet worked. · theodor defranceschi, k. k. landwehr, 1909. and it re-reads the saints. this morning this archive noted that nine of twelve children born to valentino and ursula at rijeka carried nepomucena or nepomuc, and read it as habsburg dynastic piety. that is half of it. john of nepomuk is the saint invoked against drowning, the patron of bridges and of men who work on water. in a harbour-master's town, in the hungarian crown's free port, a family that names nine children for him is not only being loyal. it is being careful.

the whole surname against american arrivals, 1820–1958 — the first time this portal has been used here partial

did a ship's name, and a large clean negative. ellis island manifests have been used by this archive for years — but through findmypast, familysearch and an aggregator, never through the foundation's own free database. it turns out to have a plain json endpoint, no account and no paywall, and to cover seven arrival collections rather than one, including new york, passenger lists 1820–1920 — the castle garden decades that the ellis island 1892–1925 set cannot reach. the ship. the 1882 household that this archive already had from italians to america — giov b. 1846 with angiola, romeo, marietta and teresa — now has a vessel against it: all five records name the st germain. their ages at arrival are on the record too: thirty-six, five, four, three and one. the st germain was a compagnie générale transatlantique liner on the le havre run, which is worth knowing about a north-italian family in 1882, although the departure port field on these particular records is blank and this archive is not asserting it from the ship alone. the negative, and it is the useful part. one thousand four hundred arrivals of this surname were read, of which 429 record a last residence. exactly two of those 429 are istrian — g. pedena and g. gallignana, which are antonio and albina on the conte rosso, 9 september 1922, already on this site. everything else is veneto and friuli: castelgomberto and cornedo in vicenza, ponte nelle alpi in belluno, pederobba in treviso, and sequals, lestans and pinzano in pordenone, with torrington in connecticut as the american end of that chain. and the spelling that is not there at all. defranceski, de franceski, defrančeski and defranzeschi each return zero records in the entire database. the -ski spelling — the family's own — never crossed to america under that form.

testing michiela de franceschi fu giuseppe against the marriage register partial

did the test is not settled, and the reason is worth more than the answer would have been. the plan was to find the marriage of michiela de franceschi × domenico giachin — a marriage entry names both of the bride's parents, so if her mother is lucia tromba she is giuseppe's daughter. her first child is baptised in 1817, so the marriage should fall about 1815–16. what was established. the register opens «liber copulatorum in ecclesia sancti blasii adignani, annus 1815», first entry 12 october 1815. the fourteen de franceschi marriages this archive has already catalogued from it run 1817–1832, and none of them is this one. so the marriage lies either in the register's first fifteen months or before the book begins. images 172–174 were opened; the 1815–16 entries have not been scanned surname by surname, and that is a bounded job, not an open one. what was found instead, and it changes the reading. there are at least three different michiela de franceschis at vodnjan in this period: michiela fu pietro — wife of andrea palin, house 24, dead before january 1831. michiela di cristoforo q.m gio: maria — mother maria luigia manzin, born about 1800, married in the register. michiela fu giuseppe — wife of domenico giachin, house 532, alive in 1833. michiela is not a rare name in this family; it is one of its commonest. that is exactly why the inference has to rest on the patronymic and not on the name — and it is a good argument for not having claimed the giuseppe link outright.

did thirty-seven entries, no de franceschi. but this stretch is where the parish register stops being only about the parish. entry 73, 24 april 1833, «caserma militare» — not a house number but the barracks. «giorgio carl… soldato della compagnia xxi, battaglione iii, reggimento xxii principe leopoldo, entrò nel 1808» — dead of an inflammation of the bone «in parte per caduta accidentale», in part from an accidental fall. enlisted in 1808 and still serving in 1833: twenty-five years a soldier. that is the third appearance of the xxii prince leopold regiment on this film — page 164 entry 11, page 172 entry 8, and now this. the regiment was quartered at vodnjan, and the parish buried its men and its men's children. entry 71, 22 april, house 280. «la sig.ra elisabetta nata klettner fu ignazio, vedova del sig.r francesco kneipf, nata … in moravia» — a moravian gentlewoman, dead of apoplexy and buried on the 24th. taken with the gunner giorgio sabotz and the man from a district in the friulian provinces, that is four outsiders in about a year, each given more biography by this register than most of the town's own children get.

january – february 1833, entries 4–44 found

did forty-one entries. one de franceschi — michiela fu giuseppe, at entry 41, written up separately — and two things that only appear if you read the book in order. house 109, in seven months. on 24 july 1832 a child of marchio and eufemia bergamasco is entered as «n. nato morto» — born dead, unnamed. on 28 july his twin, giacomo, follows him. on 10 february 1833, entry 37, the father goes: «marchio figlio delli furono giugali marco benaco fu giacomo e giustina cosseani fu pietro, era ammogliato con eufemia bergamasco d'antonio», dead of malattia acuta di petto, house 109 — the same house. eufemia buries two sons and her husband inside seven months. no index would ever have put those three entries together; they share no name and no date. only the house number and the order of the book connect them. the regiment again. entry 8, 10 january 1833, is a child of the «battaglione 3.o reggimento xxii principe leopoldo» — the same regiment named at entry 11 on page 164. the prince leopold regiment was quartered here, and its soldiers' children are buried in this parish under their fathers' units rather than a house number. also on these pages: «vajuolo naturale» — natural smallpox — entered as a cause for the first time in this stretch.

did entry 41, 20 february 1833, house 532. «giacomo figlio del fu dom.co giachin q.m giacomo e di michiela de franceschi fu giusep. giugali» — dead of idrotorace, with confession, communion, extreme unction and the indulgence. a seventh woman of the name, and she is not the michiela already known. the one this archive holds is michiela de franceschi fu pietro, wife of andrea palin at house 24, dead before january 1831. this is michiela de franceschi fu giuseppe, wife of domenico giachin at house 532, and still alive in 1833 — it is her son who dies, and her husband who is already «del fu». the father's name is the interesting part. this archive holds exactly one giuseppe de franceschi: 1758 – 14 february 1830, house 324, × lucia tromba q.m cristoforo, dead suddenly and without a priest. he was in his grave three years when this entry was written, which is what «fu» requires. if this michiela is his daughter, she stands beside don stefano the priest, pietro the ploughman, cristoforo the weaver and maria francesca as a fifth child of that household. that is an inference and is marked as one. what the register says is that her father was called giuseppe and was dead. it does not say which giuseppe, and the name is not rare. the baptism register would settle it. her son's age is written in a column this viewer will not render legibly and is left unread rather than guessed.

did forty-eight consecutive entries, no de franceschi. recorded because a family archive that only writes down its hits cannot tell you how thoroughly it has looked. two things on these pages are worth keeping anyway. page 161 carries a bishop's visitation note in a different hand: «vidi die 5.ta 9mbris 1832 — antonius, ep.us parent.» — i saw this on 5 november 1832, antonio, bishop of parenzo. the diocesan inspection, signed in the book itself. and every page closes with the parroco's own signature, «joannes tromba sac. th. d.r parochus» — the priest this archive already knows from the marriage register. 1832 opens with twin girls. entries 2 and 3, both 1 january 1832, both house 422: domenica and maria, «figlia gemella di gio. batta manzin q.m lorenzo e di bonetta manzin di venier giugali» — twin sisters, dead the same day.

did entry 84, 19 may 1831, house 456. «pasqua figlia di pietro de franceschi q.m pietro, e della fu maddalena francin di gio. giugali», dead of tosse convulsiva — whooping cough. «della fu maddalena» — of the late maddalena. the register itself confirms the march death nine weeks later, in the ordinary course of writing down her daughter. that is the check this archive wants and rarely gets: the same book, corroborating its own entry, without being asked. three deaths in that house in five months. pietro, eleven, of scarlatina on 15 december 1830. maddalena, thirty-nine, of consumption on 14 march 1831. pasqua, of whooping cough, on 19 may 1831. her age is not recorded here — the column is written small and sideways and could not be read with confidence at the resolution the viewer allows, so it is left unread rather than guessed.

did entry 48, 14 march 1831, house 456. «maddalena francin di giovanni, moglie di pietro de franceschi q.m pietro», cattolica, femmina, aged 39, dead of tisi polmonare. the sacraments column is full: conf.e, com.e, extr. unz.e, ind. in art. mortis. she is the mother of the eleven-year-old. house 456 is where, on 15 december 1830, «pietro figlio di pietro de franceschi q.m pietro e di maddalena francin di giovanni giugali» died of scarlatina — and the two entries name the same couple in the same words. the boy dies in december; his mother dies ninety days later, in the same house, of consumption. the sacraments columns set side by side are the whole of it. for the boy: «senza assistenza spirituale per la malattia repentina» — no priest, the illness was too sudden. for his mother, dying slowly of tuberculosis: every rite there is. aged 39 in march 1831 puts her birth about 1791–92, and about 27 at the boy's birth in 1819.
