the search register has been hiding forty-three per cent of itself correction

did this archive said that the search register listed every source this archive had examined — «197 sources examined», as its own header said. what is true it was showing 112 of them. eighty-five rows were on the page's data file and not on the page. the cause is dull and the consequence is not. the template grouped rows by an outcome field and knew five values — yield, partial, nothing, blocked, pending. over a year the rows had been written with twelve: 70 of them say «hit», seven say «miss», and the rest are «found», «note», «mixed», «correction», «clean». anything the template did not recognise was silently dropped. no error, no gap, no warning — the row simply was not drawn. so the register understated the work by a factor approaching two, and did it in the one place on this site whose entire purpose is to say honestly how much has been looked at. a page that exists to record negative results was itself losing results. and three of the eighty-five were written today, by me. the hungaricana searches and the anno search were all filed as «found», published, and were never visible. i found them missing only because i went back to check that a published finding had actually appeared — which is a habit this archive should make routine rather than occasional. fixed two ways: the twelve words are now mapped onto the five outcomes, and any value that still is not recognised falls into an «other» group rather than disappearing. it is no longer possible for a row to be invisible. 197 render. how it happened
i gave the harbour master's daughter the wrong allowance, off the line above correction

did this archive said that francziska defranceschi, the port captain's orphan daughter, drew a kegydíj of 80 forints a year in the hungarian state accounts of 1888 onward. what is true sixty-five. the 1888 account reads, in order: «2. marussig gentilének, marussig ferencz volt fiumei révkapitány árva leányának … évi 80 frt kegydij adományoztatott. 3. defranceschi francziska, defranceschi ferencz révkapitány árva leánya … évi 65 frt kegydijban részesült.» the eighty belongs to the woman on the line above. this is the same mistake this archive has made before and warned itself about: reading the adjacent line. it caught the vodnjan mother out of an index list and the zadar parents off a tabular marriage row, and it has now done it in a printed hungarian budget where the two entries are numbered 2 and 3 and sit one under the other. the lesson does not get learned once. the error was found the same day by going back to read the whole page rather than the search snippet — which is also the only thing that ever finds it. and the re-read gave two things the snippet had not. the 1894 account styles him m. kir. révkapitány — magyar királyi, royal hungarian — the exact counterpart of the regii written beside the name at bakar in 1849. and the 1898 account says why francziska was on the list at all: «tekintettel vagyontalanságára, munka- és keresetképtelenségére», in view of her destitution and her incapacity for work or earning. how it happened
the households list counts one omiš family twice correction

did this archive said that this archive held 112 reconstructed households, among them francesco franceschi × maria de caralipco at omiš, 1854–1877, seventeen children, and francesco franceschi × maria de caralipeo at almissa, 1856–1873, seven children — as two separate families. what is true they are one family. almissa is simply the italian name for omiš, and the two mothers' surnames differ by a single letter that two indexers read differently. six of the seven children in the smaller household are the same named individuals as in the larger one. the error was mine and it was structural: the household builder keys on the place string as the index writes it, so a town recorded in two languages becomes two towns, and a wife spelled two ways becomes two wives. nothing was invented — but a family was doubled, and the archive's household count is one too high. it is not only a subtraction. the seventh child, carlo paolo michele maria franceschi, appears in the smaller household and not in the larger. merging them does not take a family away; it gives this one an eighteenth child. the duplicate is now flagged in the data and named on the page; the merge itself is held back because the household ids are referenced in several places and a silent renumbering would be worse than the duplicate. how it happened
i corrected a note that was right correction

did this archive said that the working notes' line — «55 suppressed charts to review by hand» — was stale and wrong, and that the true figure was 763 of 1,056 dossiers with no pedigree chart: «wrong by a factor of fourteen, in the direction that makes the job look nearly done». what is true the note was right and i was measuring something else. a dossier has three possible states, not two: 238 have a chart drawn. 55 have candidate households that the date gate rejected every one of — a chart suppressed, which is exactly what the note said and exactly the pile that needs reviewing by hand. 763 have no household link at all, so there is nothing to suppress and nothing to draw. 55 is the review queue. 763 is not a backlog; it is the shape of the evidence. how it happened v.get("ptree") was read as «has a chart». it is not: the builder returns a ptree object carrying none: true when it found candidates and the gate threw them all out. conflating «suppressed» with «absent» turned a precise note into a false alarm — and the alarm was published in a commit that was itself about numbers going stale. the audit now prints all three states separately. being loudly right about an error is not the same as being right, and the check i built to stop numbers rotting produced a rotten number on its first day.
twenty-four households with the parents the wrong way round correction

did this archive said twenty-four of this archive's 112 households named a de franceschi woman as the father and her husband as the mother. «father: michiela de franceschi · mother: domenico giachin». forty people's roster entries said things like «domenico giachin — named as mother on 2 baptisms». what is true every one is inverted. the women are the mothers; the men are the fathers. all 24 are de franceschi daughters married out — which is why the error clusters exactly where it does. how it happened the households built from the familysearch index take the two parent names the index returns and assign them by position, not by sex. where the de franceschi parent was listed first — which is what happens when the mother is the one carrying this archive's surname — the pair went in backwards. so the bug bit precisely the people this archive is worst at tracking. the whole vodnjan argument is that «the surname keeps its sons and loses its daughters»; twenty-four married-out daughters were in the data and the data had them down as men. found while testing something else entirely — chasing whether one michiela de franceschi fu giuseppe was a daughter of the giuseppe this archive already documents. the check that found it is now in scripts/audit.py and runs on every publish: a female given name in the father field. it would have caught this the day it was introduced.
counted four candidates and could name three correction

did this archive said that four look-alike candidates had been examined at full magnification and given up on this film — «q.m francesco», «di francesco», «da francesche», «and one more». what is true there are three. «nicolò sussani q.m francesco» and «antonia palin di francesco» on image 560, and «bonetta da francesche» at page 164, entry 21. there is no fourth. how it happened a running tally kept in the head rather than in the file. the sentence was written, the fourth could not be named, and it went out anyway with «and one more» standing in for evidence. small, and caught within the minute — but it is the same shape as the mistake that put 1,952 on this site: a number written before it was counted. the count of things given up is exactly as much a claim as the count of things found, and this archive's whole argument is that it keeps both.
full-text result counts that were a year, not a count correction

did this archive said that familysearch's full-text search returned 1,952 results for gologorica, 1,719 for gračišće and 1,885 for defranceschi — and, noting how implausibly alike those three numbers were, that they «have not been tested» and should not be trusted. what is true every one of the three is wrong, and the real figures are not close. gologorica returns 19. gračišće three pages. crikvenica fifteen. ližnjan two. defranceschi returns about 9,900 — five times what was published, not a fifth of it. and vodnjan returns nothing at all: the croatian name post-dates every record in the corpus, which uses dignano — about 12,200 of those, most of them the other dignano, in friuli. how it happened the number was scraped with a loose pattern — ([0-9,]+)\s*results — off a page whose visible text ends «… border crossing records 1924-1952\nresults per page:». it matched a year out of a collection title. «1,952 results» was a border-crossing collection's end date standing next to the words «results per page». what makes this worse than a scraping bug: the page said the numbers looked wrong and published them anyway. three unrelated searches returning numbers of the same size was called «the shape of a number that counts something other than what you think» — and then the one check that would have settled it, look at how many results are actually on the page, was not run. it takes one request. flagging a doubt is not the same as resolving it. a figure you have publicly called untrustworthy should not be in the sentence at all. the finding underneath is unharmed and is better than it looked: 19 hits for gologorica is a set small enough to read end to end, which is exactly what makes the village sweep worth doing.
a correction that never reached the data file correction

did this archive said the families page described the southern-istrian family as «southern istria — pula, fažana, ližnjan», resting on the name being «in the pula registers from 1667». what is true those entries are from the svetvinčenat register, dgs 005497884, and the parish carries the surname from 1657. pula holds ten register entries of the name, only three accepted, and four of them are spelt bellulovich francessich — a different surname. how it happened the correction itself was made days ago and published on the lines chart. it never reached families.json, which went on asserting the original claim in its own title. this is the second time in this archive that a published correction has failed to reach the data behind it — the first cost forty-four people their parish. found by auditing the chart's place labels against every place string in the register, the roster and the households, which is a check that should run on a schedule and does not.
numbers i gave david before checking them correction

did this archive said that pula had «about fifty records» and that krk, kastav and oprtalj were towns missing from the lines chart. what is true pula has ten in the register. the fifty came from adding register, roster and households together and folding «pola» into «pula» — three different kinds of row counted as one kind. and krk, kastav and oprtalj are not gaps at all: the surnames there are franceschini and francetich, different stocks of a different name. how it happened caught before publishing, by recounting per source and printing the spelling column beside each place. the lesson is the one this archive keeps meeting from a new direction: a place count means nothing until you have looked at what surname is actually standing in it.
publishing this archive's own method back to it as a discovery correction

did this archive said that forty-five per cent of the indexed records carry no town, that the film number in each record is the way to a parish, and — presented as the day's lesson — that a reel can carry more than one parish, so the film is «a fast first pass and not an answer». what is true all three were already on this site. the parish-map section of the same page says the index «usually gives no parish… every persona carries the ark of the image it was read from, the service turns that ark into a dgs film number, and the catalogue names the film's parish». and the correction entry above it, from 9 september, already ends: «the reliable route is to resolve records to their film and read the catalogue's item list — remembering that a film can carry more than one parish.» the 45% is a measurement of something this archive had already stated qualitatively. it was written up as though nobody here had noticed. how it happened by not reading the page being added to. four sections were appended to /istria-sweep/ in one afternoon without the existing parish-map section being read first — the same page, eighty lines further down. what is actually new, and it is narrower: q.fathersurname and q.mothersurname are honoured when either is the sole name term, which the reference note said was impossible and which took the pool from 954 records to 1,619; and resolving a record through its image ark to the book waypoint is finer than film-to-catalogue — it settles a two-parish reel automatically instead of requiring somebody to remember to check. the measurement that 110 of 112 records on film 005497893 are the second parish's is new. the idea is not.
«the earliest the surname is indexed anywhere in istria: labin, 1615» correction

did this archive said that an aloÿsius defranceschi appears at albona in 1615 — «sixty-four years before the mione headmen's list, and eighty-five before the date carlo gives for his family's arrival». carried as one of three key findings of the september sweep, pinned on the atlas, and used as the outer bound of the family's presence in istria. what is true three later measurements cannot find it. the rebuilt sweep on the same page — written precisely because the first method matched a truncated field and stopped early — gives labin 1789–1892. the by-image test of 13 september gives 1826–1866, and six of labin's fourteen indexed hits are franceschich, francescich, francocich, which are not this family. and this archive's own register, 1,508 rows each carrying the id the service returned for it, holds no 1615 labin row; its only 1615 row is an andriana franchini. so the 1615 exists in one place only: the table built by the method this page has already declared broken. and the source of the number has since been found. the only aloÿsius defranceschi in any harvest on disk is born 1790, son of mathæus defranceschi and osvalda labinaz or dominj — a vižinada household. the gasparo de franceschi named beside him is in none of the data. and labin's filmed volume list contains a book called «deaths (umrli) 1615, 1585-1649». so the entry was a man from the wrong parish dated two centuries early, a man who does not exist, and a date taken from a shelf-list instead of a record. it is withdrawn, not merely disputed. what stood instead: rovinj 1619, then svetvinčenat 1628. both are in the register, both have an image behind them, and the second was read off the page the same morning. (superseded on 11 november 2026: the svetvinčenat baptism book holds the name in godparent cells from 1605; see the correction.) how it happened by checking a load-bearing number against the archive's own data instead of against the page that first published it. the check cost one grep. it was prompted by writing a new place page for labin and finding nothing in the register to put on it. withdrawn the same day after searching every harvest file for the name rather than only the published tables. that search cost one grep too, and should have been the first thing done rather than the second.
ten women shown as born in the year their own children were being baptised correction

did this archive said a birth year for each of ten married-in women — «b. 1822» for lucia bonassin, «b. 1816» for maria malusá, «b. 1841» for maria dorliguzzo, and seven more. what is true none of those is a birth year. each woman is the mother of a household whose first child is baptised in that very year, or in one of the years she was already bearing children. lucia bonassin «b. 1822» is the mother in «gio maria de franceschi × lucia bonassin, 1822–1831». maria malusá «b. 1816» is the mother in «pietro de franceschi × maria malusá, 1816–1824». anna defranceschi (voran) «b. 1865» is the mother in a household running 1857–1865. the year is the first time she appears in the record — the baptism of her eldest known child. it was carried into the roster as a birth. nobody is born in the year their own child is born. all ten now show the year as a first appearance, with the birth recorded as unknown. how it happened found by asking why the pedigree gate was suppressing fifty-five charts. the gate was doing its job: it refuses a parent who would be under twelve at the first birth, and these women were failing that test because their data said they were nought. the charts were the symptom; the birth years were the fault. and one rule was tried and withdrawn inside the same hour. generalising it — any person whose recorded birth is less than twelve years before a household they parent — «corrected» 113 rows, including an antonio defranceschi born 1897 attached to an 1825 household and a josip defranceski born 1947 attached to one from 1890. those are not bad birth years; they are name collisions, which this archive proved the same morning when «maria defranceschi» turned out to be thirteen women in thirteen parishes. the rule assumed the match was right and the year wrong; in 103 of 113 cases it was the other way round. reverted, and narrowed to the one case where the name form itself identifies a wife — «maiden (married)» — which no father and son can share.
«gio batta de franceschi and zanetta gravisi, parents of the groom» correction

did this archive said that the šterna household ran gio batta de franceschi × zanetta gravisi, and that their son bortolo's marriage stood behind two entries in the book of 1723–1820. published on the morning of 13 september, on the strength of the index's four names. what is true zanetta gravisi is bortolo's wife, not his mother. the index lists groom, groom's father, bride and bride's father; this archive read four names as two couples. the page reads: «bortolo figlio del q. gio: batta de franceschi dalla cargna… ha contratto legitimo matrimonio coll'ill.ma sig.a zanetta gravisi figlia dell'ill.mo sig.r marchese nazario della villa di cepich di questa pieve», 12 november 1777. and there was never a second marriage. the other «record» is a modern archivist's pencil finding-aid slip filmed with the book, which the index counted as a separate entry — and which independently confirms every word of the reading. how it happened by opening the two images instead of reasoning about the index rows, which is what the same page had already said was the only reliable move. the correction was published the same day as the claim. it is also the most valuable correction this archive has made, because going to the page produced the sentence the whole project has been missing: an istrian de franceschi whose origin is written down.
ten more birth years that are first-appearance dates correction

did this archive said birth years for ten people who are parents in a vodnjan household — «b. 1817» and «b. 1819» for a pietro de franceschi whose household runs 1816–1824, «b. 1822» and «b. 1830» for a domenica whose household runs 1817–1832, and so on. what is true each year falls inside the span during which that household was baptising children, and each person is a parent in it. they are first-appearance dates. twenty such years have now been corrected across the site. how it happened the earlier pass used only the name form «maiden (married)», which is safe but narrow. this one adds two tests that let the rule reach further without repeating the morning's mistake of blanking 113 good years: the places must agree. a row at draguč matched to a household at rijeka is a name collision, not a bad year — 59 of 121 candidates failed this and were left alone. the year must fall inside the childbearing span. place agreement is not enough on its own, because vodnjan recycles the same six christian names across generations: a pietro de franceschi b. 1858 sits at the same place as a pietro whose household ran 1816–1824, and he is a grandson, not a bad date. eighteen were skipped on this test, all but three of them at vodnjan. ten survived both. the rule is now narrow enough to state: a person who is a parent in a household, at the same place, whose recorded birth falls within the years that household was bearing children, has a first appearance recorded as a birth.
«francisca defranceschi × antonius cerneca, nine children 1831–1846» correction

did this archive said that the largest of the married-out daughters had nine children by an antonius cerneca between 1831 and 1846. published this morning as the head of the lost-daughters queue. what is true her husband is joannes bergamo, and they are not children. the svetvinčenat marriage book after 1815 is a ruled table with four printed column headings — sponsi, sponsae, genitores sponsi, genitores sponsae — and the index flattens all four parents into one list. «vincentius bergamo, son of joannes bergamo and francisca defranceschi, marries euphemia cerneca, daughter of antonius cerneca and joanna ferrara» arrives as one row of five names, and this archive read names three and four as the husband. the five rows are the weddings of four sons — joannes 1831, dominicus 1836, vincentius 1840, antonius 1846 — not nine baptisms. she remains a married-out daughter; that part of the queue's logic is unaffected. every husband in this archive inferred from an o list on a post-1815 marriage register is now suspect. how it happened by opening the page. the column headings are printed in capitals across the top of every opening and settle it in one look. the same morning's own text had already said that the reliable move is to read the register rather than the index; it took until the afternoon to apply that to a row this archive had itself put at the top of a queue. bergamo is also the point. kandler lists the carnian families at sanvincenti as defranceschi, lupieri, fiorencis, fabris, crosilla and bergamo — so this is two carnian houses intermarrying, which the wrong husband had hidden.
«a bartolo buried in july 1819, which is bortolo himself at the end of it» correction

did this archive said that the šterna burial of july 1819 closed the life of bortolo de franceschi, the man who came from carnia and married zanetta gravisi in 1777. what is true the entry names parents — «bartolo de franceschi, of gio: batta de franceschi and maria». a burial that names a father and mother is a child's. this is a grandson carrying the grandfather's name, in the second gio: batta's household. bortolo's own death has not been found. how it happened by reading what the index row actually said rather than what the page's narrative wanted. the same hour's work also found that šterna's registers begin in 1667, not 1723 — a composite first volume of 207 images — and that it holds no de franceschi at all, which is the negative result the carnia entry predicts.
every mother one generation too deep on the ancestor chart correction

did this archive said an ancestor chart published a few hours earlier, in which hedviga blažević was drawn as ivan defranceski's mother, uršula kovačina as anton rudolf's mother, anna kalanj as josip's mother, maria fernasar as antonio's, and francisca salomon as giovanni battista's. what is true each of those women is the wife of the man she was drawn under, not his mother. the whole maternal side of the chart was shifted by one generation. a wife belongs above her children, not above her husband — anna kalanj is anton rudolf's mother, not josip's; hedviga blažević is the mother of the living generation, not of the man she married. rebuilt so that each couple's children sit below them: i. defranceski ← ivan (1925–1995) and hedviga blažević; ivan ← anton rudolf and uršula kovačina; anton rudolf ← josip and anna kalanj; josip ← antonio and maria fernasar; antonio ← giovanni battista and francisca salomon. giovanni battista's own mother is now a wall, because she is genuinely not named anywhere. how it happened by printing the tree as a list of [role] pairs instead of looking at the rendered chart. on the screen the error is nearly invisible — every box is in a plausible place and every name is right. on one line of text per person, with «father» or «mother» against each, it is obvious in a second. the lesson is the same one this archive keeps relearning in a different costume: a shape that looks right is not a check. the descent view built from the same data was correct throughout, which is why the error survived — the two views disagreed and nobody had asked them to agree.

did a third wife named in the parents' generation. 17 july 1832, house 325: domenico de franceschi, forty-six and a widower, «figlio delli furono giugali pietro de franceschi e martina civico q.m domenico, vedovo della q.m veniera de rocchi fu onorato», marries a widow. because both parties are widowed the clerk writes every name out, and it yields a couple this archive did not have. martina civico joins michiela zambaletta and domenica manzin as the third named wife of that generation. whether her husband pietro is the same man as the pietro q.m domenico who married domenica manzin is left open — this parish has produced four pietros and two cristoforos, and only a patronymic settles it. don stefano witnesses a nineteenth time, 16 november 1832.
found vodnjan, liber copulatorum — dgs 005497894, images 211–212
late 1832 into 1833 found

did a second son, and a correction. 1 december 1832, house 282: «domenico figlio di pietro de franceschi q.m gio: maria e della q.m veniera francin q.m domenico», aged 29 — the same parents as the 1821 bridegroom, so a younger brother of gio: maria, born about 1803. and on 26 january 1833 the priest's signature reads «d.n stefano de franceschi, de parochi lic., li congiunse e benedisse nella chiesa parrocchiale» — he married them himself, which retires this archive's repeated claim that he was never the officiant. the claim was true of 1819–1832 and was stated as though it covered a book that was still sixty openings from being read. what survives is better: he acts «de parochi lic.», by the parson's licence, the same formula as the 1816 baptism.
found vodnjan, liber copulatorum — dgs 005497894, image 213

did giuseppe de franceschi's death bracketed. the weaver is «cristoforo de franceschi di giuseppe» in march 1818 and november 1828, and «fu giuseppe» on 12 february 1833 — so the father of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver died between november 1828 and february 1833. also don stefano officiates a second time, in the church of the b. v. del carmine, and pietro de franceschi fu pietro witnesses a third time. and a reading withdrawn the day after publishing it: «de par. lic.» is the register's standard formula for any deputising priest — the next entry uses it of don pietro bradamante — not the personal arrangement this archive took it for. vodnjan is running marriages through at least four churches: the parish church, san martino, the b. v. del carmine and the b. v. della trovesa.
found vodnjan, liber copulatorum — dgs 005497894, image 214
1833: the brothers' own household found

did the household of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver opens. 27 july 1833, house 324: «maria francesca, figlia del fu giuseppe de franceschi q.m pietro e di lucia tromba q.m cristoforo», marrying at twenty-eight. that gives giuseppe a father (pietro), a wife (lucia tromba) and a fourth child — and confirms his death inside the bracket his sons' patronymics had already set, after november 1828 and before february 1833. the mother is a tromba: the surname of giovanni tromba s.t.d., the parroco who signs every page and who licensed her son don stefano to baptise in 1816 and to marry couples in 1833. one of the two witnesses is andrea tromba, possidente civile. a ploughman's and a weaver's family produced a priest of the chapter, and their mother came from the family that held the parish. (the kinship is inf, on a shared surname in a small town)

did asked what «went» meant, david answered: «they went to leave the country in 1948.» that converts a contradiction into a window. their son was born at senj on 17 december 1951, so they were back on the coast by about march 1951; ivan died at senj in 1995. they left in 1948, were home inside about two and a half years, and never got out — hedviga reached johannesburg only much later, and ivan never did. the route is not a mystery either. the family already had a household in pfullingen, in the french occupation zone: ivan had worked at reutlingen from 21 october 1941, his father was on the 1947 pfullingen list of foreigners, and his brothers zdravko and anton went out to australia from there in 1949 — anton's card stamped «emigré australie le 8.3.49». ivan and hedviga were a year behind them at a door that was closing, the iro shutting its books at the end of february 1952. a failed exit leaves no yugoslav paper. the arolsen request has been rewritten accordingly and is now the highest-value errand this project holds.

whether the corsican records can be searched by surname found

did they cannot, and finding that out is the result. the archives of the collectivité de corse are free, need no account and are not familysearch — the platform refuses a command-line client but opens normally in a browser. no module has a surname field. état civil, corsica christiana, recensements, registres matricules all take the same three criteria — commune, date range, record type — and the platform says outright that anything else is une recherche non indexée. so corsica is images to be read, like vodnjan. but the record types include table décennale — the alphabetical ten-yearly index french civil registration compiled for every commune, 1793–1902. that is roughly eleven index pages per commune instead of ten years of acts, and it is why corsica can be finished when vodnjan cannot: an austrian liber defunctorum was never indexed by anybody. six cap corse communes are on the platform and all are in scope: tomino, rogliano, ersa, centuri, morsiglia, barrettali. available types: naissances, mariages, décès, baptêmes, sépultures, publications de mariage, table décennale.

a filter of mine deleted a paragraph of hers correction

did this archive said nothing — that is the problem. the account of paputchka's death, some five hundred words, silently vanished from the transcription. what is true the scanner destroyed its opening sentence, returning «ws capes fug ps pepe au sii pony fru. oi wc pi po ut uu tet» where she had written «we experienced "true" love with our siberian husky paputchka». a rule i wrote to strip scanner noise matched that line — and because prose is stored one line per paragraph, deleting the line deleted the entire paragraph. how it happened restored word for word from the original, supplied by david, and marked on the page as restored so no reader has to wonder which text they are looking at. the lesson is specific and unpleasant: a cleanup rule that operates on a whole paragraph can destroy a whole paragraph. noise-stripping must be scoped to the noise — a few tokens — and never to the container it sits in. it was also found by the reader, not by me: nothing in the build warned that five hundred words had gone, because nothing was counting. a reconciliation was then run over the whole page — every substantial line of the raw scan tested against the published text — and it found four more losses of the same kind: the closing paragraph of the husky piece, which had been left beginning mid-sentence at «anger and rage»; a sentence from a suicide avenged; a line of dialogue from it; and part of the godparents letter. all four are restored and marked. one passage is unrecoverable — three lines describing a person, from the 2004 course — and stands on the page as a stated gap rather than a silent one.

did the american half of the family, in documents. the 1930 census puts three of the eleven in one brooklyn flat — albina, her husband frank chinkojan, and her brothers anthony (immigrated 1922) and «grochina», the enumerator's gioacchino. albina's marriage licence of 23 april 1925 names her mother maria volhart; joseph's of 1926 names maria valbart; bruno's of 1931 names mary walhal — three children, three clerks, one woman, and the parish book's volhardt behind all of them. gerda's surname is seedorf, of hanover. joseph's 1917 draft card gives 12 march 1892 and «frieste»; the 1940 census gives him a wife and two children; and a sergeant joseph de franceschi of the first world war lies at long island national cemetery, dead 26 april 1940, twenty-five days after that census. basilio died 15 june 1994. and the fused spelling defranceski returns thirty-six of its own — a family of five off the slovenija at philadelphia in 1954, and two graves at horsham, victoria.

whether antonio ever went back to the wife he left at pićan found

did he did, and he came out again. the manifest of the s.s. martha washington sailing from trieste, stamped new york 31 may 1926, line 6: «defranceschi, antonio, 39, married, mason … last permanent residence n.y., brooklyn … nearest relative in country whence came: wife, defranceschi marta, pedena 10, istria, italy». «last permanent residence brooklyn» is a returning resident on a re-entry permit — so he had gone home to istria between 1922 and 1926 and come back. he was a mason, the trade his father is given by in the gračišće book of souls. and it is the ship joseph crossed on in 1910. marta never came: her only «record» carries the identifier one digit along from antonio's — she is the relation field of his own manifest line. after april 1930 he appears in no american source at all, and never completed naturalisation.

seventy articles; the earliest sixty are shipping intelligence found

did a whole chapter nobody knew was there. between 1865 and 1878 a master of this name commands austrian ships in the black sea grain and bristol channel coal trades — the natalia out of constantinople and galatz, the rachel from odessa to antwerp, the peppina luigia trieste to troon, and above all the aquilone, «aus, 350, defranceschi», tracked through nineteen printed sightings from alexandria and sulina to belfast, malta, venice, ghent, barcelona and out of cardiff for guadaloupe on 11 december 1877. the masters printed beside him are bujanovich, lacovich, cattarinich, ivancich, nicolich — the sea-captain families of lošinj, rijeka and bakar, and this archive has an unplaced dominus household at bakar. and in 1896 the south wales echo writes that «signorina defranceschi belongs to an old cardiff family, and has recently taken her degree at the vienna conservatoire of music», playing harpsichord recitals at the cardiff exhibition. published at /at-sea/.

did three more aquilone voyages (queenstown with alexandria wheat, 3 july 1872; leith for trieste, january 1874; deal, alexandria for stockton, february 1875) — and a second man of the sea entirely: «george de franceschi, a.b., an austrian», giving evidence at the board of trade inquiry into the loss of the shields steamer aberlady bay, june 1889. the first man of this surname anywhere in the archive who is named, dated, put on a named ship and quoted. also enrico de franceschi, baritone of la scala — recorded 1924 with zita fumagalli-riva («here is very excellent singing»), listed in 1926 among amato, galeffi, rouard and stracciari, and broadcast live to britain from la scala in march 1938 with gigli and pagliughi. and the single «defranceski» hit fills in a career: josip defranceski, director of external services, radio belgrade, leaving peshawar for kabul in december 1959.

did a new earliest. «adì 27 mago 1619 · morì ser piero di franceschi da pola. fu portato il suo cadavere … off. l 24» — the oldest dated appearance of this surname in istria the archive holds, seven years before the fiume baptisms and a hundred and forty-two before the name is first written at gologorica. he is styled ser; he is of pola, not of rovinj; his body was carried there; and his offering of 24 lire is near the top of a page whose other entries run at 2, 6 and 12. and the second-oldest is also a stranger: «ob.to di matt.o de franceschi da dignano», 27 december 1728, 6 lire — vodnjan, which this archive lists among the unplaced. the film holds fourteen more, including a rovinj household across three generations (giacomo → vittorio & domenica moscarda → piero anto 1736) — and carlo de franceschi's own marriage to maria michelcich, with his parents named as «giuseppe da gologorizza» and «lambertina pesle». that image has not been opened.

did found, and a correction retracted. this archive said in the afternoon that the seventy-eight vodnjan records were really vižinada's, because the catalogue answered the film number 005497893 with «župa vižinada». a reel can carry two parishes. that one holds vižinada's deaths 1754–1831 and vodnjan's baptisms 1815–1866, catalogue item koha:963267 — «metrical books for the roman catholic congregation at dignano … later vodnjan». the marriages 1815–1884 and deaths to 1893 are on films 894 and 895. the baptismal book is headed «liber baptizatorum in ecclesia s. blasii dignani», and entry 149 of 4 december 1816 gives house 376, «pietro de franceschi di giuseppe, agricoltore», «maria malusà q.m matteo di antonio», condition civile — and the baptising priest is «d. stefano de franceschi, de parocho licentia». a priest of the name at vodnjan, and five lay households. the one death on that reel, mathaeus de franceschi son of anton, house 32, 7 august 1819, is in the liber defunctorum of castellier — kaštelir, under vižinada — which is exactly why the wrong answer looked right.

whose face is on the crikvenica page correction

did the face was wrong, and it was on the direct line's own page. a hand-tinted portrait of a bearded man in a bow tie had been published here as josip defranceschi, born at gračišće 22 march 1863 — david's great-grandfather, and the only likeness the direct line had. david identified it: the photograph is from the imotski branch, and the sitter is a josip of that family. two branches' pictures sit in one collection; a card carried the name, this line has a man of that name, and this archive matched face to name without asking which josip. the register plates on that page were checked against gračišće and ledenice — the portrait was never checked against anything. withdrawn from the head card and from the 1906 entry in the story, recaptioned in the gallery, and a correction section added to the page where it stood. the companion portrait published as his wife ana is also withdrawn: its only identification was that it matched the man beside it. no likeness of the crikvenica josip is known to this archive. note the pattern — the retired 2018 gedcom spliced imotski onto this line too. the same seam has now caught this archive twice, once in a pedigree and once in a photograph.

carlo de franceschi's own marriage, opened at last found

did the historian was married lying down. 1 march 1852 at rovinj: «il signor carlo de franceschi q.m giuseppe e della sig.ra lambertina pesle di mattia, da gologorizza di pisino, assessore presso quest'i. r. corte di giustizia, celibe d'anni 40» marries «maria michelcich di luca e di maria, celibe d'anni 26» — «al letto dello sposo, per essere gravemente ammalato», at the bridegroom's bed because he was gravely ill. the banns were dispensed the same day by the imperial-royal district captaincy, note № 898, urgente necessitate, and the witnesses are the deputy state prosecutor zaccaria maver and dr barzan, physician — the law and the medicine, not the family. he did not die; he lived to 1893. the entry also fixes his office in 1852 and names both parents. two corrections fall out: the register says d'anni 40 and he was forty-two (b. 16 oct 1809); and this archive's marriage table carried the year as 1812 — it is 1852, now fixed with the reason stated. on the same film, a burial of «julius, son of carlo», born 1853, dead 13 february 1854 — very probably the first child of this marriage.

did this archive said per-place record counts for this surname across sixty istrian and kvarner towns, and a research queue carrying «vižinada — 53 records, unread», «draguč — 25», «dubrovnik — 38». what is true the place parameter on this search endpoint does not filter. ten values were tested, including «zzzznowhere» and «atlantis», and every one returned the same total: 3,652. vižinada and draguč return identical result sets. dubrovnik returns the unfiltered list. the queued «vižinada 53» records are on the vodnjan film and have already been read. how it happened the parameter is a relevance boost dressed as a filter — no error, no warning, just the whole set back in a different order. the sweep survives because its method independently checked each record's own place text before counting it; the queue did not, and carried three phantom tasks for days. the reliable route is to resolve records to their film and read the catalogue's item list — remembering that a film can carry more than one parish.

did standing rules, so nothing here can ever be mistaken for a source: no invented face is ever captioned with a real person's name; no invented lettering on a real inscribed stone and no invented heraldry for a family whose arms are documented; every image captioned as a constructed illustration with its departures from the record named; no fabricated documentary apparatus — no title block, scale bar, dimension, survey date; the unaltered original archived in the source library beside its brief, marked with whatever was removed. briefs at notes/image-prompts.md. all eight now done, seven published: the house at gologorica, with the 1711 tablet deliberately blank; imotski 1717; the road of the furlans 1679; the salamon palace; the mills at perinuša; crikvenica in the winter of 1943; pfullingen 1944. plus a lapidarius of gračišće, published as the trade and explicitly not as a portrait of antonio, because the model gave it a detailed invented face. two withheld: the first gologorica house, which carried a fabricated pseudo-latin inscription across the 1711 tablet; and a close detail of the arms and the madonna relief, because the coat of arms in it does not match the blazon carlo gave kobler and the carving the family photographed — a cross crossed by two arrows over a pomegranate. both kept in the library marked withheld. four failure modes, each seen more than once: a caption burned into the picture; a watermark; an invented inscription or coat of arms on a real carved stone; and an image returned dressed as a measured conservation survey of a real protected building, with title block, scale bar, dimensions and date. every one of them was caught before publication.

did seget: the house carries its own dates — «1724» on the courtyard portal and «1732» with the initials «ma. f.» on the cistern, marc'antonio's monogram on his own well-head. a generation appears that this archive had never printed: giorgio de franceschi, 1788–1865, who threw a staircase block along the east front in 1843–45 and put a classicist façade over it, frescoed inside by michele urban, the architect to be sought among those practising at trieste. the estate's economy turns from wine to olive oil about 1840. and the venier–valier disagreement is settled for venier, from 1623. imotski: four corrections. the friars were not at proložac village but on an islet in prološko blato from about 1600, marked by a stone cut a.d. 1609. the party zuane sheltered was fifteen people of whom nine were friars, with a lay brother, four schoolboys and a hermit. skalice at omiš was begun 13 july 1716 and blessed 29 october 1718 on ground belonging to pavao despotović and jakov mariani. and the friars did not return in 1717 — they returned in 1738, building at imotski from 1740. zuane's own dates are 1673–1741. and one unopened primary source: at skalice there is a book bound in sheepskin, written in bosančica on 416 leaves, which is the friars' own chronicle of the flight. it is in a friary, not an archive. and then the thesis was read. david cleared the repository's bot check himself, and «uloga obitelji franceschi u mletačkom osvajanju imotskog» — matea kaćunić, split, september 2025, 77 pages, open access — turns out to be the best single source on the dalmatian family that exists. it corrects this archive six times and adds a second estate. full account on the imotski page; the pdf is now in this project's library.

did a hard date for the lease, and a name for the relief. the gologorica benefice was founded in 1443 by the pazin provost andreas schuel; frederick iii took the right of appointment; the holders were the captains of pazin and the bishops of pedena, then the marquis de prié, then charles antoine biotz, and «naposljetku od 1772. obitelj de franceschi … do ukidanja feudalnih odnosa 1848» — the de franceschi held it on lease from 1772 to 1848, seventy-six years. that fits carlo's «affitto fermo» rather than contradicting it, and dates it. the house is described as «velika kamena palača obitelji de franceschi, dvokatna građevina s balkonom i portalom iz 1711., ukrašena grbom i natpisom te reljefom s prikazom isusa» — which settles a thing this site once got wrong: the relief over the door is a figure of christ, and it is real. also: gologorica burned in 1463, 1508 and 1511; the bell tower finished 1740; an imago pietatis of 1446 and a glagolitic inscription of 1595 in the parish church; and mikula gologorički, priest of this parish, wrote the croatian glagolitic version of the istrian boundary settlement of 1325.

did the family's library is not lost. it is in zagreb, and it has been catalogued. 2,396 items, 1503–1945, taken out of the house at gologorica in 1948–49, boxed, and left unprocessed in the national and university library's store for sixty years — not in the card catalogue, not in the electronic one, «nobody could know of its existence». processing began 2009 and finished in 2021. it holds an aldine of 1503, the signatures of five generations, letters of d'annunzio, poems of giuseppina martinuzzi, and the very metastasio, petrarch, tasso and ariosto that carlo says he found on the family shelves as a schoolboy. published on the library page.

did three unindexed occurrences on the first three openings. «m.ro nadal de franceschi» stands godfather on 20 may 1666, five months before his own daughter is baptised; «il sig.r ant.o di franceschi» stands godfather on 9 february 1674. godparent roles are never indexed, which is the whole reason to open the page. the baptisms of colotta (24 oct 1666) and fioretta (22 nov 1666) are confirmed word for word, both fathers styled m.ro. and the company is the argument: the godparents across these openings are spinoti, fiorenza, felicer, fabri — the canale di gorto set, standing at each other's fonts in a croatian village in 1666. by 1674 anto is sig.r and his son's compare is a count luciani: the same household, eight years, artisan to gentleman.

did this archive said «il signor carlo de franceschi … celibe, d'anni 40», 1 march 1852. what is true he was forty-two, born 16 october 1809. how it happened not this archive's mistake but the register's, and it is transcribed as written rather than silently improved. ages in these books are what somebody said in the room — and in this room the man being asked was too ill to stand up.
names that are not this name correction

did this archive said nothing — these were caught before publication and are recorded so they are not found again. what is true franceschich of buzet is a slavic patronymic, not franceschi. francin is its own vodnjan family — although pietro de franceschi's first wife was a francin, so in that parish the two are a household deep in each other. pietro francin q.m dom.co de rondel is not a de franceschi. how it happened read by eye rather than matched by string. this is the whole argument for reading a register instead of querying one.

a defranceschi daughter married into medulin — 16 november 1873

medulin «liber defunctorum», page 33, the whole of 1873 so the year stands with the entry. fourth line from the foot, annual number 139: «maria (defranceschi) ant. verinic uxor» — maria, née defranceschi, wife of antonio verinic — died 16 november 1873, aged 78 (the figure corrected in the ink), «mors ord[inaria]». the parentheses are the scribe's maiden-name convention, and the very next line proves it: «maria (vrinic q. nic.) vid. georgii lorenzin» — maria née vrinic, widow of georgio lorenzin. seventy-eight in 1873 means born about 1795 — the same generation as the ližnjan groom of 1815 and the soldier who died here in 1833. in this copy the foot of the page and the margins are trimmed, so the line cited is not the fourth from the foot of the image, and the corrected figure of the age is hard to read at this size.

from hrvatski državni arhiv, zagreb — medulin parish registers, filmed by the genealogical society of utah and read through familysearch (croatia, church books, 1516–1994) · waypoint 9r2h-hz7, frame 21 · ark 3:1:3qsq-g99x-kzbv · hda, matična knjiga umrlih medulin 1801–1899, inv. br. 158
the first defranceschi in a medulin register — 19 december 1833

medulin «liber defunctorum», page 12, the whole of the year 1833 so the column headings and the year stand with the entry. line 9, annual number 43: «mathæus defranceschi q. ant. fil. miles» — mathæus defranceschi, son of the late antonio, a soldier — died 19 december 1833, aged 40, of «chronicus morb[us]». the month is a ditto of «xbris» on the line above. forty in december 1833 means born about 1793. the lines either side are given deliberately: the same scribe writing «lorenzin», «longovich» and «radossevich» at one magnification, none of which the surname can be confused with. ⚠ read at scale the cause looked like «dissenteria»; at native resolution it is «chronicus morb.» — the magnification changed the reading, which is why the rule exists.
