the canon deputising, and the house numbers begin — 1781–1782

dapa zm34k-214, m01068941, «liber baptizatorum ii», gologorica, at native resolution. top, 26 december 1781, «sub n.o 10»: «joannes filius legitimus viti et mariæ jugalium selescho baptizatus fuit à me, mathia de franceschi can.co» — his own hand, a month before the parish priest's illness is first mentioned. middle, 20 january 1782, «sub n.o 83 domus»: «infirmo d.no parocho hujus loci gollogoritiæ, ego mathias franceschi canonicus ecclesiæ cathedralis civitatis petinæ baptizavi filium infantem natum ex severino et maria crismanich». bottom, 30 march 1782, holy saturday, «sub n.o 31. domus»: «ego joannes mathias franceschi, canonicus et parochus gollogoritiæ, baptizavi filium infantem natum ex joanne baptista et cattarina deprato … cui impositum est nomen franciscus ignatius. patrini fuerunt joannes baptista filius josephi de franceschi et margarita ejusdem filia» — margarita defranceschi alive at a font a year and three weeks before her death, beside her brother. every one of these entries carries a house number; the previous parish priest numbered none in eighteen years of this book.
«domina catharina defranceschi nata sablich buccarensis», 16 december 1783

dapa zm34k-214, m01068943, «liber baptizatorum ii», gologorica, the male sequence, entry 61, at native resolution: «ego joannes florcich capellanus baptisavi filium legitimum natum die 13 hujus ex joanne baptista deprato, et catharina ejus uxore, e parochia petinensi, conjugibus hujus loci, cui impositum est nomen joannes eusebius. patrini fuere dominus josephus defranceschi, et domina catharina defranceschi nata sablich buccarensis.» three years earlier than the archive's previous earliest sighting of her, and the register gives her origin as a single latin adjective — buccarensis, of bakar — rather than the prepositional «ex buccari» of 1786.

the chaplain's own j, against the surname he wrote fifteen words earlier

dapa zm34k-214, m01068943, the entry of 16 december 1783, three cuts at one magnification, all by the chaplain joannes florcich inside a single paragraph. top: «…chi nata sablich» — the surname's initial rises from the baseline, loops, and returns to it, with no descender. middle: «fuere josep[hus]». bottom: «joannes eusebiu[s]». in both of the scribe's own j's the stroke rises high and then drops a long descender below the baseline, hooking left; the surname's initial does neither. this scribe writes s. it does not overturn the gologorica entry of october 1786, whose «jablich» was proved the same way against its own scribe's j — it shows that both spellings are native to the parish, in different hands, three years apart.
two men, one forename pair, one patronymic, two surnames

dapa zm34k-214, «liber baptizatorum ii», gologorica, two godparent clauses at one magnification. top, m01068943, 5 february 1783: «patrini fuerunt joannes baptista deprato, leonardi filius, et catharina uxor ejusdem leonardi, ambo ex hac parochia.» bottom, m01068932, 29 october 1773: «patrini fuerunt joannes baptista defranceschi q.m leonardi, et catharina uxor antonij marion, hujates.» the village held both men at once: a joannes baptista deprato son of leonardus deprato, and a joannes baptista defranceschi son of leonardus defranceschi. where a surname is abbreviated, damaged or omitted, a patronymic cannot separate them.

the two 1785 defranceschi baptisms as liber ii records them

dapa zm34k-214, m01068944, «liber baptizatorum ii», gologorica, the male sequence, at native resolution — both of these baptisms are also entered in liber baptizatorum iv, and the two books do not say the same things. top, entry 56, 6 january 1785: «admod. r.dus carolus covaz, canonicus antignanæ, habita licentia parochi, baptizavit filium legitimum natum ex joanne baptista, ejusque uxore cattarina de franceschj … cui impositum est nomen josephus, 5.ta ejusdem mensis natus. patrini fuere antonius, ejusque uxor maria covaz ex pisino.» liber iv gives this child's house and midwife and the second forename «anton»; only liber ii gives his birth date and his officiant — the same canon who buried joannes petrus defranceschi in 1781. bottom, entry 31, 13 april 1785: «ego idem parochus baptizavi filium legitimum natum ex joanne bapta defranceschj ejusque uxore teresia … nomen franciscus antonius. patrini fuere d.nus archipresbiter grah, parochus cherbune, et cattarina uxor joannis bapta defranceschj.» liber iv names the godmother only as «catharina defranceschi»; liber ii says whose wife she is, separating the two joannes baptistas by their women for the fourth time in this volume.

this priest's 31, and the 1782 number that is not one

dapa zm34k-214, two marginal house numbers in the hand of joannes mathias franceschi, at one magnification. top, m01068944, the margin of the franciscus antonius entry of 13 april 1785, where the house is independently given as 31 by liber baptizatorum iv: the first figure is an open, angular 3 with a flat top; the second is a dotted upright, which is how this hand writes 1. bottom, m01068941, the margin of the holy saturday entry of 30 march 1782, read an hour earlier as «31» with a warning attached because its parents are deprato: the second figure matches, but the first is a closed loop, not this scribe's 3. the 1782 house is not 31 — 61 and 81 are the readings worth testing — and no deprato household is placed in the defranceschi door.

dapa zm34k-214, m01069089, folio 76 — the baptism of clementina maria defranceschi, 6 october 1822, of «dnus joseph defranceschi» and «dna lambertina ejus uxor nata pesle». top, the godparent cell entire: «pietro ant. defranceschi» and, beneath, «amalia peschle ex volosca», the pair entered «cives gollogo[ricenses]». bottom, the place-word at four times magnification: v-o-l-o-s-c-a. seven letters, opening on a flat-topped v, closing on a long terminal a; no dotted i anywhere and no e. «silesia» would need two dotted i and an e, and shows neither. this archive published the word as «ex silesia» on 1 october 2026 and built worklist 170 — a search of the austrian-silesian registers for a german origin for carlo de franceschi's mother's family — on that one word. it says volosca, which is where this archive had placed the peschle in the first place.

dapa zm34k-214, m01069447, gologorica status animarum 1862. the household of «defranceschi leonardus». his first wife «maria n. flegar», born 4 april 1842, has a death in the obitus column — 28 september 1882. beneath her children comes «maria udovičić ii. uxor» — second wife — born 28 september 1857, with 3 april 1883 in the matrimonii column, six months after the first wife's death. the next child is entered «antonius leopoldus filius ex ii. votis» — of the second marriage — born 29 january 1884, and after him «rosa filia», born 1 april 1886 with the same date again in the obitus column: she died the day she was born. this archive held leonardus, both marias and antonius leopoldus as separate rows; the phrase «ex ii. votis» appears nowhere else in its data, and nothing joined them.

two grah wives in one opening — and one of them says which house at cerovlje she came out of

dapa zm34k-214, m01069464, gologorica status animarum 1862 — two bubić households on facing pages, each with a grah wife, neither of whom the book's own family index can see. top: «franciscus bubić», rusticus, born 31 july 1842, married 18 june 1869, died 7 april 1908; «rosalia ux. n. grah-missan», born 13 may 1845, whose adnotatio reads «e cerovglie n.º 12» — out of cerovlje, house 12; their son franciscus born 19 november 1869. bottom: «joannes fil. joannis et dominicae», born 14 may 1833, died 15 february 1909, with «marianna ux. n. grah-jopan», born 19 september 1834, married 22 january 1861, died 19 august 1870; and after her «oliva ux. 2da n. crismanić». grah-jopan is a compound form this archive had never met — beside grah-mišan, a second grah byname. and the cerovlje status animarum, swept end to end on 10 october, carries grah at houses 18, 19, 23, 38 and 53, not 12, and marries its grah daughters into držetić, dujanić, šepuka, opašić, krošnjak and lušetić — not bubić.

two household bynames, and a marriage this archive had been carrying as a death

dapa zm34k-214, gologorica status animarum 1862, three bands. top (m01069446), the household of «defranceschi antonius», cives, born 14 apr. 1814, died 6 jan. 1893, married 25 feb. 1840 to «francisca ux. n. defranceschi», born 3 feb. 1819, died 8 febr. 1892 — with a byname written diagonally across the rule above his name: «osvaldo». this is the household whose adnotatio reads «ex italia (carnia)» and whose wife is «gallignanensis». middle (m01069577), the loose «ordo alfabeticus familiarum» slip under d: «defranceschi-carmel ant. et franca», page 10, with a second byname «defranceschi-tito» written smaller beneath. at seven times magnification the first byname carries a dot above its minims, which would make it «carniel», the carnian — a reading drafted as a correction to this archive's transcription and then withdrawn, because the bynames around it, osvaldo and tito, are personal names, which is how an istrian household byname is ordinarily formed; carmelo belongs to that set and carniel does not. the dot is recorded, not explained away. bottom (m01069542): «aloysius defranceschi», mercator, born 4 maji 1832, and in the matrimonii contracti column, braced across him and his wife joanna née udovičić, «25. nov. 1870» — the exact date this archive's family tree recorded as his death, and withdrew earlier the same day for want of any burial entry.

the 1894 census is a genealogy, not a house list — and it gives hector his parents

dapa zm34k-214, gologorica status animarum 1894. this book does not list households and stop: under each head it sets out «filii», «filiae», «fratres», «sorores», «parentes», and — where the wife had married before — «liberi … ex i/ii thalamo», her children by each earlier husband. top (m01069590): «defranceschi antonius, iii vir rosae n. salamon», with filii ferdinandus romanus, aloysius joannes and hector; filiae estella ida and ida-rosa; then «liberi rosae ex i th.: maria, luigia» and «liberi rosae ex ii thal.: angela, maria» — ruža's children by the two defranceschi brothers she married before this one. middle (m01069585), from the household of franciscus and clotilda née ortis: «clotilda, maria, filia valentini marcolini e beatricis n. defranceschi», born 15 january 1894 — which names the husband that the 1862 book could only abbreviate to «za ang. val.» bottom (m01069591): «defranceschi leonardus» with «maria ii ux. n. udovičić», his five sons by the second marriage — leopoldus antonius, petrus, romanus, victor, aemilius ernestus — his two daughters by it, and «filius leonardi ex i thal.: joannes aloysius», by maria née flegar. the crops end before the «liberi rosae» lines, before leonardus's second daughter and before «filius leonardi ex i thal.»; those lines are not on this image.

an «extrema unctio» register with birth dates — and two marriages the archive did not have

dapa zm34k-214, gologorica status animarum 1894. top (m01069740): a ruled register headed status animarum whose columns run nrus progress. · nrus domus · nomen et cognomen · pagus · nativitatis (dies, mensis, annus) · «extrema unctio» (dies, mensis, annus) · confessus · communicans. it records last rites by year — 1907 with eleven entries, 1908 with ten, 1909 with two — each person given a house, a hamlet and a full date of birth. extreme unction is administered at the point of death, so this is the nearest thing to a death register the archive has for the years after the 1784–1880 volume ends; no defranceschi appears in it. middle (m01069671): two defranceschi households, «aloysius» with «joanna n. udovičić» and their children aloysius-arturus, armella-elvana-aurelia, gisella-elvira and ersilia-maria; and beneath, «defranceschi aloysius, mercator» with «albina ux. n. lovrinović» and their daughters norina and elda-maria. bottom (m01069687): under the heading gologorica, «celentich josephus», ludimagister, with «lambertina lina n. defranceschi» and their daughters gemma maria and alice clotildis carolina. the crops are partial: the top shows only the column headings and the first three rows (too small to read at this size), the middle ends within the first household's daughters, and the bottom ends at gemma maria; the later rows described here are not on this image.

the second element of the grah compound is not securely read — and cerovlje house 12 is an opašić house

top two bands, dapa zm34k-214, m01069464, the gologorica status animarum of 1862, at one magnification and in one hand. the first band is «joannes», whose capital j loops wide at the top left and descends below the line with a leftward tail. the second is the disputed word, «marianna ux. n. grah-?pan»: the letter after the hyphen has a straighter, taller ascender than that j, and the word runs off into the column rule so its ending cannot be read at all. this archive published it as «grah-jopan» on 11 october; the reading is withdrawn to an open question. bottom band, dapa zm34k-214, m01068790, the cerovlje status animarum, house 12 — the house rosalia née grah-missan gave as her origin when she married into gologorica in 1869. it is an opašić household: «opašić thomas def. antonii», born 21 december 1846, with «margaritha n. dujanić», and below him his son «opašić benjamin fil. thomae» with «dominica n. gržić». a pencil «opassi» sits above the second heading, the italianised form imposed by prefectoral decree. the lower band stops at the children of opašić thomas; his son benjamin with dominica née gržić, and the pencil «opassi», lie below it and are not on this image.
from državni arhiv u pazinu, microfilm zm34k-214 — the family's own copy of the film · m01069464 and m01068790
the grah wife's burial entry — and it gives her husband's surname, not her father's

top, dapa zm34k-214, m01069287, page 115 of the gologorica death register, «liber mortuorum parochiæ gologoricensis anni 1870»: «1870 augusti 19na · 25 · marianna bubić, agla, munita ss. sacramentis, et sepulta die 20. hujus · 35 · hydropisia», signed blasius zwölber, parochus. this is the marianna whom the 1862 status animarum enters as «ux. n. grah-?pan», born 19 september 1834 — the age of 35 at death in august 1870 closes on it. the burial register confirms her death to the day and gives her cause, her house and her priest, and it gives her surname as bubić: a woman who marries in is entered under her husband in the death book exactly as she is in the household index, so the one register that might have settled her father's name does not carry it. bottom, m01068796, cerovlje house 18 — «grah mathias def. mathiae» and his son «grah matthaeus fil. mathiae», with the pencil «gracco ver. grah» above the second heading. the cerovlje grah of houses 18, 19 and 23 are plain «grah» with no second element, so that hand cannot settle the compound either. the cerovlje cut shows only the first household of house 18; matthaeus and the pencil «gracco ver. grah» above his heading are not on this image.
from državni arhiv u pazinu, microfilm zm34k-214 — the family's own copy of the film · m01069287 and m01068796
both grah compounds in one hand on one page — and the second is «žipan», not «jopan»

dapa zm34k-214, the gologorica baptism register. top and middle, page 126 (m01069140), the patrini column for the year 1864, two entries three months apart in one hand: «joannes bubich» with «marianna n. grah-missan», godparents on 7 may; and «josephus udovichich» with «rosa grah-žipan», godparents on 22 september. bottom, m01069137, the mater column: «joannes bubich, agr.» with «mariana grah-missan» — the same marianna entered as a mother, so the baptism register carries her maiden surname where her burial entry gave only her husband's. this archive published the second compound as «grah-jopan» on 11 october and withdrew the reading the same day on the ground that the initial did not match the scribe's j. it is confirmed here as ž or š followed by i-p-a-n: the word is «žipan», the croatian župan, a village headman — and this archive already holds «mattia uxor suppani joannis grach» at gračišće, the wife of suppanus joannes grach, who held that office. on this image the bottom band ends at a different line («joannes maricich», as far as it can be read), and the bubich line with «grah-missan» in the mater column that this caption describes is cut off at the rule.

the «nrus. domus» pairs — and two pages that a house-number pair cannot explain

dapa zm34k-214, the gologorica status animarum of 1826, the «nrus. domus» column. top two bands, m01069349 and m01069350 at five times magnification: «21» over a short rule over «48», and «23» over a short rule over «48». the same lower figure stands under two different upper figures, on two different pages, against two different households — «joannes opassich haeres runco» and «joannes rythno def. josephi». if both figures were house numbers under two systems, as this archive concluded on 6 october, that cannot happen: one old house cannot be two new ones unless it was split, and 21 and 23 are not adjacent. bottom two bands, m01069333 and m01069341 at page scale: house 7, «franciscus xaverius defranceschi» with «clotilda uxor ortis filia joannis et franciscae»; and house 34, «leonardus defranceschi». those two numbers are single, unpaired and unambiguous.

the first defranceschi at ližnjan — and a byname, 12 november 1815

ližnjan «liber copulatorum», page 1, the second marriage the book ever records. «12 novembre 1815», house 17: «mario de franceschi deto marulin di antonio», catolico, ætas 21, celibes, to «maddalena percouich di antonio», ætas 27. witnesses giacomo bubich di iseppo, antonio clunich di stefano, gregorio iucopila. twenty-one in 1815 means born about 1794; his father is antonio. the entry above, «gregorio runan di anni 32 q. michel», is included deliberately: it shows the same hand giving every d a tall ascender, which is how «deto marulin» was settled as a byname and not the place madolin.

the same man's burial, twenty-four years later — and the byname again

ližnjan «liber defunctorum», page 93. «addì 20 xbre 1839», house 17 — the house he married into in 1815 — «mattio franceschi d.to marulin, agr.», cattolico, maschio, «ann. 40». the byname is written on him a second time, in a different book and a different hand, which closes the reading that nearly made «marulin» into «madolin»: a place does not follow a man to his grave as a «detto». his age does not agree with itself — 21 in 1815, 40 in 1839 — and neither figure is corrected here. ⚠ this entry sits at 0.52 of the page height and was missed entirely by a scout whose crop stopped at 0.46. the cited row is cut through at the foot of this image: the byname «marulin» is only half visible and the age «ann. 40» is not on it.

what is here and what is not

seventeen photographs, three camp portraits, five pages of the gračišće parish books with the archive's letters that released them, and the working papers of a family in württemberg between 1941 and 1950. nothing on this page was found on the open web; all of it was either kept by the family or bought, page by page, from an archive.
faces of people who may be living are not published, and the children entered on the camp cards as enfant are named nowhere on this site.

a photograph with a name and a decade attached is worth more than a chart. studio marks on the back of a print name the town; a uniform names the army; a dress names the decade to within about five years. send what you have.

/archive/.title: The Archive — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 1151 registers catalogued
read directly from the state archives in pazin inventory. this is not a plan — these are books that exist, with dates, custodians and digitisation status.
register books catalogued across 14 parishes — not people
digitised — 87% of the total
earliest book — pazin baptisms
separate custodians, each with its own door

read this number the right way round. the 1151 above counts books, not people — parish registers that exist in the pazin inventory. it is not a measure of what this archive has done; it is a measure of how much is still unread. this project has opened a book in 7 of these 14 parishes, and the great majority of the 997 digitised volumes have never been looked at.

the comparable counts of people are elsewhere: everyone holds the roster, and the register holds every indexed record the surname has produced. a sister project on the falco family of arienzo shows 10,536 records naming 4,779 people against those — because it read a town's death registers act by act rather than searching an index for one surname. six thousand of its people are the town, not the family. that is the difference in method, and this page is the reason ours can close it.

every row can now be opened. 142 of these 1151 catalogued books match a volume that familysearch has photographed, and those rows link straight into the image viewer at page one of that book — same parish, same kind of register, overlapping years, and nothing linked on a looser match than that. the rest link to the pazin archive's own registers page, which is the door you would actually have to walk through. a familysearch account is free; the reading room at pazin is by appointment.

custody codes: žu parish office, still in the village · ba poreč diocesan archive of poreč-pula · dapa state archives in pazin · mu civil registry office. the state archives states publicly that its staff do not undertake genealogical research, will not act on a request lacking a name, an approximate period and a place, and will not review large quantities of material. research is done by the user in the reading room, by appointment.

familysearch catalogue, searched by place authority id, september 2026. films made by the genealogical society of utah from originals in the croatian state archives (zagreb and zadar) and the archivio di stato di udine.

two results matter most here. omiš opens in 1588 — two years before gaspar de franceschi is said to have owned a warship there — so the dalmatian family's earliest claim is testable. and ovaro has no parish books on film at all, only the napoleonic civil registration, which confirms that the carnian church registers before 1806 exist nowhere online and must be asked for at the parish.

beyond the film, the name index. a search of the croatian church books returns 3,652 hits for this surname; 2,388 of them are genuine variants rather than franchini or francetich, and 2,200 are distinct people.

austria, tyrol and the other family
147 records from the austrian index — and they settle the trentino question. this is not our family.

seventy-four per cent of italy's defranceschi live in trentino-alto adige, and the obvious question was whether that is a branch of the istrian family or an independent formation of the same patronymic. the austrian records answer it, because trentino and the south tyrol were austrian until 1918 and their registers sit in the austrian index.

sixteen records are from bozen and salorno in the tirolo, and they show settled households: joseph franzeschini and veronika kohl baptising at bozen from 1815 to 1823; franz defranceschi and maria kassler in 1852; franciski franceschi and maria koßler in 1855; leonardo franzeschini and dominica perini in 1871. behind them, a seventeenth-century family — bartholomaeus de franceschi and lucia de gregorys, with children urbanus in 1645, maria in 1649, joannes and lucia in 1651.

look at who they married. kohl, kolin, koßler, kassler, knoll, pachmann, rossler, webern, pfeifer, moser, angerer, steiner, niedermaier, volser, klinzer, tschigg — german and tyrolean names, mixed with trentino italian ones: perini, trentini, tabarelli, nardelli, benedetti, maistri, festi, scrinzi, covi, marchetti, galeazzi, avi, piffer, sandri, mosna.

there is no overlap with the istrian in-law world at all — not one skifich, malusà, bergamo, cerlon or cleva. two families, the same patronymic, four hundred kilometres apart, marrying in entirely separate worlds. the 74 per cent is a coincidence of a very common name and the same austrian habit of fusing the prefix, acting twice.

a third group sits at klagenfurt in carinthia, spelling it franceschinis — vittorio franceschinis and margaretha bierlotter, five children between 1900 and 1909. the -is ending is friulian, and carinthia borders friuli. these are almost certainly carnian emigrants who went north instead of south, the other half of the road that took a de franceschi of mione into the county of pazin in 1679.
two records in the austrian index stop you.
name born died place
pier giovanni franceschini 29 sep 1915 05 apr 1945 gusen, perg bezirk, upper austria oberösterreich, austria
attilio franceschini 23 mar 1896 13 may 1945 gusen, perg bezirk, upper austria, austria

gusen, in the perg district of upper austria, was a subcamp of mauthausen. pier giovanni franceschini, born 29 september 1915, is recorded dead there on 5 april 1945, a month before the camp was reached. attilio franceschini, born 23 march 1896, is recorded dead there on 13 may 1945 — eight days after liberation, which was common: thousands died of starvation and typhus in the weeks after the gates opened.

neither man is shown to be related to this family, and both carry the friulian -ini ending rather than ours. they are set down here because an archive that publishes a count of 268,000 index hits and says nothing about the two men who died in a camp has failed at the only thing it is for.

recorded as documented dates and places; the identification of that gusen with the concentration camp is inferred from the place and the dates, and the underlying record set has not yet been traced to its collection.
the systematic sweep
seventy-five places across istria, kvarner, carnia and dalmatia, and their neighbours, checked one by one against the familysearch catalogue by place-authority id. 189 items found across 61 places.

and the result that matters most is a negative one. gologorica and gračišće have no familysearch holdings at all. neither does pićan, cerovlje, motovun, lindar, čepić — nor mione. the genealogical society of utah never filmed the central istrian interior, which is exactly where this family is from. every other route into these parishes leads back to the state archives in pazin and to the books still sitting in the village parish offices. there is no remote substitute.

and the villages that are still not there

gologorica, gračišće, pićan, cerovlje, vodnjan, motovun and lindar have no images either. they were absent from the catalogue and they are absent from the image collection. that is now checked twice, by two different routes, and it is settled: the central istrian interior was never photographed.
but the neighbours were

what the image collection does have, and the catalogue sweep missed, is the ring of parishes immediately around them: pazin, stari pazin, lupoglav (pazin), tinjan, kringa, boljun, petar u šumi, polje čepić, kršan. a family living at gologorica married, buried and stood godparent across that ring. gračišće is four kilometres from pazin and six from tinjan. those books are open, and they are the nearest thing to the missing ones that exists.

the catch is the 24 per cent. of the neighbouring parishes, only a fraction is name-indexed — which is why a search for a defranceschi at tinjan or kringa returns nothing while the books themselves may be full of them. reading them means opening images page by page, in latin, and that is work for a person, not for this.

this page is the inventory — the volumes that exist for the places this family came from. the research map is the same question asked of the whole country: 1,196 record-book places across croatia, every confession, with a colour for how far this archive has got with each one. it is rebuilt from david's own google my map, which cannot otherwise be kept.

pazin is the prize. births reaching back to 1582 with a continuous run from 1685 to 1847, marriages from 1597 to 1852, deaths from 1655. gračišće is four kilometres away and gologorica about eight; pazin was their market, their court and their county town, and it is the parish a gologorica family would most often turn up in.

tinjan is the other one to open — births 1703–1880 and marriages 1703–1896, an unbroken two-century run six kilometres from gračišće. lupoglav has births from 1656. krbune, the small village that already yielded six indexed records, has a single combined volume covering births, deaths and marriages 1803–1870.

and the marriage books matter more than the baptisms here. the gologorica registers show that no defranceschi married in their own parish between 1771 and 1789 — the men married in their brides' parishes. those marriages are in this ring.

croatia, church books 1516–1994, collection 2040054, walked 14 september 2026. a link opens the volume's own first image; a free familysearch account is needed to see it. none of these volumes is name-indexed — searching the surname returns nothing while the pages may be full of it, which is the whole reason for listing them.
carnia — a different country, a different collection, and one village missing

carnia is not in the croatian collection, and finding what familysearch holds for it meant paging all 3,483 of its collections, because the collections api silently ignores its own text filter — a search for «udine» returns alabama. there is exactly one: «italy, udine, civil registration (state archive), 1806-1815, 1871-1911», collection 1939238, 1.26 million images.
the archive had half the dates

this site has been describing the udine holding as «stato civile (civil only) 1806–1815» — the napoleonic registers. the collection is 1806–1815 and 1871–1911. the second half, sixty years of civil registration after italian unification, has never been looked at here.
the province breaks down into 627 comuni, and ovaro is not one of them. neither is mione, muina, ovasta, luint, liariis, chialina, agrons nor cludinico — every val degano name was checked.
but colza is there, and colza is a frazione of ovaro. it holds a complete napoleonic set for 1806–1812: births, deaths, marriages, marriage banns and the indexes to all three. twenty-five volumes.

whether mione and muina are written inside those volumes is a question the images can answer and the index cannot — the record api's place filter is ignored, so it returns the same 2,201 people whatever place you give it. the volumes are linked below — but the images are restricted and cannot be opened from a desk. colza was the first thing tried on 14 september and the viewer answered «image restricted». settling ovaro now means a family history center, an affiliate library, or the archivio di stato di udine itself. the twenty-five volumes are named and numbered, which is what the request needs.

and then antenati answered it. the archivio di stato di udine has published its own registers on the italian state portal, free and open: ovaro has 271 of them, and fifty-nine are catalogued under mione's own name. nati, morti, matrimoni, the marriage pubblicazioni and the allegati, running from 1806 to 1871 and beyond. the volumes familysearch will not show are on antenati for anyone to open. see the search register for the 14 september entry.
comeglians holds the allegati this archive already used

comeglians — the seat of the gorto canton — carries the marriage allegati for 1807 to 1815, nine volumes. those are the documents behind one of this archive's load-bearing findings: the allegati are what pushed the mione family back to a giovanni battista de' franceschi already dead by 1789. they were read from the archivio di stato di udine; this is the same material, openable from a desk.
and a warning about the other two thousand

the collection indexes 2,201 people called franceschi. of the first eleven hundred, sampled by the search's own ranking, the carnian communes barely appear — five entries in all. the bulk are lowland friulian families: lauzzana and colloredo di monte albano (209), udine (129), muzzana del turgnano (114), bertiolo (101), magnano in riviera (46).
most of the franceschi in the udine registers are not this family and are not from the mountains. that is worth saying before anyone absorbs two thousand strangers into a carnian pedigree.

italy, udine, civil registration (state archive), collection 1939238, walked 14 september 2026. these links do not open the page. they open the volume and say «image restricted». the images of this whole collection are gated — «access is typically determined by local laws or the custodian» — and are viewable only at a family history center or an affiliate library. three comuni were tested, at colza, comeglians and paluzza, and all three are shut; the croatian volumes on this page open normally, so the difference is italy's, not familysearch's. what the link still gives you is the exact volume and its register number, which is what an order form or a reading-room request needs. these are civil registers, not parish books — carnia's church registers before 1806 are not on film anywhere and must be asked for at the parish. for the civil registers themselves, go to antenati rather than here: the same material, published by the archivio di stato di udine, without the gate.
the other collection — and it is the one that reaches the twentieth century

everything above is familysearch, and familysearch stops. its croatian films were made from the state archives, and its birth registers were cut at the hundred-year line as it stood when the filming was done: crikvenica births end in 1896, senj in 1894, bribir and grižane in 1886. a second collection does not stop there, and this archive had not used it. hr-hda-1448, the zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji — the supplementary microfilm collection of registers and family lists — held by the hrvatski državni arhiv in zagreb, with its own searchable finding aid on arhiv.hr.

registers of every denomination from the whole territory of croatia, from the middle of the sixteenth century to the first half of the twentieth, plus roman catholic books from bosnia and herzegovina. filming began in 1985 with the hda's own collection hr-hda-883 and was then extended outward to every other holder — state archives, church archives, parish offices, civil registry offices and monasteries. most of it was shot in the hda's central photographic laboratory, and part of it in the microfilming laboratory of the državni arhiv u pazinu — the same laboratory that answered this family's letter in 2021.
why it goes further than familysearch

because it filmed the matični uredi — the civil registry offices that took custody of the parish books after 1946 — as well as the parishes and the archives. the registry office copy of a parish register is the same book, and it was not subject to the same restriction. that single difference is the whole gain, and it is worth years.
what you get, and what you then do

the finding aid returns, for each volume: place, denomination, kind of register, period, holding institution, the roll signature (e.g. zm-34j/251), the topographic mark (m-5976), and whether a digital copy exists. it does not show images. material is read in the hda reading room — digitised rolls on the reader computers, the rest on microfilm readers, maximum ten units a day — or ordered by e-mail to info@arhiv.hr quoting place, kind, period, roll signature and topographic mark. copies are charged for by the published tariff.

proložac — the imotski parish

listed here because it is where the dalmatian family's own ground is. donji proložac is where the franciscans of the imotski monastery came from — the fifteen friars and six hundred people zuane ivan franceschi took onto his estate at dobrče in january 1715 — and there is a frančeski stone in the churchyard. the registers run unbroken from 1853 to 1949, and everything from 1892 onward is digitised.

what to order, in order
the one book to order first

crikvenica, status animarum, twentieth century. roll zm-34j/251, topographic mark m-5976, župni ured crikvenica, digitised. a status animarum is a household census: it lists a house, its head, his wife, and every child under them with a birth date beside each name. it is the book that gave this archive the whole of gračišće house 24 — the midwife, the mason and the eleven children — in one opening. a twentieth-century crikvenica volume should hold josip defranceschi's household on the kvarner in the same form, and if it does it answers the zo…, the pold… and the ruža of the monument in a single page, without ever needing the missing baptisms.

crikvenica, marriages 1909–1947. roll zm-34j/362, mark m-6957, matični ured crikvenica, digitised. ruža defranceschi, born 1903, married a jarmacki and died in 1939. her marriage falls squarely inside this book, and a croatian marriage entry of that period names both parents of both parties. one line settles whether she is josip and ana's daughter. added 27 october 2026: the book also holds the marriage of anton rudolf defranceschi and uršula kovačina, thought to be 21 june 1912 (the geni tree's date); the finding aid, searched again that day, still lists it as digitised.

crikvenica, deaths 1909–1928. roll zm-34j/363, mark m-6958, digitised. if the pold… born 1901 died young, he is here — and the death column would give his age and his parents. the register also runs through the influenza of 1918 and the whole of the first war.
and what will still be missing

crikvenica births 1897–1908 are in neither collection. either that volume was never filmed, or it did not survive. if the three books above do not answer the question, the remaining step is the parish office at crikvenica itself, or the rijeka archdiocesan archive — a letter, not a search.
a note on method — how to read an unindexed image properly

most of what this archive still wants is in images nobody has indexed, and the ordinary way to look at them — the viewer in a browser window — shows a 6000-pixel register page shrunk to about 600 pixels, which is unreadable for handwriting. there is a better way and it is worth writing down. familysearch serves every image as a deep zoom pyramid: an xml descriptor at /service/records/storage/deepzoomcloud/dz/v1//image.xml giving the master dimensions, and 256-pixel tiles beneath it at /image_files//_.jpg. from a signed-in session the tiles for any chosen rectangle can be fetched and composed onto a canvas at true resolution, so a single column of a register can be read as clearly as if the book were open on the desk. that is how entry 17 of the imotski deaths for 1845 was read. it needs a signed-in session and it respects the same access rules as the viewer — it is the same images, at the size they were photographed.

hrvatski državni arhiv, hr-hda-1448, zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji, searched through the finding aid at arhiv.hr on 8 september 2026 for crikvenica and proložac across all seven kinds of register. the collection description, the abbreviations and the ordering procedure are quoted from that page. nothing here has been read yet: this is a list of what exists and where it is, which is the step this archive keeps finding is missing.

/map/.title: The Map — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 1394 places · 7771 register volumes catalogued · 1031 people placed · 194 burials

one map and four layers. where are the record books and how far have we got with them; where can this archive put a named person; where is the family actually in the ground; and where does a record merely name somebody of the name on one day. switch any of them on or off. a place that answers more than one question is still one dot, and it wears the colour of the rarest answer it has — so with everything on, the records, the graves and the people stand out of the shelf rather than hiding under it.
three layers — switch any of them on or off
red through amber to green is the shelf, and red means nobody has opened it violet and pink is our people blue is the ground
click any marker. bigger markers hold more people.

1394 places, merged out of 1527 markers across four sources. 96 answer more than one of the three questions and 20 answer all three — and with every layer on, those are the ones wearing the rarer colour.

in no catalogue at allcatalogued, never openedresearched, books unopeneda volume of its own readevery volume readthe documented linecarnia — where it may startistria, where the name isother families of the namethe senj and karlobag sidewhere they wenta headstone, photographeda line in a burial registerboth, at one placea record names somebody here
why there is one map here and not three

this archive had grown three maps off the same ground. a map of the record books. a map of the people. a map of the graves. each was built by its own script, each geocoded its own place names, and each had its own legend — so the same town was a dot on three pages and the reader had to hold all three in their head to see what was actually there.
1245 + 165 + 69 markers are 1394 places. 96 of them answer more than one question and 20 answer all three: rijeka, ližnjan, pazin, poreč, omiš, split, pula, rovinj, bakar, kaštelir, sovinjak and tar.

rijeka is the case for merging. on one page it now says: sixty-nine register volumes catalogued and not one of them opened; ninety-six people the archive can put here; and twenty-three burials. those were three separate facts on three separate pages, and the third of them — that we have twenty-three burials in a town whose registers we have never read — is only visible when they sit together.

the layers change the colour. they never change the panel. click any marker, with any combination switched on, and it tells you everything it has: the registers, the people, the graves and the records together.

the fourth layer is a different kind of claim, and it is drawn that way. the shelf, our people and the ground are all statements about where this family is. findmypast is not: a census line, a landing, a marriage licence is a record of somebody of the name at a place on one day. 156 such records stand on 31 places, in amber, and the panel calls them what they are — named in a record here, not who the archive puts here. a 1913 arrival at ellis island must never be allowed to look like a home. a further 21 records name only a state or a country and get no dot at all, for the same reason.

a place that answers two questions is still one dot. drawing it twice is exactly what merging the three maps was for. it takes the colour of the rarest question it answers among the layers that are on — the ground before our people, our people before the shelf. there are 1,235 shelf places, 167 with people and 61 with graves, so the rare thing is the thing worth seeing and the common thing is the ground it sits on. rijeka answers all three and wears the burial colour; gologorica answers two and wears the line's; senjska draga answers one and is sand.

every view of this map is a link. the layers, the basemap, whatever is typed in the find box, which filters are switched off and where the map is looking all live in the address bar, so a view can be sent to somebody rather than only remembered for you. every parish where a book has actually been opened is six places and one link; so is the ground alone, on satellite. the button says copy link to this view.
it was a switch for a day — one question at a time, and asking a second put the first away. david: «can our map rather layer the shelf, our people and the ground?»
the old addresses still work. /research-map/, /atlas/ and /graves-map/ all land here.

and there was a map before any of these. the google my map this family drew over years, imported whole from its kml and kept exactly as it was drawn — pins the atlas has no place for, the movements david traced by hand, and the links that have since died. it is not a fourth layer, because it is not this archive's reading of anything: it is the map that came first, kept as a record of what was already known before any of this was built.
one provider at a time

the map above is every provider at once. these show one each, with the colours meaning exactly what they mean here — a parish that is sand on the familysearch view and absent from pazin's is a parish whose books are filmed but whose originals nobody has listed.

the second question: the towns of our people

ask the map about our people and every marker re-colours. 165 towns, holding 1031 placements of named people, and 113 of the 165 are outside croatia altogether — mione and gologorica, but also torrington, memphis, pfullingen, broken hill, adelaide, horsham and brisbane. use the whole world button at the top right of the map to see them.

the six colours here are not coverage states. they say how the archive knows a place — the documented line, carnia, the istrian sweep, the senj and karlobag side, the diaspora, and other families of the name. weight on this map is not kinship: a parish can hold forty people of the surname and be connected to this family by nothing whatever.
32 of these towns also carry a shelf, and 20 carry all three questions at once. they are one marker, not two: click it and it tells you the registers, the people and the graves together.

nothing here is geocoded twice. the three maps this page replaced each resolved their own place names; they now share one set of places, and the coordinates come from a single gazetteer committed to the repository rather than from three different files in three different states.
living people are on this map by name and by town, and by nothing else.
where this map comes from, and what it is worth
it is david's map, rebuilt because the original cannot be kept

david built a google my map of the croatian record books over several years — familysearch first, then the other confessions — and drew in a second layer of croatian genealogists working their own parishes. a my map dies with the account, and it cannot be crawled.

so it was exported and rebuilt here. that export is where the trouble starts. the kml holds 1,709 placemarks, but only 247 of them carry coordinates — and of its 1,196 record-book places, only ninety do. the rest are address pins, which google geocodes when it draws the map and not before. as a backup, the export is about eight per cent of a map.

what every pin does carry is a familysearch browse waypoint — 1,194 of them — and a waypoint is the key that opens a parish's shelf. that turned out to be the last thing his map was needed for. each confession root in the collection lists its own parishes, so the list is now walked from familysearch's own tree instead: 1,333 shelves, against his 1,288, and ždala through zvoneće that his export never had because the root returns exactly one thousand and stops.

his map still supplies what the tree does not: the confessions, drawn as he separated them, and ninety coordinates. the rest of the coordinates came from the geonames country dumps for croatia and its seven neighbours — 1245 of 1286 places placed, without a single geocoding call.
41 places are still unplaced — they are mostly compound parish names like split-lučac or sv. jakov-šiljevica that no gazetteer carries as one string.
what the colours mean — and what they do not

the colour says how far we have got with the shelf, and nothing else. sand is catalogued and never opened. teal is researched and its own books never opened — real work, done from print and index rather than from the registers. gold means a volume of this parish's own registers has been read. green is every volume, and there is not a single green marker on this map.

that is the honest picture and it is meant to be uncomfortable. 1252 places catalogued and untouched · 23 researched without their registers being opened · 6 with a volume of their own read · 0 finished · 18 volumes of 7771 read one by one.

teal is new, and it exists because gold was lying. twenty-two markers were gold and twenty of them had never had a single register volume opened. they were gold because the search register names them — a local history of žminj; a migration paper that lists žminj among the towns the carni settled at. reading a book about a parish and reading the parish's own registers are two different acts, and a scale whose legend says «how far we have got with the shelf» must not paint the first in the colour of the second. logged as a correction.

this is the third scale this map has worn. it carried three coverage states until the cataloguing finished and turned 1,219 of them the same colour; then it shaded by depth — one or two volumes against ten or more — which looked better and said less. a parish with forty volumes nobody has opened and a parish with two nobody has opened are in the same state. depth now lives in the panel, in words, next to the sentence that says whether anybody has read it.

«read right through» can only be claimed where this archive knows which volumes were read — which today is antenati alone, because its catalogue carries a per-volume flag. everywhere else a reading is recorded against the place, not the book, so the best that can honestly be said is «started». that is on the work list.

and the map cannot see what is filed abroad. a croatian town's registers sit wherever the state that kept them filed them: čakovec is under «csáktornya», in a hungarian county, inside a collection named for slovenia; five croatian istrian parishes are inside an italian one. croatia, filed under other countries lists what the walk of all 3,488 familysearch collections turned up.

grey is «in no catalogue at all», and every grey marker on it is now a checked negative. they are places this archive walked the familysearch catalogue for and found nothing — grožnjan, lindar, motovun, višnjan, villa santina and pirovac. a checked negative is worth more than a blank.

two of them used to be grey for a worse reason. brekinjska and hrastovac were evangelical, and this archive had written that it «never found the evangelical root in familysearch's waypoint tree» — the shelf was not walked, not proved empty. the root was found on 15 september and it was never hidden: the collection's own waypoint list names it — evangelical (evangelička crkva), one of ten confession roots. it holds six parishes and seven volumes, brekinjska and hrastovac among them, and all seven are now openable from this map. the lesson is the honest one — the archive had not looked in the place the collection tells you to look.

the first cut of this map used three colours — not walked, catalogued, read. it worked for about a day, and then the cataloguing finished and 1,219 of 1,239 places went gold. a map where everything is one colour is not a map, so the shading was re-cut to carry something that still varies.

researched, books unopened means a row in the search register names the place as a source or a destination — and no volume of its registers has been read. that flag is derived by matching place names against the register's own source and destination fields — never against its prose, which mentions places for all sorts of reasons. a handful of names that are also ordinary croatian words or surnames are excluded by hand. it is approximate, and it will be wrong in both directions until every row is tagged properly.
the number this page exists to show
6 of 1286. that is how many places on this map have had anything at all read out of them — 0.5 per cent. the other 1252 are catalogued down to the volume and untouched.

seven providers, and they are not the same kind of thing. familysearch — croatia — 1204 of 1204 places walked, 5299 volumes · familysearch — udine — 26 of 26 places walked, 642 volumes · pazin state archive — 14 of 14 places walked, 1151 volumes · antenati — 3 of 3 places walked, 74 volumes · familysearch — pola & trieste — 9 of 9 places walked, 36 volumes · matricula — the littoral — 3 of 3 places walked, 9 volumes · familysearch — međimurje — 46 of 46 places walked, 365 volumes · familysearch — delnice — 1 of 1 places walked, 6 volumes · familysearch catalogue — 75 of 75 places walked, 189 volumes.

familysearch is broad and shallow: a title, a year span, and nothing name-indexed. antenati is the opposite shape again — two comuni, fifty-nine volumes, and every one of them a book to be turned by hand, because the italian portal publishes no index of names at all. its arks sit on a different host from everything else here, so the map sends you to the archive's own list rather than dressing them up as familysearch links. pazin is narrow and deep, and it is the only one that admits what it has not done — 154 of its volumes are marked «not digitised». that column means «not digitised by pazin» and nothing more: checked against the films, 116 of the 154 have been photographed by familysearch anyway, and only 38 are books that two catalogues agree nobody has filmed. every one of the 7771 catalogued volumes that familysearch has filmed is now openable from this map — the ark harvest finished on 15 september, 5,482 of 5,482, with nothing left outstanding.

this paragraph said something else for about an hour. it reported that thirty-four of the forty kvarner parishes had never been walked — and they had been. the builder was reading the wrong field: kvarner keeps its volumes under a field called films, like dalmatia, and carries a stale books title-list on six of its forty parishes. reading books invented a gap that did not exist and under-counted the archive by thirty-four parishes and 201 volumes. logged as a correction.
where two providers describe the same place, and disagree

30 places on this map are described by two real shelves, and they are the only places where a hole can be seen at all. it was six, and all six were in istria — pazin's own register list against familysearch's films. it is 30 now, and the comparisons have multiplied with the providers: istria against pazin, međimurje against the slovenian collection, croatian istria against the italian one, delnice against the main croatian shelf.

339 volumes are listed by one holder, from before 1890, that the other has not filmed. those are the ones worth caring about — books on a shelf with no photograph of them anywhere. pazin's own list marks 154 volumes «not digitised», of which 38 are filmed by nobody else either — the short list actually worth posting, set out place by place and holder by holder on the undigitised.

448 more fall after 1890. they are not a gap. familysearch withholds recent registers for privacy and the other holder lists them because it holds the paper. counting those as missing film would have turned a real finding of 339 volumes into a fake one of 787.

the test is deliberately strict about what counts as a shelf. the library catalogue is not one. its records are bibliographic lines that can span three centuries — «matična knjiga, 1568-1917» is a single row standing for a parish's whole holdings — and letting it into the comparison inflated this test to seventy-eight places and 1,572 volumes, almost all of it a catalogue entry being read as a claim about a particular year. it is excluded, and the number came back down.

and strict about what counts as cover. an index is not a register and an allegato is not a register; a marriage index for 1815–1830 does not make the marriage book for those years present. only births, marriages and deaths are compared, and only against their own kind.

volume counts in brackets. a span is merged from consecutive volumes, so «births 1629–1714 (5)» is five books covering that stretch with nothing of their kind on film across it.
what the four marks beside a volume actually claim

every volume in a panel carries one of four marks, and all four are statements about this archive's own reading — none of them is a statement about the book, or about what anybody else has done with it.

● read — somebody here opened it and went through it end to end. there are two such volumes outside antenati: gračišće's baptism book 1667–1745, read image by image off pazin's microfilm, and donji proložac's deaths 1837–1859, swept page by page.
◐ part read — opened, and some of it read: a stretch of years, a run of images, an index followed. svetvinčenat's 1663–1708 and one vodnjan reel.

○ never opened — this archive keeps a per-volume record for this parish, and this volume is not in it. nobody here has read it. it is a checked negative about our work, and about nothing else: the book is filmed, it is linkable from this panel, and for all this archive knows somebody read it yesterday in pazin.
· not written down — the archive keeps no per-volume record for this parish at all, so it cannot say either way. most of this map is in this state.
the difference between the last two is the difference between a negative and a silence, and it is the whole reason there are four marks rather than three.

and the honest limit of «never opened». it is only as good as the ledger behind it. a volume somebody read before that ledger existed, and never wrote down, would show as never opened — so the state means «not recorded as read», and the archive's answer to that is to record readings the day they happen rather than the week after.
matricula — the nine littoral volumes, and where each one opens

matricula online publishes the austrian protestant registers of the küstenland, free and without an account, and until 17 september no map this archive keeps had them. nine volumes, four congregations, 1848 to 1918.

pola is this family's ground and trieste and gorizia are not, so the provider is drawn as what it is — a shelf that mostly overlaps nothing else, in the way antenati and the delnice films already do. they do not open from a marker, because the panel builds familysearch addresses and these are not familysearch; they open from here.

the forty-one places this map cannot draw

1,285 parishes are catalogued and 1,244 of them have a dot. the other forty-one carry 130 volumes between them and cannot be put on the ground, because no gazetteer this archive can reach knows where they are.

they are small croatian parishes — trojstvo, viduševac, taborsko, sobotica, prvić šepurina, juraj u trnju, hrnetić, vlaška kapela — and a handful of institutions that are not settlements at all: bolnica dubrovnik, nahodište dubrovnik and nahodište split, which are a hospital and two foundling houses and should in the end hang on their towns.

what was tried. geonames files a village too small for a settlement record under its church or its railway stop instead, and reading those classes as well as the populated places rescued four — mađarevo is a railway stop, mandalina a railway halt, komarevo a locality. a stream or a hill of the same name is not the village and is deliberately not used: the glogovnica in the dumps is a river.
the rest need a croatian source and a person, not another pass of the same script. they are listed by the place audit, which runs the two tests that found six parishes standing in the wrong country.
«gap» and «not filmed anywhere» are opposites, and neither means «no link»
three different silences turn up in one panel and they were easy to confuse, so here is each one.

gap — no marriages register listed anywhere, 6 years. nobody has a book of that kind for those years. not pazin, not familysearch, not antenati, not anyone this archive walks. the book is missing, or it never existed. this is the row that should make you unhappy; it is tinted for exactly that reason. (it said «no register filmed» until 16 september, which was the wrong word and made it look like the next one.)

not filmed anywhere. the opposite. the book exists — a catalogue names it, a shelf holds it — and nobody has photographed it. nothing is lost; it is simply not readable from a desk. these are set out one by one on the undigitised, and they are the ones worth writing a letter about.

a volume with no link at all. a third thing again, and the commonest. gračišće is the example: thirty-two volumes, every one of them listed by the pazin state archive, which publishes a register list and no images — and familysearch's croatian collection does not hold the parish. so there is no address to link to and there never was one to harvest. the panel now says so in those words. where a place's volumes do come from a filmed collection and still show no link, that is the other case: an address this archive has not fetched yet, and the panel says that instead.
so: a gap is a hole in the record. not filmed is a book waiting for a camera. no link is a book waiting for a reader to travel, or an errand this archive has not run.
what a marker tells you now: the shelf, by record type, with the holes named

the panel used to list a parish's volumes in whatever order the providers were walked — births, births, deaths, births again — and a reader had to hold thirteen year-ranges in their head to see that nothing survives between two of them. it now collapses them into a coverage timeline, one block per record type, and names the gaps.
176 of the 1245 places on the map have a real hole in at least one register series — 308 of them in all. 559 have none: every year between their first volume and their last is covered by something.

a one- or two-year hole is usually not a hole. a volume titled «1716–1816» sitting beside one that ends in 1714 leaves 1715 uncovered on paper and almost certainly not in fact, so those are marked as a labelling artefact rather than cried over. the exception is a parish whose volumes each cover a single year — the napoleonic comuni are all like this — where a missing year is a missing book. that rule is why mione's lost 1807 shows on the map as three gaps and not as three shrugs.

an index is not cover, and neither is an allegato. they are counted separately at the foot of each panel, because a marriage index for 1815–1830 does not make the marriage book for those years present.
the confessions, as david separated them
the map keeps his own layers, because the confession decides which archive holds the book and in what language it is written.
roman catholic — 997 · orthodox — 240 · civil — 53 · military — 17 · jewish — 16 · greek catholic — 15 · reformed — 11 · evangelical — 6
croatian registers are not all catholic and a family that looks absent from one set can be sitting in another. the 240 orthodox parishes in particular are a body this archive has never touched.
and a layer that is not records at all

his map carries a tenth layer of 372 croatian genealogists — each with a researcher number, the parish they work, their confession, and the surnames they are chasing. it is a directory of living people working the same ground, and it is not on this map, because people are not record books and because the archive's rule on living people applies to strangers as much as to family.
it is kept in the data, unpublished, and the useful question it answers is narrow: is anybody else working our parishes?
our people: reading the second question

nine places carry the whole documented descent, and seven of them sit inside a hundred kilometres of each other. the family did not move much until 1939, and then it moved to three continents in a decade.
the cluster is not the line
rijeka, pula and ližnjan carry far more of the surname than gračišće ever did — and none of them is connected to this family by any document. weight on the map is not kinship.
the gap is the argument
between mione in 1679 and gologorica in 1711 there is nothing but a house with a date on it. that two-hundred-kilometre jump is the one thing this archive cannot yet prove.
what a people marker means, and what it does not

a place is coloured under our people because somebody in the roster is attached to it — by a record, a headstone, a register or a family tree. it does not mean that person was born there, and where the archive has only a parish it has used the parish. names in three languages are folded together: almissa is omiš, vitipolis is rijeka, promontore is premantura, spalato is split.
1031 placements across 165 towns, and 143 of those towns carry at least one named person.

living people are on this map by name and by town, and by nothing else. the rule until 15 september 2026 was no place of residence, which kept every living relative off the map entirely. it is now name and town, never a date — and all 27 living people this archive names are placed.

8 of them are at johannesburg and 3 at brisbane, and two are at both. that is the shape of it: the family left senj for the rand, and one household of the three went on to australia — the aunt and her husband, the uncle's widow and his daughters, and the cousins are all still in south africa. not one of them has a date on this map, and none ever will.
the ground: the third question, and the finding in it
the two colours never meet, and that is the finding
96 places have a photographed headstone. 98 have a burial register entry. not one place has both.

that is not a quirk of the data. it is the emigration, drawn: the people who stayed are in parish books and have no findable grave; the people who left are under stones and were never in a croatian register. the register entries run 1619 to 1997 and are almost all istrian and kvarner — rijeka, ližnjan, poreč, pula, kaštelir. the headstones run 1844 to 2024 and are almost all somewhere else — connecticut, rome, queens, broken hill, ticino.

the green colour in that legend has no members. it is left there because the day a place turns green — a grave found in a parish this archive has read — is the day one of these two halves joins the other.

4 burials have no place to pin. thirty-six are entered as «croatia, parish not named» and four as «not stated», read out of indexes that record a death without recording where. they are counted on the burials page and deliberately absent here: a map that guessed at a parish would be worse than a map with a hole in it.

the research map was built from familysearch's croatian church-book collection. croatian places also sit inside italian, hungarian, austrian and slovenian collections, under names the map has never heard of.

this archive's map says it shows «every parish in croatia whose registers are on film». it did not, and it never had. it showed every parish in one collection — croatia, church books, 1516–1994 — plus three sources added by hand.

familysearch publishes 3,488 collections. the whole list was walked on 15 september 2026 and every one that could touch this family's ground was opened. the result is below, and it is meant to be complete rather than interesting: where a collection holds nothing for us, that is recorded too, so nobody walks it again.

the short version: a croatian town is filed wherever the state that kept its registers filed it, under the name that state used. čakovec is under csáktornya, in a hungarian county, inside a collection named for slovenia.

6.85 million records, 17.4 million persons — and no browse tree at all. it is a name index, not a filmed collection, so it cannot be walked by place.

it does not cover the austrian littoral. searched inside the collection: 289 defranceschi records, and every named place among them is tyrolean — bozen, salorno, tirolo, st. florian bei linz. not one in istria, gorizia or trieste. the same for three istrian surnames tested alongside: sestan (zwettl, longomosso, feldkirch), kostesich (bozen), miškulin (bozen).
so the hole stays open. gračišće, gologorica and pićan are not here either, and this was the most promising place they could have been.

two things worth keeping anyway. there is a whole tyrolean defranceschi population — 289 records around bozen and salorno — which is a separate family of the same name and a standing warning against arguing from a surname. and one record reads «vukovar, sriem, croatia, austria», so slavonian places do appear in this collection even though istrian ones do not.

hungary, civil registration, 1895–1980 ↗
33 hungarian counties — abaúj-torna, arad, bács-bodrog, baranya … vas, veszprém, zala. not one croatian-slavonian county, and no fiume.
it does not reach croatia, and the reason is constitutional rather than archival.

hungary introduced civil registration in 1895. croatia-slavonia did not. under the nagodba it ran its own administration and kept the parish registers as the legal civil record until 1946 — which is why familysearch's croatian collection is church books, and why there is no croatian civil-registration collection anywhere to find.
and it explains međimurje. međimurje's civil registers exist from 1895 because međimurje was administered as part of zala county — as hungary proper, not as croatia. that is the whole anomaly.

checked rather than assumed: zala here holds 235 districts and not one of csáktornya, perlak, nedelicz, stridó, kottori or légrád — they are in the slovenia-titled collection instead, so the two do not overlap. the 16 defranceschi records inside are budapest, esztergom and sopron.

what this page is, and is not

three of these are now on the map — pola and trieste, prekmurje and međimurje, and delnice — as their own providers, each place shown under the name its catalogue uses as well as the name it goes by today. čakovec and «csáktornya» are one dot.

and the merge paid for itself immediately. with the parish books and the hungarian civil registers on the same marker, čakovec shows a four-year gap in 1891–1894 across births, marriages and deaths — the interval between the church books closing and civil registration opening. neither catalogue could show that on its own.

the lesson is about method rather than about any one collection. a map built from a collection named for a country will show the places that country's archives filmed, and nothing else. the border moved five times in a century and the paperwork did not follow it. every place on this family's ground was, at some point, filed by venice, by vienna, by budapest, by rome and by zagreb — and familysearch files by whoever kept the book.

croatia, filed under other countries
every familysearch collection that could hold a record for this family's ground, opened one by one — including the ones that hold nothing, so nobody walks them twice.
the research map was built from one collection — croatia, church books, 1516–1994 — and its standfirst claimed to show «every parish in croatia whose registers are on film». it never did.

so on 15 september 2026 the whole of familysearch was walked: all 3,488 historical record collections, every title read, and every one that could plausibly hold a record for this family's ground opened through its browse tree or searched inside.
this page is the complete result, including the failures. a negative is recorded as carefully as a find, because the point of it is that nobody has to walk that collection again.
five collections hold places on this family's ground, and all five are now on the map.

croatia, church books (the original) · croatia, delnice deanery — a second croatian collection nobody knew was there, browsable only by film · italy, pola and trieste — five croatian istrian parishes filed by italy · slovenia, prekmurje and međimurje — 46 districts, nearly all croatian towns, under hungarian names · and italy, udine, already here for carnia.
thirty-nine others were opened and hold nothing for us.
what is not there at all
there is no serbian, bosnian, montenegrin or yugoslav collection in familysearch. not one, in 3,488. the dalmatian hinterland has no coverage from that direction.
and croatia itself has exactly two collections. for a country with a thousand-year parish record, that is the whole of it.
why austria and hungary both failed, which is the useful part

both looked like the obvious hiding place for gračišće, gologorica and pićan — the three parishes at the centre of this family that the croatian collection does not hold. both came back empty, and between them they explain why.

hungary introduced civil registration in 1895; croatia-slavonia did not, keeping the parish books as the legal record until 1946. so there is no croatian civil registration anywhere to find — it was never created. and austria's collection is a name index of the alpine dioceses, not of the littoral, which stopped being austrian in 1918 and whose registers stayed in istria.
on present evidence those three parishes are filmed nowhere at all. pazin holds the paper, and that is the only route left.
and a warning the walk handed over for free
defranceschi is not a rare name. it is a veneto name.
9,626 records at padova · 6,546 at venice · 2,076 at verona · 1,285 at treviso · 289 in tyrol, around bozen and salorno.

none of them is this family, and none can be shown not to be without a document. the mione households already proved the surname was a population rather than a family in one valley. this is the same proof at the scale of a province, and it is why this archive will not bridge two places on a name.
5 hold places on this family's ground. the other 39 were opened and hold nothing — recorded so that nobody opens them again.

/undigitised/.title: The hundred and fifty-four — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 154 volumes pazin has not digitised · 38 of them filmed by nobody else either
the hundred and fifty-four
every register in pazin's own list marked «not digitised» — and, for each, whether anybody else has filmed it. most of them somebody has. the ones nobody has are the short list worth a letter.
why this list is different from everything else here
every other source this archive uses says what it has. pazin is the only one that says what it hasn't. its register list carries a digitised column, and 154 of its entries say no.

that single column is worth more than the rest of the catalogue put together, because it converts an absence into an address. familysearch not holding a book tells you nothing — it might be at pazin, it might be lost, it might never have existed. pazin saying «not digitised» tells you the book is real, where it is, and what it is called.
42 of the 154 are in parishes on our own line — gologorica, gračišće, pazin, pićan, svetvinčenat.
and a sentence this page carried for a day that was not true
this page opened by saying these were «books that exist, on a shelf in istria, and cannot be read from anywhere else». for 116 of the 154, that is wrong.

pazin's column means «not digitised by pazin». it says nothing about anybody else, and checked against familysearch's films of the same parish, record type and years, 116 of these volumes are already photographed — often inside a longer film that swallows several of pazin's shelfmarks at once. barban's births 1716–1750, 1750–1781 and 1781–1816 are three pazin volumes and one familysearch reel.
38 are left. those are the ones where two catalogues agree that nothing has been photographed, and they are the only ones worth a letter.

the overlap is inferred, not proved. same parish, same record type, overlapping years is a strong match and not an identity — a parish copy and a diocesan copy can both exist. but it is more than enough to stop calling all 154 unreachable.
the 38 nobody has filmed
pazin has not digitised these and no film of that parish, record type and period turns up anywhere else this archive can reach. this is the list worth posting.

/antenati/.title: Antenati — the Carnia registers — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: 3 comuni · 74 volumes · 16 of them read · no name index on any of them
antenati — the carnia registers

the napoleonic and austrian civil registers for mione and ovaro, held by the archivio di stato di udine and photographed by the portale antenati, with mieli next door where the numbering put it. every line below opens the book at its first image.

antenati (portale antenati, archivio di stato di udine) — the napoleonic and austrian civil registers for the carnia comuni this family came out of. every volume here is an ark that opens the book at page one; the portal has no name index for any of them. every entry below was fetched one at a time from its own catalogue page.
why this page exists at all

antenati publishes no index of names. there is no search box that will find a de franceschi in these books; there is only the book, and the reader, and the hand. a volume here is a thing to be turned page by page, which is why the archive counts a register as read only when someone has gone through it, and why so few of them are.

every volume below was checked one by one. an earlier version of this page assumed the portal numbers its arks one comune per block, and named series spans from that assumption. it does not: an_ua667510 to 667513 are mieli, in a different comune altogether, sitting immediately before mione in the numbering. each ark here now carries how its identity is known.

six series. the marriages, the banns and the deaths each run nine volumes — 1806, then 1808 to 1815. the births run four and stop at 1810. both sets of indices stop at 1812, and only one volume of death allegati survives, for 1809. 1807 is absent from every mione series.
