/carlos-book/.title: Carlo's Book — The Defranceschi Archive
blocks: l'istria: note storiche · parenzo, 1879

the family's historian wrote a history of his province and it has been online, free, all along. read whole, it gives the home parishes a diocese, the seget estate a chain of owners and a roll of its people — and stays silent about carnia.

carlo de franceschi is the family's historian, and until now this archive had used him second-hand: quoted in the kandler literature, in the blasonario, in puhmajer's monograph on the seget house. the book itself is online and free. reading it whole does three things — it puts the family's home parishes into an ecclesiastical world nobody had described here, it gives the seget estate a documented chain of owners and a list of the people who worked it, and it is conspicuously silent about the one thing the family most wants him to have said.
a negative worth publishing
what the book does not say

carlo's own published history of istria never claims the family came out of carnia. the words carnia and cargna appear twice in 524 pages, both times about something else — a parish priest called «carnialico» who destroyed roman inscriptions at s. andrea, and a latin tag about mortal flesh that the scanner's software misread. there is no passage on friulian settlers named de franceschi, no mention of mione, muina or ovaro, and no origin story of any kind for his own family.

this does not overturn the carnia thesis. carlo gave that account in his memoirs and in the letter this archive holds, not in this book, and a public history of the province is not where a nineteenth-century secretary of the provincial assembly would set down his own pedigree. but the archive has been treating carlo as a single witness speaking with one voice, and he is not: the historian who published in 1879 and the man who wrote privately about his ancestors are the same person choosing to say different things in different places. where the carnia page says the claim is testimony and not record, that now has a sharper edge. see «back to carnia».

the one friulian thread the book does carry is unrelated to the family: it describes the furlan dialect of the interior as roman speech fused with carnic, and the road that brought friulian soldiers, podestàs and merchants into istria for four centuries. — back to carnia →
the diocese nobody had named

gallignana and gologorica — the two parishes this archive's line runs through — were not in the diocese of pisino. they were in the diocese of pedena, the smallest in istria, and carlo lists it entire.

the diocese of pedena, entire: pedena, gallignana, lindaro, novacco, cerovglie, chersicla, gollogorizza, cherbune, berdo, cepich, s. ivanaz, grimalda — twelve parishes, with the vicariates of sarez, scopliaco, grobnico, previs, tupliaco and gradigne.
gallignana held the only chapter

trieste had collegiate chapters at muggia, umago, pinguente and rozzo; parenzo at rovigno, montona, valle and four more; pola at nine places. «nella diocesi di pedena unicamente a gallignana con arciprete» — in the diocese of pedena, at gallignana alone, with an archpriest. apart from the cathedral itself, the family's home parish was the ecclesiastical head of its diocese.
and it was a town, not a village

in the diet of the county of pisino the bench of communities seated only those places holding the title of città: antignana, bersez, pedena, gallignana, lovrana and pisino. six. gallignana sat in the prelates' bench too, through its chapter. the place the registers call a hill parish was one of six towns in the county, with two seats in its parliament.
a quarrel over the parish, 1324–1335

the parish priest of gallignana, giovanni of capodistria, died, and the bishop of pedena failed to name a successor within the canonical term. then the bishop died too. the vicar of the vacant diocese was nicolò, pievano of gollogorizza — the priest of this archive's other parish — and on 3 november 1324 he conferred the parish of gallignana on a priest cernaz of pisino superiore. the patriarch bertrando held the appointment void and ordered the abbot of rosazzo to install jacopo sembiante instead, which happened on 24 march 1335. eleven years, and the two parishes this line comes from are the two ends of the argument.
the bishops' own style

the simple benefice of gollogorizza was founded in 1444 by currado schuel, provost of pisino. after its last holder, don clemente bioz, died, its revenues were assigned to the bishops of pedena — and from then on those bishops signed themselves «dominus gollaegoritiae, scopliaci et tupliaci», lord of gologorica, škopljak and tupljak. a village of a few dozen houses is in a bishop's title.
what the bishops took

at gallignana the bishop drew half the fixed wine render called the episcopal census, and half the cheeses. at pedena the whole tithe of grain, wine and lambs. the count of pisino took the rest — money and animals.
deeper than the church

carlo, following kandler, reads the territory of the diocese of pedena as the land of the secussi, one of the alpine peoples pliny counted among the most illustrious of their neighbours: chersicla, grimalda, previs, bottonega, sarez, novaco, cerovglie, gollogorizza, gradigne, berdo, carboneto, scopuliano, tupliano, lindaro, calliniana, pedena, half of gimino. roman inscriptions carrying plain roman names have been found at gollogorizza, as at bogliuno and cepich. the two parishes are on ground that has been a unit since before the romans arrived.
the parish under arms
when what as the book has it

may 1617 venetian troops besiege gallignana in the uskok war. trautmannsdorff rushed a relief force from gorizia under don baldassare maradas, who attacked on 14 may and forced the venetians back, took fianona and albona on the 20th — and, recalled to gorizia, left istria only after «assicurata gallignana», securing gallignana and reinforcing its garrison.

1617 raiders strip the territory of gollogorizza the venetian captain verzi, having burnt what was left of a village and killed an uskok holding a house with ten countrymen, «scorse il territorio di gollogorizza, ove predò 100 animali minuti ed alquanti grossi» — ran over the territory of gologorica and took a hundred small beasts and a few large.

1 january 1563 the priest of gallignana joins the croatian protestant press francesco claj, priest of gallignana, contracted at pisino with the reformers to revise and correct the croatian translations, which he later declared exact. he offered to help only «rimanendo in patria» — on condition of staying home. the vicar of pisino who signed with him, matteo zivcich, later turns up among the lutheran preachers posted through the province.

after the plagues bosnian and morlach families settled at gallignana among the smaller resettlements — gallignana, pisino, pisinvecchio, lindaro, zamasco and others took fewer than the big campaigns at antignana, corridico, terviso, vermo and gimino.
seget, in carlo's own words
the archive already had the cretan origin of the seget branch from petar puhmajer's monograph. here is the sentence puhmajer is citing, in its place — and the footnote under it, which is worth more.

il capitanio di raspo alessandro zorzi in data 15 febbraro 1604 investiva il capitano vincenzo cuchich da sebenico d'un corpo di terreni incolti della circonferenza di circa quattro miglia nel territorio di umago, sul quale furono da lui trasportate trenta famiglie da paesi turcheschi. il cuchich vendette nel 1623 la tenuta, che ora chiamasi di seghetto e giuba, ai n. u. valier di venezia, dai quali più tardi l'acquistò la nobile famiglia de franceschi, attuale posseditrice, emigrata dall'isola di candia dopo conquistata dai turchi nel 1669.

alessandro zorzi, captain of raspo, on 15 february 1604 invested captain vincenzo cuchich of sebenico with a body of uncultivated land some four miles in circumference in the territory of umago, onto which he brought thirty families from turkish lands. cuchich sold the estate — now called seghetto and giuba — in 1623 to the noble valier of venice, from whom it was later bought by the noble de franceschi family, its present owner, emigrated from the island of candia after the turks conquered it in 1669.
the footnote under it

«questa notizia la dobbiamo alla gentilezza del sig. giambattista de franceschi deputato al consiglio dell'impero, che la trasse dal proprio archivio domestico.» carlo's source is not a chronicle. it is giambattista de franceschi — a deputy to the imperial council in vienna — reading his own family's papers and passing them to a historian of the same surname. two de franceschi, one in parliament and one at the provincial assembly, settling their family's record between them in the 1870s.
and the people who worked it: seghetto di umago, 30 april 1764

giambattista sent carlo a second thing from that archive — the roll of colonist families then living on the estate, which carlo prints entire. these are the descendants of cuchich's thirty families. they are named, counted, and given their home cities, and every one of those cities is a place venice had lost or was losing to the ottomans.

a hundred and eleven people counted by name, plus three families whose provenance had already been forgotten by 1764. carlo adds that other greek families lived at giuba — the carciotti and the stradiotti — and that the melisana, atica and chitriza must have been foreigners too. coron, malvasia, nauplia, corinth, arta: this is the morea, emptied westward. the de franceschi came from crete to an estate already full of people who had come the same way.
the seget house and the branch that held it →
two more of the name, by two more roads
sabba de franceschi, of bologna

a ducal grant licensed leonardo fioravanti, sabba de franceschi and vincenzo dall'acqua, bolognese, to bring a hundred and twenty-four families to pola to break new ground. they undertook to purify the air, uncover springs and introduce new methods of agriculture, and got twenty years free of taxes and military service, and two fairs to be held in the amphitheatre. the earliest bearer of the name in istria this archive can date to a document, and he is neither istrian nor carnian.
franceschi at pola, «venuti da capodistria»

among the noble families living at pola before the plague of 1631 — locatelli, dragoni, sargo, albini, roberti, cassinati, barbabianca, bolis, marini, franceschi (come from capodistria), forlani, sozomeno. after the plague reduced the city to three hundred souls, these families either died out or settled elsewhere. a third, separate franceschi arrival, by a third road.

the archive has had four separate arrivals of this surname in istria and dalmatia and has treated them as a puzzle to be solved into one tree. carlo's book makes the opposite case without meaning to: a bolognese contractor at pola in 1562, a capodistrian family at pola before 1631, a cretan family buying seget after 1669, and a stonecutting household on the hill at gallignana. de franceschi is a patronymic — the sons of francesco — and it was formed independently wherever the name francesco was common, which was everywhere. the right question is not which trunk they all hang from. it is which of them this line actually is, and the registers answer that: gallignana.
on the texts, and a correction

two texts were used. the internet archive's google scan of the 1879 parenzo edition, item listrianotestor00frangoog, read through its ocr layer — which garbles accents, splits words and mangles the footnotes badly. and a clean transcription of several chapters published by istrianet.org from the arnaldo forni reprint, which the family has held since 2004 in its own files and which this archive did not open until it was pointed at it. where the two disagree the transcription is followed, and the roll of 1764 above has been corrected against it — a dozen of the colonists' names were previously printed here in their ocr-mangled forms. passages that survive only in the ocr are flagged as such in the text.
a hundred years later, a croatian historian argues with him for forty-six pages

david handed this archive a 475-page book on 9 september 2026: stjepan antoljak, «hrvati u prošlosti» — croats in the past — a collected volume by one of the leading croatian medievalists of the twentieth century. it had never been read here. its index has an entry for «franceschi de, c.» with sixteen page references, and what it shows is something this archive had not been able to show before: not that carlo is cited, but what happens when a serious opponent takes him seriously.
he is a source on every page of the slav settlement chapter

antoljak's long study of when and how the slavs came into istria cites «c. de franceschi, l'istria: note storiche, parenzo 1879» twenty-one times, at pages 24, 25, 33, 38, 41, 45, 47–49, 52, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64, 66 and 70 — and also his 1852 article «sulle varie popolazioni dell'istria» in the trieste paper «l'istria». he is quoted for the date istria fell to byzantium (539), for belisarius, for the charter of 1234 that names a «monte schiavo» opposite brtonigla, for the road called the «callis sclavonica», for the chronology of the lombard and avar raids. he is used exactly as a modern historian uses a nineteenth-century authority: constantly, and never quite trusted.
and antoljak catches him out

«…a drugim se navodom de franceschija da u listini iz iste godine piše villa sclavorum de longera, naprosto ne može poslužiti jer je netočno pročitan i tako iznesen.» — de franceschi's other citation, that a document of the same year reads villa sclavorum de longera, simply cannot serve, because it was misread and reported that way. the archive should say plainly what that is. it is the same failure this project keeps finding in its own work: a document read at speed, transcribed wrong, and then argued from. carlo did it in print in 1879 and it was still being corrected ninety years later.
the hard one, and it belongs on this page

«c. de franceschi 1885. godine toliko se zaboravlja kada piše da povijest pokazuje da istra nije bila nikada zauzeta od nekog slavenskog naroda ili da je takav njom vladao.» — in 1885 c. de franceschi so far forgets himself as to write that history shows istria was never occupied by any slav people, nor ruled by one. antoljak goes on: that although carlo uses constantine porphyrogenitus, he interprets him to suit himself; that he asserts the croats never crossed the border of istria and spread only as far as the river «tarsia» — and that carlo has confused the rječina at rijeka with the arsia, the raša, which is a different river eighty kilometres away and the whole point of the argument. this archive has called carlo the family's historian and leaned on him for the carnian origin, and will go on doing both. it should also say this. on the national question he was a partisan of the italian side of a bitter argument, and he was wrong in a way a specialist could demonstrate from the sources he himself was using. being wrong there does not make him wrong about his own family's origin — a man is a better witness to his great-grandfather's house than to the seventh century. but it is the reason this archive tests him rather than quotes him.
«prilično oprezni de franceschi»

not all of it is against him. elsewhere antoljak calls him «prilično oprezni de franceschi» — the fairly cautious de franceschi — for declining to credit an early slav presence that other writers assert freely. the same man, in the same book, is both the careless reader and the cautious one. that is what a real reputation looks like at a hundred years' distance.

stjepan antoljak, «hrvati u prošlosti: izabrani radovi», književni krug, split 1992 (the abbyy-scanned pdf david supplied, 475 pp.). index entry «franceschi de, c.», p. 24 ff.; the criticisms at pp. 33 and 45–47 of the printed pagination.
the other book — the one he dictated for a son who died

«l'istria: note storiche» is the book carlo published and the book this page has been reading. it is not the book that would answer this archive's questions. that one is «memorie autobiografiche», and it was never printed in his lifetime, because — as a trieste reviewer put it in 1926 — «impossibile sarebbe stato il pensarne la pubblicazione sotto l'austria». it would have been impossible to think of publishing it under austria.
what it is, and when he made it

«le memorie sono scritte in forma di lettere, ché dall'aprile al dicembre 1883, l'illustre storiografo istriano, già settuagenario, dettava per compiacere al desiderio del figlio giampietro, morto immaturamente un anno dopo.» the memoirs are written as letters, dictated between april and december 1883 by the historian, already in his seventies, to satisfy the wish of his son giampietro — who died prematurely a year later.
and the archive has the son's grave

on the right-hand tablet of the family tomb at gologorica, photographed this year: «pietro fu carlo / magistrato / rovigno 1854 — moncalvo 1884». born at rovigno in 1854, dead at moncalvo in 1884. a newspaper in trieste in 1926 and a stone in an istrian village churchyard, and they say the same thing: the son asked, the father spent nine months dictating his life, and the son was dead within the year. the book exists because of him.
camillo published it, and annotated it heavily

it appeared for the first time in the 1926 volume of the «archeografo triestino», the review of the società di minerva, edited by carlo's other son camillo — who added not only a preface «dove con serenità di storico delinea il ritratto e l'opera del padre», drawing his father's portrait and work with a historian's composure, but over a hundred notes. it was also sold separately by booksellers, which is why copies circulate as a book of about three hundred pages.
what the reviewer says is in it

an intimate view of istrian political life from the first decades of the nineteenth century almost to its close. his father and his uncle still held to the old devotion to the empire; he was the risorgimento generation. at graz he read nothing but italian authors and talked so boldly that his landlady predicted the gallows for him. as a judicial official he was under the eye of the captain of pisino, baron grimschitz. in 1848 the istrian electors sent him to the vienna parliament with madonizza, vidulich and fachinetti; he saw the october revolution, the siege and the bombardment, and «di quei tragici giorni ci dà nelle memorie una descrizione drammaticissima, che basterebbe essa sola alla fama del libro» — of those tragic days he gives a description dramatic enough on its own to make the book's reputation.

back at his obscure post in rovigno he lasted until 1854, when he was thrown out with a pension so poor he could be called destitute. he took refuge at fiume, living in a generous lawyer's office until 1860, keeping up the historical and archaeological work that had made him kandler's collaborator. when the constitution was restored, the diet of parenzo — «la famosa dieta del nessuno», the famous diet of nobody, which refused to send deputies to vienna — called the exile to be its secretary. offered a rise on his meagre salary, he refused it out of regard for the province's poor finances, and went on living «pur carico di famiglia, nella voluta povertà» — burdened with a family, in chosen poverty. the government opposed every candidature he stood for.
and a date it settles, and one it gets wrong

«carlo de franceschi nacque il 1809 in moncalvo, un umile villaggio della contea di pisino.» born 1809 — which is what his own tomb says, mdcccix, and what this archive published against a newspaper obituary of 1893 that gave 1810. but the same review has him dying «l'8 gennaio 1898», and that is wrong: he died on 8 january 1893, as the tomb, the obituaries and the whole of this archive agree. the day and month are right and a digit has slipped. printed sources make this mistake too, which is the point of checking them.

so: this archive does not have the «memorie autobiografiche», and should. it is carlo in the first person, at seventy-four, on his own family, his own village and his own century, with a hundred notes by the son who spent his life on the family's history. everything on this site about carlo has been assembled from the outside — from kobler's correspondence, from the istrian press, from a monograph, from his tomb. the book in which he speaks for himself has been in print since 1926.

«il piccolo» of trieste, 24 april 1926, page 3, reviewing the 1926 volume of the «archeografo triestino»; noticed also in «il piccolo» of 16 april 1926. both read from the internet archive's run of the paper, september 2026. the book: carlo de franceschi, «memorie autobiografiche», with preface, notes and appendices by camillo de franceschi, archeografo triestino / lloyd triestino, trieste 1926, about 300 pp. the bibliography of carlo's works is from istrianet.org.
and then it was found, free, in an afternoon

the section above was written saying this archive did not have the «memorie autobiografiche» and should. it now has them. the whole book is open access at openstarts, the institutional repository of the university of trieste, which has digitised the «archeografo triestino» entire: 309 pages, handle 10077/24521, no login, no charge. a first read gives the following, and there is a great deal more in it.
his grandfather and his great-uncle, and what the uncle did in 1809

camillo, on where his father's politics did not come from: «non le assorbì certo in famiglia, dove tanto il padre giuseppe che lo zio giacomo ostentavano sentimenti di tenace attaccamento all'austria e a francesco i.» he certainly did not absorb them at home, where both his father giuseppe and his uncle giacomo made a show of stubborn attachment to austria and to francis i. and then: «giacomo de franceschi aveva preso parte attiva alla preparazione dell'insurrezione istriana del 1809 contro i francesi, soffocata nel sangue», and with two other representatives of the county — the young triestine antonio dietrich, later a lieutenant field marshal, and ivancich of pisino — had gone to rovigno. giacomo de franceschi helped prepare the istrian rising of 1809 against the french, and it was drowned in blood.
carlo was born a french citizen

«era nato cittadino francese, tre giorni dopo la cessione della contea di pisino alla francia, ed egli soleva dire scherzosamente d'avere nutrito dalla culla le idee liberali e democratiche della grande rivoluzione.» he was born a french citizen, three days after the county of pazin was ceded to france, and used to say jokingly that he had been fed the liberal and democratic ideas of the great revolution from the cradle. so the man who spent his life asserting the italianness of istria was, for the first weeks of it, a subject of napoleon — and knew it, and made a joke of it.
which settles a date, by arithmetic

camillo opens by saying his father was born «il 16 ottobre 1809». the gologorica baptism register, which this archive read from the microfilm, gives 17 october 1809, house 17. camillo's own «three days after the cession» is the tie-breaker: the treaty of schönbrunn was signed on 14 october 1809, and three days after that is the 17th, not the 16th. the register stands. a son writing in 1926 was a day out, and his own sentence catches it.
the son the book was written for

«furono da lui scritte per compiacere al desiderio e alle insistenti richieste del figlio gian pietro, aggiunto giudiziale in pola, giovane di promettente ingegno e di felici attitudini letterarie, morto immaturamente a trenta anni nel 1884.» written to satisfy the wish and the insistent asking of his son gian pietro, assistant judge at pola, a young man of promising talent and happy literary gifts, dead prematurely at thirty in 1884. the tomb at gologorica says pietro fu carlo, magistrato, rovigno 1854 — moncalvo 1884. thirty exactly. and camillo adds that gian pietro, before he died, left the manuscript to his two brothers.
what carlo thought he was writing

«gettate giù in fretta e alla buona, spesso senza ordine e successione cronologica dei fatti, non essendo in origine destinate alla pubblicità, ma considerate come semplici scritti confidenziali di padre a figlio.» thrown down in haste and plainly, often out of order, never meant for publication — simple confidential writings from a father to a son. which is why they are worth more than the book he did publish.
the village, as his son saw it

«nato nell'umile sperduto villaggio di moncalvo, dell'antica contea di pisino, in faccia al superbo panorama del monte maggiore e della valle dell'arsa … mentre a destra si profilano sull'orizzonte i monti di pedena, gallignana, lindaro, con le vette segnate dagli agili campanili veneti di pietra bianca.» born in the humble lost village of moncalvo in the old county of pazin, facing the monte maggiore and the arsa valley, with the hills of pedena, gallignana and lindar on the horizon to the right, their summits marked by slender venetian bell-towers of white stone. every place-name in that sentence is a place this archive has been reading registers from.
and the first history lesson of his life

coming home from his first year at the gymnasium at fiume, riding with his father, they stopped at passo on the monte maggiore road with «il parroco ierbulla di gallignana, uomo colto e patriotta» — the parish priest of gallignana, a cultivated and patriotic man — who asked the boy whether he had studied any history. he managed pola, nesactium, and a battle near lovran. the priest told him that among the ancient istrian cities there was also faveria, whose remains he said were at čepić by lake arsa. «queste le mie prime notizie di storia istriana» — these were my first pieces of istrian history. the historian of istria got his start from the parish priest of the town whose baptism book this archive has just finished reading.
and the cost, in his son's words

«con tutti i suoi talenti ed i suoi meriti, condusse una vita stentata e morì povero.» a family of seven mouths and two sons kept at their studies away from home; eleven years in the service of the istrian provincial committee on twelve hundred florins without a single rise, because he had refused to sign the officials' petition for one, so as not to unbalance the provincial budget. and baron federico grimschitz, captain of istria, kept a black book of istrians politically dangerous — «in cui apparivano annotate oltre quattrocento persone», with more than four hundred people entered in it.

this is one afternoon's reading of a book of three hundred and nine pages, and the search terms that failed are as telling as the ones that worked: «carnia» does not appear in it at all, «gologorica» not once — the village is always moncalvo — and neither does the year 1711 nor the name leonardo in any family sense. so the memorie do not, on a first pass, answer the question this archive most wants answered. carlo wrote about his century, not about his descent. but there are a hundred notes by camillo, appendices, and the whole of the narrative still to read properly, and camillo was the family's own historian.

two more came off the same shelf at trieste in the same minutes, both open access, neither previously held here. francesco salata, «un precursore: carlo de franceschi», the address given at pisino on 23 june 1929 with notes and documents, 52 pages, handle 10077/23581. and «a carlo de franceschi, dedicandogli pisino pubblico busto bronzeo» of 1928, 110 pages, handle 10077/23559 — which carries a preface, a bibliography of his published writings, and «lettere di carlo de franceschi a pietro kandler e ad altri». letters to kandler and to others: a body of his correspondence this archive knew existed in the zagreb boxes and did not know was in print.

carlo de franceschi, «memorie autobiografiche», with preface, notes and appendices by camillo de franceschi, «archeografo triestino», serie iii vol. xii (xl), 1925–26, 309 pp. open access at openstarts, università degli studi di trieste, hdl.handle.net/10077/24521. downloaded and read 7 september 2026.

the old site is on the public record now

david is switching defranceski.com off. before that happened, all twelve of its pages were submitted to the wayback machine and captured — on 14 september 2026. this is the standing reference: the permanent address of every page, and the live one while it lasts.

one thing the capture cannot hold, and the reason the kml matters

the places · the map archived at 150 kb, and the surname does not appear in it once. that is correct and expected: the page is a frame around google my map mid=1nsf2idd4q8mn0vqgpbwwpgojp6ba1sk, and a wayback capture keeps the frame, not the map inside it. the reference survives; the pins do not.

this is why both my maps were exported as kml on 8 september 2026 and are held with the archive's own material. a my map dies with the account and no crawler saves one — it is the single part of the old site that archiving could never have rescued.
what it took, which is worth writing down

save page now no longer accepts anonymous requests. a post without a session returns 401 «you need to be logged in to use save page now» — a change from the days when that endpoint was open to anyone. david signed in; no credential passed through this project.

it also rate-limits a signed-in account: submitting twelve pages nine seconds apart drew 429 twice, and both were taken on a later pass. the other google site on the same domain, drawinglight, keeps its single capture of 28 november 2021. it is not family history, and is noted only so that nobody later wonders whether it was missed.

home — the purpose, and the six hotspots seget, gologorica, ližnjan, omiš, mione, corsica, and onward to koper, crete, johannesburg, germany, the united states and australia. every one of those is a page or a section here. ližnjan is now third of eighteen towns in the record sweep and has its own man in ante defrančeski; corsica is on the roadmap; crete is the seget tradition, argued against on the carnia page.

the people carlo, camillo, andrea and titian, girolamo, alessandro op, francesco the painter, francesco the printer, domenico, mariano, carlo francesco the composer, the two napoleonic defrance / franceschi-delonne. all on the namesakes page, most now with fuller lives and every one labelled as kin or not kin. two remain owed: andrea and titian, and francesco the painter — both still open, both listed on the roadmap.

the story · the name the spellings: franceschi, de franceschi, franceschini, defrančeski, defranceschi, dei francesci, de franceschi. the name page carries all of these and more, with counts. «defrančeski» is now evidenced three times in print and in five zagreb graves; «franceschini» and «dei francesci» are noted as variants this archive has not found in its own records.

the story · the coat of arms houseofnames, heraldrysinstitute, coadb, plemstvo.hr, and the blasonario giuliano pdfs. the arms page rests on the blasonario giuliano entry and on carlo's own blazon in his letter to kobler — and now on photographs of the carving itself. the commercial crest sites are recorded below as consulted, and not relied on.
about · publications the works of carlo and camillo, with links. sources page and the person pages, with the acquisition list in the search register.
about · resources a link list for researchers. carried over in full, below.
about a google sites template that was never filled in — «tell your viewers about how the club got started». nothing to migrate.
and four things we did not have
checked again, line by line, on the three pages you named

the reckoning above was made from the whole site at once. on 8 september 2026 the three pages you asked about — the name, the coat of arms and the people — were re-read out of the stored html, claim by claim, against what this archive now publishes. three things were genuinely missing. they have been written. two things are deliberately not carried, and here is why.

the old page's variant list ended with two forms this archive had never addressed. «dei francesci» is now on the name page with the verdict it deserves: not found once in eighteen towns, and almost certainly dei franceschi with the -h lost in transcription. «franceschini» is now there too, with the correction that it is not a variant of this surname at all — it is franceschi plus the diminutive -ino, formed independently wherever francesco was a common name. four people in this archive carry it, every one of them by marriage or as a mother's name.
the name — already here, and tested

everything else the old page carried from plemstvo.hr is here: niccolò and the buda charter of 8 march 1359, the 1838 submission to the austrian nobility commission, heyer von rosenfeld 1873, zuane and perinuša, giovanni de franceschi of «la dalmazia». one claim was tested and failed: «franceschi dalle rose», ravenna to venice in 1040 and the giudecca, is the origin story of the donà dalle rose — a different venetian house entirely. that is on the searched page so it is never repeated.

toma de franceschi is now on the namesakes page. notary of zadar: sworn to the city council by hereditary right in 1714, appointed public notary in 1722, forty years in the office, and — the detail worth having — running his practice in croatian as well as italian, in a city whose notarial record is otherwise latin and venetian. his son ivan krševan followed him. he matters because a notary of forty years leaves an archive, and the zadar notarial fond is where the whole croatian noble claim can actually be tested.
the people — already here, and then some

the old page had eleven figures. this archive has twenty-eight, every one labelled kin or not kin, and the two the earlier reckoning listed as still owed — andrea dei franceschi and titian, and francesco the painter — have both since been written. piero della francesca, girolamo, alessandro op, domenico, mariano, carlo francesco, and both napoleonic defrance / franceschi-delonne are all present with fuller lives than the old page gave them.
the coat of arms — well ahead of it

the old page reproduced four blasonario giuliano blazons and linked houseofnames, heraldrysinstitute and coadb. the arms page here carries the same four — the stork of gianantonio 1724, the lion, carlo's cross-arrows-and-pomegranate, and giacomo of pisino 1788 — drawn, translated, and set against three independent witnesses the old site did not have: carlo's own letter of about 1873, matejčić's 1979 architectural survey recording the shield on the moncalvo façade, and the 2012 american reunion album describing the same weathered stone. it also says plainly what the old page did not: there is no coat of arms for a surname, and the crest vendors are selling a picture keyed to a text string.
not carried, on purpose — the works list

the old people page ran a long catalogue of piero della francesca's paintings, museum by museum: arezzo, berlin, the gardner, the uffizi, lisbon, the national gallery, thyssen-bornemisza, the brera, poldi pezzoli, monterchi, the frick, the louvre, perugia, the tempio malatestiano, sansepolcro, urbino, the accademia, washington. it is a good list and it is not family history — no connection between the tuscan franceschi and this family has ever been shown, and a hundred-line museum catalogue for a man we cannot claim would be the largest single block of text on the site. he keeps his entry on namesakes, with the diptych, and the catalogue stays in the stored html.
not carried, on purpose — the living

the old page listed the members of the croatian noble corps by name, with birth years, professions and current cities. they are living people. this archive omits the living rather than hiding them, so they are not here and will not be. the stored html keeps the record for the family's own use.
and four things on the old site that this archive did not have
the comparison was supposed to be a formality. it was not.
«franceschi dalle rose» — chased, and it is almost certainly a confusion

the pin read «franceschi dalle rose move 1040 to venice», with ravenna and the giudecca beside it. searched: the form does not exist in the literature. what does exist, and matches the pin exactly, is the donà dalle rose — a venetian noble house whose own origin story runs from romagna and altinum, which is to say ravenna, whose «dalle rose» is the main surviving branch, and which gave venice two doges. «dalle rose» is their byname, not this family's. the likeliest reading is that a nobiliary source was misfiled at some point and the two ran together. it is recorded here so that it does not get repeated: this archive can find no franceschi dalle rose anywhere.
a german branch route this archive had no idea about

the «german defranceski's» layer runs ližnjan → monheim, with «grga dies in zagreb», and separately «petar moves to metzingen». metzingen is four kilometres from pfullingen, which is where the family's own wartime papers are from. ližnjan is the third-largest cluster in the record sweep. neither grga nor the monheim line appears anywhere in this archive.
the veneto emigration hotspots, and são paulo

a layer of forty-four pins — castelnuovo, pederobba, cornedo vicentino, castelgomberto, scorzè, moniego — all in the veneto, all marked as places of heavy emigration, ending at «state of são paulo». this archive's diaspora page has the brazilian cluster as the largest of all and has never had a departure region for it. here is a candidate one.
the dalmatian narrative, laid out as a route

ravenna → venice 1040 → giudecca → niccolò to zadar in the 1300s → tomasso to omiš → francesca de franceschi from venice to omiš in the 1500s → zuane to imotski → antonio to proložac → antonia to trsat → pisak and vruja. most of it this archive now holds independently and in more detail. two names in it are new: tomasso, and francesca de franceschi of the 1500s.

the live tree, read against this archive
what david's own tree holds that this archive has never read, and what this archive holds that the tree has not.

this archive and david's myheritage tree have been growing beside each other for a year without either reading the other. the roster's family file was the export of july 2018 — 8,286 people, 254 of them of this surname. the tree exported on 16 september 2026 holds 15,643 people in 4,777 families, 1,413 of them of the name.

reading one against the other is not a merge. it is four separate questions, and they have four different answers: who is in both and agrees, who is in both and does not, who only the tree knows about, and who only this archive has found. the fourth is the one people forget — a year of register reading here has turned up 780 people the tree still does not have.

matching folds the nine spellings of this surname together and compares given names and years, so de franceschi, defranceschi and defranceski are one family and not three. on 16 september 2026 the tree flagged 117 of the 1,413 as living, under the rule then in force. under the standard of 16 october 2026 a person is living only at 80 or younger with no death recorded and no public source, and a living person appears below by name and town, never by a date.
where the two disagree

a disagreement is the same person written down twice with one field wrong. the first pass at this called 2,414 of them disagreements, which was a cross-join wearing a finding's clothes: it paired every francesco in the tree with every francesco in the roster and reported the difference. the test that survives needs an anchor — the two must agree on one year exactly and differ on the other. two people of one name and no shared year are two people, which is the thing this archive keeps having to say out loud.

and what kind of disagreement each one is
set the twelve side by side and they are not twelve of the same thing. three kinds, and only one of them needs a register.

seven are a year's worth of arithmetic. josephus 1886 against 1887, cattarina 1825 against 1826, jacobus 1762 against 1761, valentinus 1776 against 1775, davide 1876 against 1875 — the death year agreed in every case, the birth year out by one. that is what a record which gives an age rather than a date does: a man who dies in march aged sixty-four was born in one year if his birthday had passed and the year before if it had not. a headstone and a burial register will disagree for ever about which. albino is out by two and maria by three, which is the same fault with a rounder age.

two are out by more than arithmetic can explain. mario de franceski, 1919 against 1924 — five years, on a man who died in 2012, which means somebody has a document. girolamo of omiš, 1632 against 1622 — ten years, and this archive's side rests on the published omiš chart while the tree's rests on a myheritage profile.

three are a disputed death, which is the serious kind. clementina maria of gologorica, dead in 1840 here and 1870 in the tree — thirty years. josephus lambertus, the same parish, 1857 against 1878 — twenty-one. lina defranceschi of torrington, 1923 against 1925. a death year is the one thing a parish register states outright, and this archive's gologorica dates were read off the register itself. the gologorica books settle two of the three in an afternoon.
and 2 rows that are not disagreements at all

these came back in mirrored pairs — the tree's 1786 against the archive's 1789, and then the tree's 1789 against the archive's 1786. that shape means both sides are holding the same person twice, under two years, and each copy is being matched to the other side's other copy. it is a duplicate to merge, not a date to decide, and this page will not pretend otherwise.

what a month's full subscription reaches that two expiring trials could not, and the two threads it opened.

david took a one-month full subscription on 16 september 2026. every earlier pass ran against a clock — the trial of 9 september and the one that lapsed on 14 september, sixteen rows between them on the search register, both ending with a note about reading transcripts before the trial died.
this is the first sweep with no clock on it. four spellings, 644 distinct records, 44 record sets — six more sets than the trials could see, because a subscription opens collections a trial does not.

the index rows are not the point. an index row gives a name and a year. a transcript gives parents, a parish, a ship, a street. the transcripts read below are where the two findings on this page came from.

what is published, and what is not
220counted, not published31 electoral · 22 ssdi · 20 obituaries · 3 divorce · 144 no anchor before 1930

published only where the person was born before 1930 or a death is on record. the uk electoral registers, the social security death index, the obituary notices and the divorce indexes are excluded entirely — they are where the living are, and this archive publishes a living person's name and town and nothing else. 424 of the 644 pass; 220 are counted here and published nowhere.
americas (port unstated)280

«americas» is findmypast's own label for a passenger record whose port it does not state. it is 280 of the 644, and it is why the map layer these records are going to feed has to draw a crossing rather than a home.
a de franceschi married a cosulich in cardiff in 1876

wales roman catholic marriages. emerico de franceschi, son of francisci de franceschi, married mariettam cosulich, daughter of josephi francisci cosulich, at st peter's, roath, cardiff, on 26 july 1876 — the names in the latin genitive the priest wrote them in.

cosulich is not a name that turns up by accident. it is one of the great shipowning families of the austrian littoral — lussinpiccolo and trieste, and in time the cosulich line. and cardiff in 1876 is the coal port of the world, where the adriatic sailing fleet went to load. two austrian-adriatic maritime families marrying in a catholic church in a welsh coal port is the sea, not migration.
nothing yet joins emerico to this archive's own people. but it is the first record of the name in wales, and it sits exactly where the lloyd's list work already pointed.

and it is orderable. marietta cosulich appears exactly once in the whole of findmypast — this marriage — and the second entry for it is the civil register, not the parish one: england & wales marriages, cardiff district, q3 1876, volume 11a, page 428, where the gro clerk read his name as «emmerico defrancrschi». the certificate behind that reference gives both ages, both residences, both occupations and the witnesses. if emerico is a master or a mate, his occupation joins this marriage to the lloyd's list work outright. written up as an errand.
next order the gro certificate — cardiff q3 1876, 11a 428. then look for emerico in the lloyd's registers and in lussino's parish books.
the puerto rican cluster, read to the bottom

isabela 11, san lorenzo 9, ponce 7, and after them guayama, lajas, luquillo, peñuelas, san sebastián, yauco, ceiba and pueblo este — fifty-two records across eleven puerto rican towns, every one of them the 1920 united states census.

and every one of them is a woman. filomena franceschi dávila de padilla. carmen callejo y ferrer de franceschi. catalina juliani de franceschi. ramona mato de franceschi. read them in spanish and the reason is plain: «de» here is the marital particle, not the italian nobiliary one. a woman born callejo y ferrer who marries a franceschi is indexed de franceschi; a woman born franceschi who marries a padilla keeps franceschi as her first surname. a search for «de franceschi» catches every married woman of the family and not one of its men, who are filed under plain franceschi.

so the cluster is real and this archive has been looking at it through a keyhole. it is a franceschi family, not a de franceschi one, and the surname this site is built on is not the surname in it. nineteenth-century corsican emigration to puerto rico is well documented, and corsica is already here as a parallel rather than a connection — which is still the right word for this.

and then the census itself answered it. two of the san lorenzo women were read in full: cármen colón de franceschi, twenty-three, and aurora cruz de franceschi, twenty-five. both are born in puerto rico; both have a father and a mother born in puerto rico; both are entered as esposa, the wife; and the enumerator records both as black.

so the thread closes. these are afro-puerto rican women married to men called franceschi, in a family that was already two generations on the island in 1920. the surname very probably did reach puerto rico with the corsican settlement of the nineteenth century — that much is well documented and it is why corsica is on this site at all — but by 1920 it is a puerto rican surname, and the people carrying it here are not immigrants and are not related to this family.
this page said «a puerto rican cluster of the name» when it was first published on 16 september. it was the name minus its particle, and then it was not the name at all.
next nothing. the cluster is understood and it is not ours.
the italian parish sets are naples and vicenza — a clean negative

three record sets the trials never opened — italy births & baptisms 1806-1900, italy marriages 1809-1900, italy deaths & burials 1809-1900 — hold ten records of the name, and every transcript read puts them somewhere this family is not.

two brothers baptised at san marco di palazzo, napoli in 1842 and 1844, and a sister born at napoli in 1855, all three children of carmine de franceschi and angiola conti. a valentino mario born at vicenza in 1900 to florindo and angela torresan. a lucia caterina born the same year in the frazione settecà, who married at torri di quartesolo and died at vicenza in 1967. a domenico, born 1829 and buried at vicenza in 1900, son of carlo and teresa facco.
napoli and vicenza. not istria, not carnia, not the kvarner. written down so that nobody opens these three sets again expecting the family in them.
next nothing. the set is closed unless a vicentine or neapolitan line is ever proposed.
two american households, read end to end — memphis and chicago
the sweep counted records. reading the transcripts turns two piles of them into families.

memphis, tennessee — nine children and a german wife. antonio de franceski, born 1875 in italy, arrived 1902, in the 19th ward of memphis by 1910 with bertha, born in germany. both his parents born in italy. the same household is there in 1930 as anthony de franceschi, and again in 1940: pietro, aurora, alba, albert, flora, estelle, serena, juliet, romeo and a second anthony, born between 1904 and 1917. twenty-one records across three censuses.

the 1910 sheet spells them «de franceski» — the fused form this family uses and almost nobody else does. and born in italy in 1875, left in 1902 is the carnian emigration window exactly. istria in 1875 was austria and an american enumerator would have written austria.

chicago — a household with a document at every stage. giovanni / john de franceschi, born 1895 in italy, head of a household at chicago in the 1930 census with freedia (1904) and the children thersa (1925) and ateo (1926). naturalised at chicago in 1937 — nara m1285, roll 41. buried 12 april 1951 at st joseph's cemetery, river grove, cook county. frieda outlived him to 1988; attilio f defranceschi, 1925–2010, is almost certainly the son the census wrote as ateo.

neither census says more than «italy». the petition behind the chicago naturalisation does — a naturalisation petition names the comune — and it is orderable from nara with the roll number above. written up as an errand.
next order nara m1285 roll 41 for giovanni's chicago petition; find antonio of memphis's own petition, which will name his town.
smyrna, 1906–10 — and it stays open

eveline l a m de franceschi married at smyrna between 1906 and 1910, in the gro consular registers — archive reference mcon, volume 788, line 70. she appears once in the whole of findmypast and this is it.

the index does not say whom she married. findmypast's own marriage finder offers three names from the same page: helen whittall, frederick p wilkinson, reginald e turrell — and whittall is the levantine british merchant house of smyrna, the same kind of world as cardiff and the cosulich: an adriatic-and-levant trading network with a british consulate in the middle of it.
it is not resolved and this page will not pretend it is. a consular marriage certificate would name her father, which is the only thing that could join her to anybody here.
next order the gro consular certificate, or read the smyrna consular register at the national archives.
zdravko defranceski, horsham — the victorian probate file and the billion graves headstone, and ruža «rosa» beside him, 1996. both already known; both now have a second source.
two burials at river grove, cook county, illinois in the chicago roman catholic cemetery records — frieda (1905–1988) and john (1895–1951).
seven new york parish records at named manhattan churches: our lady of mount carmel, ascension, transfiguration, our lady of pompei, st joseph on sixth avenue, st anthony of padua.

a consular marriage at smyrna, 1906–10 — eveline l a m de franceschi, in the british overseas registers. the candidate spouses findmypast offers include a whittall, which is the levantine merchant family of smyrna. unresolved, and probably not ours.
manuela campos de franceschi, panama, 1861–1904, and antonio juan de franceschi rovo, argentina, 1899 — both of whom the live tree also cites, from the same two collections.

how it was read, and what is left

the session lives in the in-app browser, and on findmypast.com.au rather than the .co.uk domain the earlier passes used. the results page is a client-rendered application: its url wants «_page», not «page», and its own pagination anchors have to be clicked, because a link built by hand triggers a full reload and loses everything gathered so far. each page yields twenty rows and a transcript id; the id is what the transcript reader takes.

what this sweep did not do. the transcripts were read for ten records, not for six hundred — every one of them gives parents, a place and often a note in italian, and they are the difference between an index and a source. the images behind them are a further step again. and the irish, scottish and english parish collections have still never been opened under this name.
it is on the work list, twice: the month, and the map layer these 644 records are going to feed.
